Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy showed 89.8% lower solid-electrolyte interphase resistance, 18.1% lower charge-transfer resistance, and 77.7% lower total resistance. These results show that topology and electrode microstructure can jointly improve scalable low-frequency piezoelectrochemical energy harvesting.

title: Ga(III) ion release from gallium-based liquid metals: The trade-off between efficacy and safety
abstract: Due to unique pharmacological activities and distinctive physicochemical properties, gallium-based liquid metals (LMs) have attracted tremendous attention in therapeutics. As biodegradable metallic materials, gallium-based LMs can predominantly release Ga(III) ions under physiological conditions, which represents a double-edged sword for clinical translation. On the one hand, the Ga(III) ions act as redox-inert Fe(III) competitive inhibitors and may provide therapeutic effects for broad-spectrum therapeutic applications. On the other hand, upon nonspecific biodistribution or uncontrolled Ga(III) release, substitution of Fe(III) by Ga(III) may disturb iron metabolism in normal cells and subsequently induce toxicological outcomes. Therefore, understanding and managing the trade-off between efficacy and safety is a key prerequisite for the clinical translation of gallium-based LMs. This review aims to systematically summarize the therapeutic activities and toxicological characteristics of gallium-based LMs. Meaningfully, the unresolved challenges and future perspectives regarding the balance between efficacy and safety are outlined to inspire future academic explorations and clinical translation.

title: Two-photon light-sheet microscopy with isotropic near-diffraction-limited resolution in three dimensions
abstract: Achieving isotropic high-resolution three-dimensional imaging across a large field of view (FOV) remains a key challenge in two-photon light-sheet microscopy (TPLSM). To address this limitation, we developed a TPLSM system that stitches multiple short Bessel beams into a large, ultrathin illumination light sheet and employs a dedicated control protocol to suppress stray light. The system delivers isotropic near-diffraction-limited resolution across a 332.8 μm FOV, enabling uniform visualization of fine structural details in biological samples and avoiding morphological misinterpretation. In vivo imaging of zebrafish embryos validates the system's performance, confirming its utility for high-fidelity biological observation. Furthermore, the proposed approach is broadly applicable to other microscope modalities using Bessel-beam illumination, extending its utility well beyond TPLSM.

title: Chased and displaced: Impact of anthropogenic disturbance on habitat use and movement patterns of Asian elephants in South West Bengal, India
abstract: Managing large mammals sustaining on crops in human-dominated landscapes is challenging, and the most common mitigation strategy is "driving". In South Bengal, elephants are driven away by locals or organized " hula " teams. Over 223 monitored days in 2017–18 (56 no drive, 97 local, and 70 hula drives), we collected data on elephant movement, habitat use, costs, and community responses. Mean monthly movement type differed significantly, with local drive being highest (0.43 km ± 0.10 SD), followed by hula (0.31 km ± 0.11 SD) and no drive (0.26 km ± 0.12 SD). Mean daily path length differed too, hula drives being highest (9.43 km ± 4.24), while local drives were lowest (5.20 km ± 2.34). Expenditure on hula drives correlated positively with hula size (5.86 ± 2.00 SD). Drives were mainly triggered by grievances (54%) and crop damage (24%). Local communities interfered in 55.71% of drives. Hula drives are reactive, socially mediated, energy-intensive interventions offering only short-term relief, not a long-term mitigative measure.

title: Excessive activation of the RAS/MAPK pathway triggers adult-onset motor axonal degeneration
abstract: Abstract Axonal and synaptic degeneration are key hallmarks of neurodegenerative diseases, but the underlying molecular mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we performed an unbiased forward genetic mosaic screen to identify genes required for maintenance of adult motor axons and neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) in the Drosophila leg. We identified 49 mutations in 30 genes, including mutations in 8 genes resulting in adult-onset progressive degeneration. We found that loss of pebbled ( peb ) function results in adult-onset motor axonal and NMJ degeneration, and age-dependent motor deficits. Peb is the Drosophila RREB1 ortholog, a C 2 H 2 zinc-finger transcription factor that negatively regulates transcription of RAS/MAPK pathway target genes. Loss of peb function resulted in excessive RAS/MAPK pathway activation, and loss of function of other negative regulators of the RAS/MAPK pathway also induced adult-onset progressive NMJ degeneration and motor deficits. Importantly, treatment of adult flies with the MEK1/2 inhibitor mirdametinib induced a dosage-dependent rescue of peb mutant motor neurodegenerative phenotypes. Thus, RAS/MAPK pathway overactivation results in adult-onset progressive neurodegeneration, which can be prevented by RAS/MAPK pathway inhibition.

title: Macrophages promote collagen deposition through circadian regulation of fibroblasts
abstract: Fibroblast collagen deposition is regulated by macrophages and the circadian rhythm; understanding how these processes interact provides insights to collagenous tissue homeostasis. Here, we reveal that macrophage-fibroblast interaction enhances collagen deposition and requires a functional circadian rhythm. Macrophage polarization status determines how fibroblast responses were elicited, where naive and pro-inflammatory macrophages require direct cell-cell contact, and anti-inflammatory macrophages secrete soluble factors. One key secreted factor identified by mass spectrometry proteomics analysis is PDGFA. Crucially, macrophages lacking PDGFA, or treatment with PDGFRa inhibitor, showed diminished ability to modulate fibroblast circadian rhythms and collagen production. Impaired circadian rhythms in either cell type also led to a reduced collagen fibrillogenesis response. These results confirmed that the collagen deposition pathway is under circadian clock control in lung fibroblasts, and demonstrated that macrophages can re-synchronize fibroblast circadian rhythms to promote collagen deposition and extracellular remodeling, which are implicated in processes such as wound healing responses.

title: Non-canonical cleavage of GPR125/ADGRA3 releases extracellular receptor fragments detectable in cerebrospinal fluid
abstract: Adhesion G protein-coupled receptors (aGPCRs) are crucial for barrier tissues and typically autoproteolytically cleaved into N- and C-terminal fragments (NTF and CTF) that remain non-covalently associated until separation is triggered. Here, we show that human GPR125 (ADGRA3), expressed in choroid plexus epithelium, is not cleaved at the GPCR autoproteolysis site (GPS), consistent with its divergent SLS motif. Instead, it undergoes non-canonical proteolytic processing that generates and releases atypical, non-canonical N-terminal fragments (ncNTFs), a process further enhanced by insulin. Using mutational analyses, metalloprotease inhibition, and ADAM10/17-deficient cells, we find that multiple proteases likely participate in cleavage. Mass spectrometry reveals one specific cleavage site, and real-time imaging uncovers GPR125's intracellular trafficking and shedding dynamics. Changing the GPS destabilizes the ncNTF-ncCTF association and increases ncNTF release, thereby promoting cell viability. Finally, detection of multiple GPR125-derived peptides in human cerebrospinal fluid suggests ncNTF shedding in vivo and possible biological relevance.

title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls
abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens. Untargeted shotgun metagenomic sequencing offers a broader, unbiased view of the wastewater virome, although its performance is challenged by low human viral abundance, complex background signals, and genome assembly challenges. We also discuss key challenges complicating bioinformatic analysis, including limited human viral sequences, co-circulating viral lineages, viral dark matter, reference database limitations, large data volumes, and methodological biases, as well as emerging computational approaches aimed at improving wastewater sequencing analysis and interpretation.

title: Data-driven burst shape analysis for functional phenotyping of neuronal cultures
abstract: are instrumental for studying network dynamics under normal and pathological conditions. Mature networks typically exhibit network bursting activity, traditionally quantified by simplified features such as inter-burst intervals and burst durations. These features have advanced our understanding of development, disease phenotypes, and drug effects. However, they overlook the temporal structure within bursts, which is highly sensitive to network changes and can thus reveal additional physiological or pathological effects. Here, we developed a comprehensive framework to quantify burst shapes, the time-course of network firing during bursts. On four datasets, including rodent- and human pluripotent stem cell-derived cultures, we show that burst shapes contain rich information about the underlying network dynamics. We quantify this information by classifying conditions (genetic disorders, pharmacological agents) using traditional and burst-shape features, and find that including shape features significantly improves accuracy. We provide an open pipeline for burst shape characterization, introducing burst shape as a complementary functional phenotyping feature that expands the analytical toolkit for disease modeling and drug screening.

title: Assessing machine learning prediction of recycled aggregate concrete strength with a tabular foundation model
abstract: Recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) supports more sustainable construction, but recycled concrete aggregate (RCA)'s heterogeneity complicates compressive-strength prediction. This study evaluates the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) against nine conventional machine-learning models using a standardized literature-derived database of 833 RAC mixtures. Cube strengths were converted to equivalent cylinder strengths, with conversion sensitivity also assessed. Among conventional models, CatBoost achieved the highest accuracy (R 2 = 0.843), whereas TabPFN achieved R 2 = 0.870, mean absolute error (MAE) = 3.924 MPa, and root mean squared error (RMSE) = 5.551 MPa. TabPFN also produced a lower RMSE than CatBoost across all four RCA replacement intervals without extensive task-specific hyperparameter tuning. Feature importance and Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analyses identified effective water-to-cement ratio, aggregate-to-cement ratio, RCA density, and RCA absorption as key predictors, while RCA replacement level alone had limited influence. The moderate improvement over CatBoost indicates that further gains depend on improved RCA characterization.

title: IL-4 and arginine synergy accelerates early bone regeneration via enhanced efferocytosis and ameliorated microenvironment
abstract: Host bone microenvironment is a critical factor for successful bone regeneration during implantation. In this work, we identified a spatiotemporal mismatch at drilling-induced injury sites where initial apoptosis outpaces macrophage recruitment, leading to apoptotic cell accumulation and oxidative stress that impairs osteogenic differentiation. To mitigate this phenomenon, we developed a synergistic strategy co-delivering interleukin 4 (IL-4) and arginine (Arg) to reprogram the microenvironment. Mechanistically, IL-4 recruits and polarizes macrophages toward a pro-reparative M2 phenotype, while Arg fuels the arginase-1 metabolic pathway to sustain continual efferocytosis and secretion of pro-regenerative cytokines. In a mouse bone injury model, transcriptomic and histological analyses confirmed that this strategy accelerates apoptotic clearance and establishes an M2-dominant environment, significantly enhancing early bone regeneration. Altogether, this work proposes a novel therapeutic paradigm targeting macrophage efferocytosis to resolve early microenvironmental imbalances, providing a promising therapeutic approach to promote bone defect healing and offering novel insights into optimizing host microenvironments for osseointegration following implantation.

title: Decoding the role of cancer-associated fibroblasts in cisplatin resistance of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: Cisplatin remains the primary chemotherapy drug for the treatment of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). However, acquired resistance significantly limits its clinical application, contributing to treatment failure and a poor patient prognosis. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in the tumor microenvironment influence HNSCC sensitivity to cisplatin by modulating tumor cell responsiveness to treatment via paracrine signaling. CAFs impede deep penetration into tumors by remodeling the extracellular matrix (ECM). Various subtypes of cisplatin-resistant CAFs have been identified in HNSCC. Potential compounds targeting these subtypes could enhance cisplatin sensitivity. Simulation of the dynamic tumor microenvironment remains limited in research, hindering clinical translation. Bioinformatics has shifted research into cisplatin resistance in HNSCC. Single-cell sequencing and spatiotemporal transcriptomics could analyze the molecular profiles of CAFs that promote drug resistance in greater depth, potentially facilitating the development of highly targeted drugs and effective combination therapy strategies to overcome cisplatin resistance in HNSCCs.

title: PXT3003: Lessons for therapeutic development in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A and related neuropathies
abstract: Most drug development stories end predictably: promising compounds either succeed or fail. Occasionally, however, a therapy repeatedly returns from apparent extinction. PXT3003 for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A (CMT1A) represents one such example. More than a decade after early promise, the program has survived formulation instability, interrupted clinical development, regulatory uncertainty, and controversy surrounding efficacy before re-emerging with renewed evidence of clinical benefit. Yet, as with many therapeutic development programs, interpretation of the available evidence is influenced by the extent to which findings are publicly accessible. In a recent issue of iScience , a phase 3 clinical trial evaluated PXT3003, a combination of baclofen, naltrexone, and D-sorbitol, versus placebo over 15 months in participants aged 16–65 years with mild-to-moderate CMT1A across 25 sites in China. PXT3003 is not simply the story of one drug; it highlights the scientific, methodological, operational, and reporting challenges of developing disease-modifying therapies for slowly progressive inherited neuropathies.

title: Monotropein mitigates atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability through circ_0140736/miR-495/SIRPα-mediated efferocytosis
abstract: Efferocytosis is a biological process in which phagocytic cells engulf and degrade senescent, damaged, or dead cells to prevent secondary necrosis and inflammation. This process is implicated in various diseases, including atherosclerosis (AS). Enhancing efferocytosis efficiency may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for managing AS. Consequently, increasing attention is being paid to pharmacological agents that can promote efferocytosis. Monotropein (MON), the predominant iridoid glycoside in Morinda officinalis , has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties in previous studies. However, its role in regulating atherosclerotic plaque stability remains unclear. In this study, we show that MON enhances plaque stability in AS. The expression of circ_0140736 was found to be elevated in unstable atherosclerotic plaques. MON suppressed circ_0140736 expression and alleviated miR-495 sequestration via a competing endogenous RNA mechanism, thereby increasing miR-495 levels and downregulating signal regulatory protein α (SIRPɑ) expression. In conclusion, MON exerts its anti-atherosclerotic effects by promoting efferocytosis through the circ_0140736/miR-495/SIRPɑ axis, suggesting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for AS.

title: Development of proteome-derived cyclic peptide libraries via ortho-phthalaldehyde-assisted cyclization
abstract: Cyclic peptides possess unique structural features and binding capabilities that make them attractive scaffolds for molecular recognition. However, strategies for generating functionally diverse libraries directly from natural proteomes remain comparatively underdeveloped. Here, we present a proteome-informed approach for constructing cyclic peptide libraries by integrating cysteine-enrichment protocols with ortho-phthalaldehyde (OPA)-mediated macrocyclization. This method enables direct library generation from proteome digests and is compatible with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)-based annotation and downstream functional screening. We systematically identify key parameters governing OPA-mediated cyclization topology and develop a rule-based pipeline for automated library annotation of OPA-cyclized peptides. Applying this strategy, we generate a library of over 15,000 unique cyclic peptides and perform target-specific screening against human IgG. This yielded cyclic peptide binder candidates, including one lead peptide showing cyclization-dependent IgG-binding potential. Our study establishes an OPA-enabled, proteome-informed workflow for cyclic peptide library construction and annotation.

title: Stress induced hyperphagia in C. elegans as a genetic model for binge eating disorders
abstract: Binge eating (BE) is often triggered by stress, dieting, and adverse environmental factors, and represents a common precursor to eating disorders such as anorexia, bulimia, and BE disorder. Stress-induced hyperphagia captures core features of binge-like feeding and shares neurobiological substrates will BE disorder, making it a useful behavioral readout for dissecting underlying mechanisms. We used the genetically tractable worm Caenorhabditis elegans to examine how starvation and stress interact to drive feeding, quantifying pharyngeal pumping as a measure of food intake. Combined starvation and heat stress increased feeding beyond starvation alone, with effects shaped by stress timing, food quality, and sex. Feeding phenotypes were separable from locomotor and feeding-capacity defects. Mutations in evolutionarily conserved homeostatic and hedonic feeding-pathway genes showed distinct hyperphagic responses, implicating that conserved neuronal circuits govern stress-induced feeding across species. This model offers a platform for genetic screening and drug testing to accelerate discovery of therapeutics for binge-like feeding disorders.

title: Pharmacological protection from a sugar-rich diet through inhibition of Ras/MAPK signaling
abstract: Consumption of sugar-rich diets adversely affects health and reduces life expectancy through the excessive production and storage of triacylglycerides (TAGs), leading to metabolic dysfunction. Here, we show that in Drosophila , pharmacological inhibition of Ras/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling using the highly specific MEK inhibitor, trametinib, mitigates several of the detrimental effects of a high-sugar diet by reducing TAG accumulation, restoring TAG composition, and increasing survival. Notably, Ras/MAPK activity is required for the transcriptional response to elevated sugar intake, including expression of the glucagon-like hormone, Akh . We further demonstrate that adipokinetic hormone (AKH) is essential for the protective effects of trametinib under high-sugar conditions. Together, our findings support Ras/MAPK signaling as an important link between dietary sugar and metabolic dysfunction and show that its pharmacological inhibition can uncouple excess sugar intake from adverse metabolic outcomes.

title: Contrasting fate and GHG emissions of algal vs. manure DOM under light and microbes in lakes
abstract: The escalating dissolved organic matter (DOM) inputs from algal (ADOM) and livestock manure (MDOM) sources are altering lake ecosystems, yet their fate under light and microbes in steppe lakes is unclear. Using microcosms, we found that photodegradation suppressed ADOM bioavailability by 4.8% via substrate competition and reactive oxygen species (ROS) inhibition (especially singlet oxygen), while light enhanced MDOM bioavailability by 5.4%. ADOM mineralization released 1.6× more CO 2 than MDOM. Multi-group structural equation modeling (SEM) indicated that efficient ADOM microbial transformation drove higher CO 2 emissions, whereas light-induced ROS shifted microbial communities and transformation pathways. ADOM and MDOM inputs predominantly enhanced CO 2 emissions and water browning, respectively. These processes are interconnected—exogenous MDOM can promote algal blooms and subsequent greenhouse gas release. For eutrophic steppe lakes, integrated management combining exogenous load reduction and endogenous bloom suppression is critical to mitigate ecological risks and greenhouse effects.

title: Boid inclusion body disease in Boa constrictor: Unraveling the myth of immunosuppression
abstract: Boid Inclusion Body Disease (BIBD) is an infectious disease of captive boid snakes of prime relevance since the 1970s. BIBD is caused by reptarenaviruses and characterized by intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies (IB) in most cell types. Affected snakes frequently develop secondary (bacterial) infections which led to the hypothesis that BIBD is associated with immunosuppression. To investigate this, we analysed peripheral blood from 48 Boa constrictor, with confirmed BIBD and reptarenavirus infection, three infected snakes without the disease, and 84 reptarenavirus negative snakes, assessing haematology, biochemistry, stress parameters, and immune function. BIBD-positive snakes showed significantly lower percentages of circulating Iba1+ phagocytic cells, reduced cholesterol, and lower total Ig concentrations, while virus-specific IgY and IgM levels were elevated. The findings indicate impaired function of the monocyte/macrophage phagocytic lineage, providing first mechanistic evidence of increased susceptibility to secondary bacterial infections, and highlights that specific immune components are affected in BIBD.

title: Inhibitory receptor profiles for joint prediction of benefit and toxicity in immune checkpoint blockade
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has transformed cancer therapy, but durable benefit is limited to a subset of patients and can be accompanied by immune-related adverse events. This Review evaluates inhibitory receptor profiles as candidate biomarkers for predicting both antitumor benefit and immune toxicity. We examine how receptor abundance, co-expression, cellular lineage, clonality, spatial context, and treatment-induced dynamics shape interpretation across tissue imaging, cytometry, bulk transcriptomics, single-cell multi-omics, and spatial profiling, with particular attention to organ-specific toxicity and time-dependent analytical bias. Current evidence supports context-dependent associations, especially for multi-receptor T-cell states and early on-treatment changes, but not universal thresholds or stand-alone clinical use. Because benefit and toxicity share pathways yet arise from partly distinct biological determinants, they should remain separate model outputs. We propose a staged path from mechanistic discovery to a locked minimal assay, external validation, and prospective evaluation of clinical utility.

title: Endometriosis and chronic pain syndrome: The role of stress mechanisms
abstract: Patients with endometriosis report increased levels of perceived stress, which correlates with disease severity and pain intensity, creating feedback loops that perpetuate the cycle of endometriosis inflammation, chronic pain syndrome, and pathological stress response. Stress and chronic pain form an integrated biopsychosocial system in which neuroendocrine dysregulation, central sensitization, neuroinflammation, large-scale network reorganization, and maladaptive threat learning mutually reinforce each other. Sex differences, developmental experiences, and resilience factors modulate this interaction. Chronic pain in endometriosis emerges as the result of a progressive integration of peripheral inflammation and central nervous system plasticity. Thus, mechanism-based therapeutic strategies for endometriosis-associated pain should address both peripheral drivers and central amplification processes. Further research is needed to better understand whether chronic stress is a contributing cause for the onset of endometriosis and whether there is an opportunity to modify this risk factor before endometriosis is fully established.

title: Association between human genomes and mycobacterial genomes contributes to severity and transmissibility of pulmonary tuberculosis
abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) remains a major infectious disease globally. This study aimed to identify determinants of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) transmission clustering, treatment outcome, and pulmonary cavitation by simultaneously analyzing host and pathogen genomic data. Whole-genome sequencing of 1,960 MTB isolates identified four major lineages (L1–L4). Host population stratification by principal component analysis of genome-wide single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) classified 899 patients (70%) into a genetically homogeneous main group for genome-wide association study (GWAS). Multivariate regression demonstrated that MTB lineage was the primary determinant of transmission clustering, rifampicin resistance was the dominant predictor of unfavorable treatment outcome, and host genetic group was independently associated with pulmonary cavitation. GWAS identified novel loci in collectin subfamily member 10 ( COLEC10 ), CTNNA3 , and long intergenic non-coding RNA 2775 ( LINC02775 ) associated with clustering, treatment outcome, and cavitation, respectively, with the association of COLEC10 also found in the remaining group of patients. These findings highlight the importance of integrating bacterial and human genomic analyses to understand tuberculosis host-pathogen interaction.

title: Rhizobacterial biocontrol of potato late blight and genomic insights into disease suppression and growth promotion
abstract: Late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans remains a major challenge to sustainable potato production. In this study, we evaluated five bacterial strains for their ability to reduce late blight and improve potato growth under field, in vitro , detached-leaf, and greenhouse conditions. All tested strains reduced disease severity, with Serratia rubidaea AV10 showing particularly strong antagonistic activity and consistent suppression of disease. Genome sequencing of the two potato-associated strains, AV10 and S. rubidaea EV23, revealed biosynthetic clusters and genes potentially linked to antimicrobial activity, siderophore production, biofilm formation, nutrient acquisition, and plant growth promotion. Bacterial treatment also influenced the expression of potato genes associated with jasmonic acid, ethylene, salicylic acid-related defense, and auxin-linked growth response. Together, these findings identify AV10 and EV23 as promising rhizobacterial candidates for integrated late blight management and provide genomic insight into traits that may contribute to disease suppression and plant growth promotion.

title: Climate vulnerability and governance impact the payoff of policy drivers for SDG 7 outcomes in BRICS countries
abstract: Achieving Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7) in large emerging economies requires energy policies that operate under diverse institutional and climatic conditions. We examine BRICS countries over 2000–2022 to assess how climate vulnerability and governance quality condition the estimated marginal effects of environmental policy stringency, innovation, financial development, inequality, and demographic structure on energy access, renewable energy, and energy efficiency. A two-stage empirical framework combines moderated GLS estimation with post-estimation evaluation of marginal-effect surfaces across contrasting governance-vulnerability regimes and country-specific conditions. The results show that stronger governance and lower climate vulnerability are generally associated with more favorable estimated effects of finance, innovation, and policy stringency, while weak governance and high vulnerability can weaken or reverse these relationships. Policy priorities also differ across SDG 7 subgoals and BRICS economies. These findings support context-specific energy policies that align institutional strengthening and climate resilience with SDG 7 implementation.

title: Impacts of trail running and mountain biking: Resilience of a Mediterranean mountain ecosystem
abstract: Rising outdoor activities have created major challenges for managing protected natural areas due to uncertain ecological effects. This study analyzes the impacts of two expanding sports, trail running and mountain biking, on flat and sloped terrains in a Mediterranean mountain setting in the Sierra de Guadarrama National Park, where transects were subjected to different use intensities. Early short-term impacts and subsequent recovery were monitored over a year using biotic and abiotic indicators: soil compaction, vegetation (total cover, Simpson's diversity index, and composition), bacterial colony-forming units, and edaphic microfauna. Results show that soil compaction and vegetation cover are the most affected among the variables analyzed, with significant alterations when applying a high number of passes on foot or by bicycle, but without significant differences between the two sports. Vegetation recovered faster than soil compaction, and Mediterranean seasonality strongly modulates impacts. Management measures are proposed to balance recreation and conservation.

title: Inducible dCas12a system expands CRISPRi/a capabilities for functional genomics in malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum
abstract: We developed inducible dead Cas12a (dCas12a)-based CRISPR interference/activation (CRISPRi/a) systems for Plasmodium falciparum , expanding the gene regulation toolkit beyond dCas9. Our previous systems fused dCas9 to the catalytic domains of PfSir2a or PfGCN5 under DiCre/ loxP regulon, enabling conditional gene regulation but remaining constrained by Cas9's NGG protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) requirement. Unlike dCas9, dCas12a recognizes T-rich PAMs and processes a single transcript into multiple sgRNAs via its RNase activity, allowing multiplexed regulation of one or multiple genes. Functional validation targeting EBA175 and ATG18 demonstrated that single sgRNAs mediated CRISPRi/a's active gene regulation, while multiplexed sgRNA arrays enhanced CRISPRi activities. Using this platform, we showed that conditional repression of the histone methyltransferase gene PfSET7 impairs schizont egress and merozoite invasion, highlighting its critical role in parasite multiplication, consistent with its Toxoplasma homolog TgADTM1 . Altogether, these results establish dCas12a-based CRISPRi/a as a versatile platform for conditional and multiplexed gene regulation in P . falciparum .

title: Dysregulation of neuronal androgen receptor signaling by divergent collaborative transcription factors in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: The transcriptional mechanisms through which androgens and androgen receptor (AR) exert specific effects on human tissues remain elusive. Here, we demonstrated that neuronal cell-specific transcription factors (TFs) may play an important role as epigenetic modifiers that shape the AR cistrome during neuronal activity. The binding of GATA3 to specific regulatory sequences in human neuronal cell models is associated with enhanced AR-mediated transcription. AR-binding sites (ARBSs) are enriched in regions overlapping with super-enhancers (SEs) that encode critical neuronal factors. Furthermore, AR signaling in aged human male brains indicates its role in supporting neural function and declines during the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). The expression levels of AR-associated TFs were dysregulated during aging and AD development. Altered expression of TFs may contribute to disruption of AR signaling. Thus, collaborative TFs could contribute to the neuronal androgen response and epigenetic regulation involved in aging and the progression of dementia.

title: Resveratrol-mediated Fe(III)/peroxydisulfate activation for ofloxacin degradation at circumneutral pH
abstract: Iron-mediated peroxydisulfate (PDS) activation is limited by slow Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox cycling under circumneutral conditions. Here, resveratrol (RES), a natural stilbene polyphenol, was introduced as a low-dose redox mediator to promote Fe(II) formation from Fe(III) for enhanced PDS activation. The Fe(III)/RES/PDS system showed higher ofloxacin (OFL) degradation than the corresponding single-reagent and binary systems and achieved approximately 90% OFL degradation at pH 6.5. Chemical quenching and competition-kinetic analysis indicated that sulfate radical (SO 4 ·− ) was the major contributor to OFL degradation, while hydroxyl radical ( · OH) played a secondary role. Matrix experiments showed that Cl − and NO 3 − had minor effects, whereas NO 2 − strongly inhibited OFL degradation. This work provides a case study of RES-mediated Fe(III)/PDS activation for antibiotic degradation under near-neutral conditions.

title: Lateralized vagal oxytocin receptor signaling separately controls feeding and socioemotional functions via hypothalamic oxytocin neurons
abstract: Oxytocin neurons in the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVH Oxt ) regulate feeding, anxiety, and social behaviors. Activation of Oxt receptor (Oxtr)-expressing vagal sensory neurons engages these PVH Oxt neurons and improves hyperphagic obesity; however, their roles in anxiety and sociability remain unclear. Here, we activated vagal Oxtr-expressing neurons in male mice using a single intraperitoneal (IP) Oxt injection or chemogenetics. IP Oxt reduced anxiety-like behavior, enhanced social interaction, and suppressed feeding while activating both vagal sensory neurons and PVH Oxt neurons. These effects were abolished by chemogenetic inhibition of PVH Oxt neurons or central Oxtr blockade. Subdiaphragmatic vagotomy revealed lateralized functions: right-side vagotomy eliminated anxiolytic and prosocial effects, whereas left-side vagotomy blocked feeding suppression. Consistently, chemogenetic activation of left-sided neurons suppressed feeding, while right-sided activation reduced anxiety and increased sociability. These findings identify Oxtr-expressing vagal sensory neurons as a major peripheral pathway in which left- and right-sided inputs differentially control feeding and socioemotional behaviors.

title: Massive histone H3 phosphorylation without mitotic chromosome condensation
abstract: Histone post-translation modifications change dramatically as cells enter mitosis, Indeed, histone phosphorylation and deacetylation have been proposed to be major factors driving the compaction of mitotic chromosomes. However, whether these modification changes directly regulate mitotic chromatin compaction remains a subject of debate. Here, we use a CDK1as chemical-genetic system to accumulate cells in G2 phase. Treatment of these G2 cells with the phosphatase inhibitor calyculin A efficiently causes them to undergo premature chromosome condensation, even when the CDK1as allele is inhibited with 1NM-PP1. Surprisingly, simultaneous treatment of the cells with R547, an inhibitor of CDK1, 2 and 4 kinases, causes them to remain phenotypically in G2 phase. Strikingly, although mitotic-like chromatin condensation fails to occur in these cells, LC-MS reveals that histone H3 phosphorylation occurs even more efficiently than in a normal mitosis. Furthermore, histone deacetylation also occurs in those interphase-looking calyculin A-treated cells. These results reveal that histone phosphorylation and deacetylation are not sufficient to drive mitotic-like chromosome condensation and compaction.

title: High-resolution prediction and risk mapping of Haemaphysalis longicornis habitat suitability in the Jiaodong Peninsula, China
abstract: Ticks are vectors of numerous human pathogens, and accurate predictions of their spatial distribution are essential for the effective prevention and control of tick-borne diseases. High-resolution predictions remain scarce in China. To address this gap, a tick survey was conducted across the Jiaodong Peninsula at 2,647 points during the summer of 2024, integrating high-resolution environmental variables. Seven machine-learning algorithms were used, and ensemble learning was applied, resulting in a habitat-suitability map for Haemaphysalis longicornis at a 10-meter resolution. The ensemble model showed robust predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.8355). Summer normalized difference vegetation index was the primary environmental driver, followed by land use and land cover and winter normalized difference vegetation index. High risk villages accounted for 70.0%, 40.2%, and 16.9% of rural, urban rural fringe, and urban areas, respectively. Ensemble machine-learning provides a robust approach, revealing how ecological factors and human activities shape distribution patterns and risk heterogeneity.

title: Small-molecule activators of the Staphylococcus aureus ClpC/ClpP AAA+ protease
abstract: Summary/Abstract The central AAA+ ClpC/ClpP protease in Gram-positive bacteria is crucial for virulence and stress resistance and has been recognized as drug target. Natural cyclic peptides deregulate the essential Mycobacterium tuberculosis ClpC1 and cause cell death. Similarly, overactivated mutants of the non-essential Staphylococcus aureus ClpC homologue cause uncontrolled proteolysis and severe toxicity in vivo . However, no chemical modulators of S. aureus ClpC have been described. Here, using a biochemical high-throughput screen we identify eight chemically distinct bona fide small molecules that robustly stimulate ClpC ATPase and proteolytic activity in vitro . Structural, computational, and mutational analyses define two ligandable regulatory sites within the ClpC N-terminal domain (NTD) as compound targets: a conserved hydrophobic groove and an allosteric pArg1 pocket, both engaged in substrate recognition. These findings establish S. aureus ClpC as chemically targetable and provide mechanistic insight into its regulatory architecture, enabling future development and optimization of chemical probes to deregulate AAA+ protease control.

title: Short term overfeeding disrupts small intestinal barrier integrity and activates hepatic immunity in healthy men
abstract: Obesity is associated with intestinal barrier dysfunction and low-grade inflammation, prompting investigations of early human adaptations to overnutrition. In a controlled "holiday-style" overfeeding model, healthy men underwent a 2-week hypercaloric, sedentary lifestyle with 8-week follow-up (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04859322). A targeted gastrointestinal uptake and translocation (GUT) plasma panel showed increased citrulline, consistent with enhanced epithelial absorptive capacity, and mucosa-restricted immune activation, reflected by elevated anti-lipopolysaccharide (LPS) immunoglobulin (Ig)A, without systemic 16S rRNA changes. A dynamic zonulin-like signal and hepatic inflammatory markers (serum amyloid A (SAA), C-reactive protein, interleukin-32) also increased after overfeeding. Most perturbations normalized after return to habitual lifestyle, but anti-LPS IgA, SAA, lipocalin-2, intercellular adhesion molecule-1, and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 remained elevated, indicating a partially persistent inflammatory imprint. These findings reveal how overfeeding episodes reshape epithelial, mucosal, and hepatic immune responses and highlight plasma biomarker panels as scalable tools to interrogate intestinal function and gut-liver crosstalk in human studies.

title: Species-specific inflammatory responses of chondrocytes: Toward evidence-based model selection in OA research
abstract: To inform evidence-based osteoarthritis model selection, this study compares inflammatory responses of articular chondrocytes from six species (human, horse, sheep, rabbit, rat, and mouse) under standardized IL-1β and TNF-α stimulation in 2D and 3D culture. Chondrocytes were assessed for viability, proliferation, wound healing, and transcriptomic changes via RT-qPCR and 3′RNA sequencing. Marked interspecies differences were observed in morphology, proliferation, and inflammatory gene activation, with only two genes ( SOD2 , NFKBIA ) conserved across all species. Human, horse, and rat chondrocytes shared pathways including acute phase response, deubiquitination, and class-A/1-GPCR signaling. Species-specific responses included matrix remodeling in horses, rheumatoid arthritis-related pathways in sheep, and mixed inflammatory-regenerative profiles in rats. While no species fully replicates human OA, equine and rat chondrocytes best reflect key aspects of human inflammation. These findings underscore the need for molecular criteria in model selection and advocate for human cell-based models when interspecies differences limit the translational value of animal models.

title: Evidence for exposure to and infection with H5 clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses among polar bears inhabiting Alaska
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) have become widespread among wildlife including within the Arctic. We summarize histopathological findings for three cases of HPAIV infection among polar bears ( Ursus maritimus ) inhabiting Alaska, genomically characterize viruses causing disease, and assess probable non-lethal exposures. Polar bears found dead and infected with HPAIVs exhibited meningoencephalomyelitis and neuronal necrosis, consistent with neurologic disease. Genomic sequence information obtained for H5N1 and H5N5 subtype HPAIVs associated with two cases supported epidemiologically independent spillovers. Serologic testing provided evidence for antibodies reactive to H5 and N1 antigens among most polar bears inhabiting Alaska during 2023–2024, consistent with contemporary non-lethal exposures, whereas antibodies were not found among bears sampled during 2013. These data indicate that HPAIV infection may represent an emerging threat to polar bear health within the Alaska Arctic; though, population immunity seems to be building and may protect this species from widespread demographic impacts of disease.

title: Low-frequency non-destructive adaptive fastest pulse preheating for lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Low-temperature polarization sharply reduces lithium-ion battery capacity and power, limiting electric vehicles and energy storage systems in cold regions. Bidirectional pulsed current (BPC) self-heating exploits increased internal resistance to enable efficient, rapid, and uniform heating, but high-rate pulses may induce lithium plating. Although high-frequency (>100 Hz) BPC suppresses plating, it requires additional power components. Here, we propose an adaptive, non-destructive BPC heating strategy that adjusts pulse current with temperature and state of charge (SOC), enabling the fastest heating within the lithium-plating-free boundary at low frequencies (<1 Hz). Using parameters optimized with three-electrode cells, lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) batteries were heated from −15°C to 10°C while maintaining the negative electrode potential above 0 V (vs. Li/Li + ). After 100 heating cycles, neither chemistry showed capacity degradation, and post-heating analysis revealed no lithium plating, confirming safe and non-destructive low-temperature heating without compromising battery performance or requiring high-frequency auxiliary power electronics.

title: Cancer cell-intrinsic rewiring of the colorectal cancer secretome
abstract: Secreted factors are essential mediators of cellular communication that are exploited by tumors to control their environment and evade immune attack. However, how cancer cells rewire their secretome is unclear due to challenges in reliably profiling cancer cell-specific secreted factors. Here, we apply a click chemistry-based approach to selectively profile the secretome of patient-derived colorectal cancer (CRC) and healthy colon organoids. We observe cancer cell-intrinsic rewiring of the secretome during malignancy, with clear separation between microsatellite stable (MSS) and instable cancers. We then leverage this secretomics dataset to identify secreted factors that mark immune-excluded cancers, revealing NOTUM as a marker of decreased T cell infiltration across four independent datasets. Overall, our study provides an in-depth characterization of the cancer cell-intrinsic secretome of MSS-CRC and nominates NOTUM as a secreted factor marking immune-excluded colorectal cancers. This provides a scalable framework to link cancer cell-derived secreted factors to relevant tumor phenotypes.

title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from multiple pretrained protein language models, aligns graph-based structural features with pretrained semantic embeddings for drugs under subspace constraints, and progressively refines drug-protein interaction representations through cascaded cross-modal signal propagation. Experiments on six benchmark datasets under standard, cold-start, and cross-domain settings demonstrate that SF-DTI achieves competitive performance relative to seven state-of-the-art baselines across evaluation scenarios. These results suggest that SF-DTI is a promising framework for DTI prediction and may support virtual screening, drug repositioning, and drug discovery.

title: Longitudinal pre-diagnostic blood samples predict osteoporosis risk
abstract: Cross-sectional biomarker discovery studies for degenerative diseases are limited by selection bias, post-diagnostic confounding, and high biological variability. Repeated pre-diagnostic sampling can address these limitations. We analyzed 538 plasma metabolomic profiles (1-6 samples per participant, yearly intervals) from 99 pre-diagnostic osteoporosis cases and 99 matched controls in the Danish Blood Donor Study. We compared performance of cross-sectional and longitudinal modeling using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression and random forest. Longitudinal LASSO modeling of metabolite trajectories achieved area under the curve (AUC) values between 0.67 and 0.76, outperforming cross-sectional models with AUC values of 0.57-0.63. Batch- and participant-independent validation of the best model demonstrated stable methodology (AUC: 0.70). The longitudinal data revealed that hippuric acid decreased over time in cases while increasing in controls. We conclude that longitudinal sampling costs more per participant, but the substantial information gain makes it a viable strategy when patient recruitment, not sampling capacity, is the bottleneck.

title: Impact of GCR and SPE on space radiation shielding: OLTARIS simulation and quantum optimization of material selection using quantum algorithms
abstract: During long-term deep-space missions, a key challenge to the human and spacecraft is the space radiation, which is coming from the three different sources: Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCRs), Solar Particle Events (SPEs), and trapped particles in regions of Van Allen belts. High-energy particle radiation can have harmful effects on the spacecraft systems, sensors, electronic components, and astronauts, compromising mission reliability. This makes effective shielding a critical requirement. Traditionally, passive shielding materials such as aluminum have been used, but their limitations, especially in generating secondary radiations, necessitate the search for more efficient alternatives. In this study, the performance of various shielding materials, such as Lithium hydride (LiH), Polyethylene (C 2 H 4 ), Lithium borohydride (LiBH 4 ), Beryllium borohydride (Be(BH 4 ) 2 ), and Ammonia borane (NH 3 BH 3 ) is systematically evaluated in the GCR and SPE environment using On-Line Tool for the Assessment of Radiation in Space (OLTARIS), a NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)-developed simulation tool. Further, the effect of SPEs (October 1989) on the performance of shielding materials is studied and evaluated through particle flux distributions (energy spectrum) and equivalent dose distributions for these materials. The relative shielding effectiveness of these materials in the SPE environment varied from that in the GCR environment, suggesting that material performance is dependent on the radiation environment. Beryllium borohydride (Be(BH 4 ) 2 ) emerges as the best material in the SPE environment, while lithium hydride (LiH) gives the least dose equivalent in the GCR environment. The particle-wise dose equivalent and flux contributions reveal that, in the SPE environment, the material performance is directly linked to the hydrogen content of the material. In addition, the effect of solar modulation on dose equivalent in the GCR environment is studied. As solar modulation increases, the GCR intensity reduces and hence dose equivalent also reduces. As the space radiation environment consists of complex particle radiation of high energies, in order to validate the large sample of materials for space radiation shielding, the combinatorial complexity of possible configurations presents a major computational challenge. To address this challenge, the material selection problem is formulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model and is solved using the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). By mapping OLTARIS dose-equivalent data to the Ising model and utilizing the quantum-classical hybrid approaches of VQE and QAOA, optimal shielding configurations that minimize radiation dose are identified, demonstrating the potential of Quantum Algorithms in advancing space radiation protection strategies. Our results are in agreement between OLTARIS and Quantum Optimization in the SPE environment.

title: FKBP12 determines ligand-specific SMAD signaling in individual living endothelial cells
abstract: The BMP signaling pathway plays a pivotal role in regulating the formation and maintenance of our vascular system, employing a diverse set of ligands, receptors, and cytoplasmic mediators. However, little is known about how the interplay of these elements is regulated dynamically in individual living endothelial cells. Here, we developed fluorescent reporter to quantify BMP signaling and used a combination of time-resolved microscopy and computer-aided analysis to demonstrate ligand-specific dynamics of SMAD1, SMAD5, and SMAD9. Using this approach, we identified FKBP12 as a critical regulator of receptor complex activity that determines the balance of SMAD1/5/9 and SMAD2/3 signaling upon treatment with angiogenic ligands such as BMP7 and Activin A. This provides insights into the regulation of the BMP pathway in endothelial cells and offers a potential node for modulating vascular pathologies where the SMAD1/5/9-SMAD2/3 balance is disrupted.

title: Patent insights on advanced polymer composites for transport systems
abstract: Polymeric materials have become increasingly important in transportation and aerospace due to their low weight, processability, and ability to provide tailored functional properties. This study examines the patent landscape of polymeric materials used in these sectors through a combined keyword and International Patent Classification (IPC) search strategy. The results show that the United States accounts for the largest share among national patent offices, while the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) represents the major international filing route. The leading IPC categories include B29C, C08L, C08K, C08F, C08J, B32B, C09D, and C08G. Recent patent activity is concentrated on lightweight structures, protective and flame-resistant coatings, thermal management, bio-based resins, fiber-reinforced composites, graphene-based materials, and high-temperature polymers. Overall, the findings indicate that current development is increasingly directed toward durable, sustainable, thermally functional, and multifunctional polymer systems for advanced transportation and aerospace applications.

title: Energy absorption of multicell thin walled structures filled with polyurethane infiltrated open cell aluminum foam
abstract: Compact energy absorbers are needed to protect testing electronics in high-impact systems with limited installation space. Unlike previous studies that mainly examined tubular or fully filled configurations, this work investigates selective filling within a 12-mm-high multi-cell thin-walled structure. Partial and full configurations using aluminum foam (AF) and polyurethane-infiltrated aluminum foam (AF/PU) were evaluated through quasi-static compression, dynamic impact testing, finite element simulations, and theoretical analysis. Comparisons among five configurations and three wall thicknesses showed that filler distribution affected the balance between crushing resistance and effective crushing stroke. The partially filled AF/PU structure with a 1.2 mm wall thickness exhibited the best overall performance, absorbing 895.41 J quasi-statically and 984.40 J dynamically, with a volumetric specific energy absorption of 21.32 J/cm 3 and crushing force efficiency of 0.84. Compared with full filling, selective AF/PU filling uses less filler while retaining greater deformation space, providing a practical strategy for compact impact protection.

title: Viral persistence and immune dysfunction in chronic hepatitis B: Mechanisms of post-treatment antigen asynchrony
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Following antiviral therapy, the dynamics of hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) may become discordant, a phenomenon referred to as post-treatment asynchrony. This review summarizes the three principal forms of post-treatment asynchrony and examines their underlying mechanisms. We integrate the limitations of current antiviral targets, host immune dysfunction, virological characteristics, and host genetic factors into a unified framework to explain the discordant dynamics between HBsAg and HBV DNA. A better understanding of post-treatment asynchrony may help refine the interpretation of serological markers and inform patient stratification and individualized therapeutic strategies. Overall, this review provides an integrated perspective on the mechanisms and clinical significance of post-treatment asynchrony in CHB.

title: The effectiveness of sound-based interventions on promoting sleep quality in hospitalized patients: A systematic review
abstract: Sleep quality strongly affects hospitalized patients' recovery, yet pain, anxiety, and environmental factors such as noise and light frequently disrupt it. Sound-based therapies offer a promising, non-pharmacological approach, but their effectiveness has not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review examined fifteen studies (2012-2026, 2024 patients, mostly intensive care settings) evaluating sound-based interventions, including calming music, nature sounds, and white noise, on sleep quality. Intervention duration and timing varied widely, from brief five-minute sessions to continuous overnight administration, and sleep quality was most often measured using validated questionnaires. Despite substantial heterogeneity, sound-based interventions were associated with an overall improvement in sleep quality, although effect sizes varied considerably and several studies showed no significant benefit. These findings support the potential of low-cost, non-pharmacological sound interventions to improve sleep in hospital settings, while underscoring the need for further research to clarify which intervention characteristics drive effectiveness.

title: Resilience assessment of lithium ion battery supply chains under critical mineral shortages
abstract: The energy transition and transportation electrification have increased the reliance of lithium ion battery supply chains on critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt, and nickel. Here, we construct a multi-tier interfirm supply network of nine major battery manufacturers and develop a propagation recovery model to assess mineral shortage impacts and recovery pathways. Lithium shortages generate the largest cascading losses, followed by cobalt and nickel shortages. Recovery is primarily achieved through cross-tier resource reallocation, which contributes approximately 70% of total recovery, whereas newly established supply links provide a smaller contribution. Manufacturer resilience varies across minerals, reflecting heterogeneous supply chain exposure and recovery capacity. These findings identify mineral-specific risk pathways and recovery mechanisms, providing insights for resilient supply chain management and critical mineral governance during energy transitions.

title: Real-time intelligence framework for microplastic monitoring and coastal resilience
abstract: The growing threat of microplastic contamination of the marine biosphere requires that monitoring technologies surpass the limitations of conventional approaches. This paper presents the development and validation of an integrated, machine learning-based framework for real-time detection and management of microplastics in coastal environments, whose primary contributions are real-time IoT-edge-cloud integration, multi-sensor fusion, and 72 h predictive modeling. We deployed a multi-sensor platform integrating hyperspectral imaging (400–2,500 nm) with IoT sensor networks at five monitoring locations over 18 months. The analytical pipeline employs a stacked ensemble of CNN, SVM, and random forest algorithms with soft-vote fusion. The framework achieved 96.3% accuracy in classifying microplastic polymers and successfully detected particles as small as 75 μm in diameter. The system demonstrated a strong correlation ( r = 0.92, p < 0.001) between predicted and observed pollution levels, enabling 72 h forecasting of pollution events with 84% probability. The framework processes samples 340% faster than traditional laboratory analysis while reducing operational costs by 67%. Through continuous real-time evaluation, this scalable solution will provide a quick instrument in a global network of coastal monitoring tools to create evidence-based policy and focused intervention approaches.

title: A multimodal in situ framework for spatial characterization applied on SARS-CoV-2 live-attenuated vaccines in the nasal mucosa
abstract: Respiratory viruses frequently initiate infection in the nasal mucosa, where virus-host interactions shape disease progression and transmission. Yet this site remains undercharacterized due to anatomical and technical challenges. Spatially resolved technologies are limited by cost and complexity, leaving most studies reliant on bulk or descriptive approaches lacking spatial context. We present a framework for spatially resolved investigation of infections in the nasal cavity. Using wild-type SARS-CoV-2 and two live-attenuated vaccines (OTS-206, OTS-228) as model viruses in Syrian hamsters, we integrate standardized sampling, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, multiplex RNA in situ hybridization, and quantitative image analysis across spatial scales, including tissue, single-cell, and subcellular resolution. We identified distinct infection patterns and graduated tissue damage from wild-type to OTS-228. Despite limited infection, OTS-228 induces a robust tissue-preserving immune response. Subcellular analysis shows that both vaccines exhibit a primarily cytoplasmic distribution of host antiviral transcripts, whereas WT infection is characterized by predominantly nuclear RNA localization.

title: Network-based characterization of latent co-testing patterns in antimicrobial susceptibility testing
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance depends on antimicrobial susceptibility testing, yet antibiotic panels vary by pathogen cohort, specimen, year, ward, and care setting. We term these empirically reconstructed testing architectures shadow antibiograms: structures that shape which susceptibility results enter surveillance datasets and which resistance relationships can be observed. We analyzed approximately 13 million bacterial isolates from Germany's National Antibiotic Resistance Surveillance system (2019-2023) across six WHO BPPL-aligned operational cohorts. Co-testing networks were constructed using Jaccard, Dice, cosine, and phi-coefficient similarity, evaluated with Fisher's exact tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and partitioned with multi-resolution Louvain community detection. Networks contained three to four dominant co-testing communities; false discovery rate (FDR) retention ranged from 89 to 100% across cohorts and specimen types. Jaccard provided the best balance of coherence, stability, antimicrobial-class alignment, interpretability, and edge retention. This work provides one of the first national-scale empirical characterizations of shadow antibiogram structure, supporting diagnostic stewardship and bias-aware AMR surveillance interpretation.

title: Multimodal imaging reveals no evidence for magnetite-based magnetoreceptors in the mole-rat eye
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetoreception, the ability to perceive the geomagnetic field, is widespread across animals. The underlying sensory mechanism remains elusive, but a long-standing hypothesis proposes single-domain magnetite linked to mechanosensitive ion channels. The Ansell’s mole-rat ( Fukomys anselli ) is a subterranean rodent with a magnetic sense, and published behavioral and histological data are consistent with magnetite-based magnetoreceptors in the cornea or retina. Here, we systematically screened for magnetite in the mole-rat eye, combining iron detection via enhanced Prussian blue staining and synchrotron X-ray fluorescence microscopy (XFM) with magnetic detection via MRI quantitative susceptibility mapping (MRI-QSM) and quantum-diamond microscopy (QDM). This revealed only a few iron particles in the retina and cornea, which predominantly overlapped with titanium or chromium, indicating a non-biogenic origin. XFM showed iron-enriched lines in the cornea, but these did not show ferrimagnetic signals. Focusing on other ocular tissues, MRI-QSM revealed the highest susceptibility in the ciliary body, where iron-rich pigmented cells were identified. A TEM-screen, however, failed to detect single-domain magnetite particles in these cells. We conclude that our high-sensitivity multimodal screen provides no evidence for magnetite-based magnetoreceptors in the mole-rat eye, suggesting that mole-rat magnetoreceptors either do not reside in the eye or are based on different physical principles.

title: Reconstructing tropical cyclone intensity in southeastern China over the past century using tree-rings
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) significantly impact coastal forests, yet long-term records remain scarce. In this study, we investigate the influence of TC frequency and intensity on the radial growth patterns of three dominant tree species in natural forests of southeastern China. Using tree-ring data, we reconstruct historical TC intensity and explore its relationship with the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Our findings reveal that anomalously high TC wind speeds during the late 1950s and late 1980s led to enhanced radial growth in the studied trees due to improved light conditions caused by TC impact. The reconstructed TC wind speeds since the 1920s indicate that the intensity of landfalling TCs in southeastern China increased during El Niño phases. These results demonstrate that tree-growth anomalies can serve as a reliable proxy for reconstructing TC activity beyond the instrumental record, providing valuable insights into the linkages between TC variability and large-scale climate oscillations.

title: Trimodal ultrasound imaging of brain-tumor interaction
abstract: Patients with brain tumors often suffer debilitating neurological dysfunction as their tumors disrupt brain tissue, affecting both local and global neural activity and blood flow. However, studying tumor-brain interactions in animal models is challenging due to a lack of methods that simultaneously capture dynamics of tumor growth, neural activity and vascular alterations over time. Here, we overcome this limitation using a multimodal ultrasound imaging platform, an imaging technique that offers brain-wide coverage in living animals at 10-100 μm resolution. To monitor the co-evolution of tumor growth, neural activity and vascular remodeling, we integrated (1) nonlinear imaging of acoustic reporter gene expressing-tumors, (2) hemodynamic functional imaging of brain activity, and (3) super-resolution microscopy of the vasculature. Integrating these modalities for the first time and applying them to a common model of glioblastoma, we followed tumor-brain interactions in individual animals over their disease lifetimes. Our approach allowed us to precisely map the spatial displacement of functional brain regions, the local and global disruption of functional connectivity, and the remodeling of the blood supply to support tumor growth. This integrated method bridges a critical gap in brain cancer research and therapy development by providing a unified dynamic view of what happens to the brain as tumors grow within it.

title: MED26 facilitates Mediator-Pol II complex assembly and promotes nuclear stress body formation during heat stress
abstract: Cells adapt to environmental stress by reprogramming gene expression. During heat stress, the transcription factor heat shock factor 1 (HSF1) translocates into the nucleus and activates heat shock-responsive loci, including the long non-coding RNA HSATIII, promoting nuclear stress body (nSB) formation. We show that the Mediator complex subunit MED26 enhances HSATIII transcription and nSB formation through a mechanism distinct from its role at heat-shock response (HSR) genes. Under heat stress, MED26-containing Mediator is recruited to HSR genes and nSBs through interactions with HSF1 and MED15. Phosphorylation of the intrinsically disordered region of HSF1 appears to facilitate Mediator recruitment to nSBs. Acute loss of MED26 leads to the dissociation of the Mediator and RNA polymerase II (Pol II) from HSR gene promoters, whereas the Mediator remains bound to HSATIII despite Pol II dissociation. These results suggest that MED26 acts as molecular switch, thereby facilitating Mediator-Pol II complex assembly at nSBs and promoting nSB formation during heat stress.

title: Hyperopic reserve, early myopia risk and screening strategies in children: A multi-regional analysis from the CREAM-KIDS consortium
abstract: Reduced hyperopic reserve (HR) in early childhood is a strong predictor of future myopia. A harmonized dataset from the CREAM-Kids Consortium was utilized to assess regional differences in HR. Among 7-year olds, mean (SD) HR was 1.44 (1.17) D in Europe, 1.32 (0.80) D in Australia, 0.78 (0.89) D in Hong Kong, and 0.59 (0.66) D in Singapore ( p < 0.001). The annualized decline in HR was −0.12 D/year among European-Australian followed from age 6.73 (0.64) to 11.64 (1.49), and −0.35 D/year among Asian followed from age 7.71 (0.77) to 10.71 (0.77). In European-Australian aged 6–7, the sensitivity and specificity of myopia screening was 67%–75% and 98%, and in Asian aged 4–9, 92%–99% and 70%–77%, respectively. Asian children demonstrated substantially lower HR and a faster consumption than their European and Australian peers, placing a larger proportion of Asian children at higher risk for early-onset myopia.

title: Reprogramming bone homeostasis: The recoupling-oriented framework of bidirectional regulation strategies for osteoporosis
abstract: Current osteoporosis treatments reduce fracture risk by suppressing bone resorption, stimulating bone formation, or combining both effects. Yet these clinical benefits do not show whether formation has resumed at sites where bone was previously resorbed. This Review uses a remodeling recoupling framework to examine this resorption-to-formation transition. We define recoupling as restoration of the sequence from resorption through reversal to osteoblast recruitment and bone formation. This differs from bidirectional regulation, in which osteoblast activity increases and osteoclast activity decreases without evidence that the two responses are linked. We review the cellular communication, signaling pathways, cell-survival mechanisms, and systemic conditions that influence this transition. We also assess candidate targets and treatments according to the strength of clinical, human, animal, and mechanistic evidence. The available evidence is strongest for established therapies and several human-supported pathways, whereas many proposed targets and delivery approaches remain preclinical. This framework may help guide treatment sequencing, patient selection, bone-targeted delivery, and the development of measures that determine whether formation follows resorption.

title: When grooming stalls: Assessing communicative repair, negotiation, and progressivity in chimpanzees
abstract: Human social interaction is built on progressivity (the forward flow of interaction), which communicative breakdowns may disrupt. Communicative repair (resolving communicative troubles) and negotiation (a collaborative sequence to resolve communicative breakdowns) may both serve as processes to restore progressivity following breakdowns. Here, we investigated gestural redoings (reproduction of a previous signal in any form), negotiation, and progressivity in grooming interactions ( N = 311) among male East African chimpanzees ( Pan troglodytes schweinfurthii ) in the wild. These chimpanzees produced gestural redoings as repetitions, substitutions, and modifications ( N = 158) occurring at delayed temporal gaps relative to grooming turn-taking latencies. Both substitutions and negotiations ( N = 219) were associated with restored progressivity. Strongly bonded pairs showed a higher likelihood of compromise outcomes during negotiation. These findings indicate that these chimpanzees employed repair-like processes associated with restored progressivity, bearing certain resemblances to those observed in human conversation—raising the possibility that such capacities may have evolutionary roots predating the emergence of language.

title: Procedural circulatory support-enabled intracoronary cell delivery in advanced dilated cardiomyopathy
abstract: Advanced heart failure due to dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) has limited treatment options. Although intracoronary autologous cell therapy may improve cardiac function, its use in patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction is limited by procedural risk. This exploratory study investigated whether temporary mechanical circulatory support with an Impella device could enable safer therapy delivery. Twenty patients with DCM and a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of ≤35% received granulocyte colony-stimulating factor pretreatment followed by Impella-supported intracoronary infusion of autologous bone marrow mononuclear cells. The procedure was feasible, well tolerated, and not associated with major complications. After three months, mean LVEF increased by 2.9%, with numerically greater gains in those with more severe baseline impairment. Participants also experienced symptomatic, exercise capacity, and quality of life improvements. Changes in microvascular function and circulating soluble receptor for advanced glycation end-products (sRAGE) suggested potential mechanistic pathways. As a single-arm study, these findings are hypothesis generating and support further evaluation in randomized controlled trials.

title: Deep brain stimulation mechanisms in comorbid pain and emotional dysregulation from animal models
abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a potent neuromodulatory intervention for chronic pain and comorbid affective disorders. This review synthesizes preclinical evidence detailing the neural circuits and molecular cascades engaged by DBS in models of pain and emotional dysregulation. We delineate how DBS-targeting regions like the prefrontal cortex (PFC), thalamus, and nucleus accumbens (NAc) recruit the prefrontal-midbrain-spinal axis to facilitate endogenous opioid release and modulate neurotransmission, thereby attenuating nociception. Concurrently, stimulating the ventromedial PFC (vmPFC) or lateral habenula (LHb) ameliorates affective deficits by restoring serotonergic (5-HT) and dopaminergic (DA) tone and stabilizing circuit dynamics. By mapping these convergent and divergent mechanisms, we highlight how DBS fine-tunes reward, anti-reward, and descending antinociceptive pathways. This mechanism-based framework outlines a translational roadmap for personalized neuromodulation, guiding symptom-specific target selection and the development of biomarker-driven, closed-loop DBS systems to concurrently treat pain and affective pathologies.

title: Long non-coding RNAs in tuberculosis: Immune regulation and clinical biomarker potential
abstract: (Mtb), remains the leading infectious cause of mortality worldwide, with an estimated 1.25 million deaths in 2023. Despite therapeutic advances, the lack of precise early screening tools continues to impede epidemic control. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as essential modulators of host anti-Mtb immunity, and elucidating their functional mechanisms is pivotal for developing effective interventions. This review systematically synthesizes lncRNA-mediated immune regulation during Mtb infection, with emphasis on their roles in modulating immune cell death, extending beyond apoptosis to encompass necrosis and pyroptosis. Importantly, we provide a comprehensive analysis of lncRNAs and related gene polymorphisms as predictive biomarkers for anti-TB drug-induced adverse reactions. Current research gaps and future priorities are also discussed. Together, the dual potential of lncRNAs as molecular diagnostics and candidate targets for host-directed therapy represents a promising frontier in TB management.

title: Strongly coupled cogeneration increases the competitive value of nuclear reactors for industrial process heat
abstract: We incorporate the thermodynamic efficiency benefits of cogeneration into an evaluation of the competitiveness of alternative nuclear reactor designs in supplying heat to a sample of industrial facilities in two regions of the US. Earlier work by Vanatta et al. had captured the capacity utilization benefits but had not incorporated the efficiency gain. Doing so increases the number of facilities for which nuclear supply is competitive. Doing so also reorders which design is most competitive for any specific industrial facility.

title: Morphological plasticity facilitates lung adaptation and dynamic immune remodeling in Mycobacterium abscessus infection
abstract: Mycobacterium abscessus pulmonary disease (Mab-PD) shows rising global incidence and low cure rates. Mab exhibits marked phenotypic heterogeneity, with infection outcomes likely dependent on strain-specific host interactions. Through in vivo morphotype switching, we obtained a rough strain (Mab-R) that showed higher virulence, bacterial loads, and lung pathology than the smooth morphotype. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that Mab-R adapts to macrophage functional states by modulating virulence and metabolic genes, promoting intracellular survival. Single-cell RNA sequencing uncovered dynamic macrophage reprogramming during infection. In acute infection, alveolar macrophages and C1qa+ interstitial macrophages cleared Mab-R via programmed cell death, while newly recruited monocytes showed strong phagocytic capacity but incomplete bacterial clearance. During chronic infection, enhanced T cell immunity and resident-like macrophage dominance facilitated inflammation resolution. These findings reveal host-pathogen interplay driving Mab-R persistence and identify bacterial metabolic adaptation and macrophage reprogramming as potential therapeutic targets for chronic Mab-PD.

title: Neurofibrillary tangle deposition in primary idiotypic isocortices using flortaucipir PET in histopathologically confirmed Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Tau deposition in Alzheimer's disease (AD) spreads throughout the brain in a stereotypical pattern captured by the Braak neurofibrillary tangle staging scheme. While involvement of primary isocortex defines the highest stage, it is unclear whether flortaucipir PET uptake differs among primary isocortical regions. We determined relationships between flortaucipir uptake in primary visual, auditory, motor, and somatosensory isocortices and Braak stage in 155 autopsy-confirmed participants with AD. Flortaucipir uptake was observed starting at Braak stage V, with visual and auditory isocortices showing greater and faster increases in uptake than somatosensory and motor; age and APOE ε4 influenced uptake. Flortaucipir uptake and change in primary isocortices were similar in the lateral temporal cortex but different in the entorhinal cortex. Findings suggest that tau deposition in primary isocortices in AD occurs earlier than currently emphasized, although there are differences among them. Given these findings, clinical correlations of primary isocortical involvement in AD need to be evaluated.

title: Sonocavitation therapy for pancreatic cancer: Research progress, clinical application and future perspectives
