Analysis of the dorsal pallium-meninges boundary showed specific regulatory patterns in outer brain and meningeal layers, with strong links to developmental processes and distance-dependent regulation in major pathways, including those involved in neurodevelopmental disease and cancer. Overall, REBOSEP provides a systematic framework for studying gene expression regulation at tissue boundaries.

title: PTTG1 drives intestinal-type gastric cancer progression via G2/M checkpoint-mediated cell-cycle reprogramming
abstract: Intestinal-type gastric cancer (IGC) progresses through the Correa cascade, yet the molecular determinants of this transition remain insufficiently defined. Using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on matched normal, intestinal metaplasia, and tumor tissues from five patients, we identified eight epithelial subtypes, including a transitional enterocyte population that expanded along the disease trajectory. Pseudotime and network analyses revealed a progressive upregulation of PTTG1 , which was further supported by public cohorts, bulk transcriptomics, and tissue microarrays. Functional assays demonstrated that PTTG1 knockdown impaired G2/M checkpoint regulation and reduced gastric cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas its overexpression enhanced organoid growth and altered mucin-related features. In xenograft models, PTTG1 depletion suppressed tumor growth and was accompanied by secretory differentiation-associated histological changes. Collectively, these findings suggest that PTTG1 contributes to intestinal-type gastric cancer progression by regulating G2/M checkpoint-associated programs and modulating mucin-associated phenotypes, supporting its potential as a risk biomarker and candidate therapeutic target for IGC prevention.

title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics uncovers region-specific molecular features underlying selective aging vulnerability of cholinergic neurons
abstract: Cholinergic neurons exhibit functional and molecular heterogeneity across the basal forebrain (BF), midbrain (MB), and brainstem (BS), while the aging-associated transcriptional features remain poorly characterized. Here, we performed single nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on 108,062 nuclei from the MS/VDB, HDB/SI, PPTG/LDTG, 7N, and 12N in adult and aged mice. BF cells showed greater age-associated transcriptomic alterations than MB and BS cells, with pronounced region-specific divergence among cholinergic neurons. Intercellular communication analysis revealed BF-specific age-related changes in APP and ApoE signaling. Within this altered milieu, intrinsic transcriptional responses varied across brain regions. In aged BF cholinergic neurons, transcriptional responses were characterized by increased oxidative stress and inflammatory signatures and reduced expression of genes involved in neuronal structural maintenance. In contrast, MB and BS cholinergic neurons maintained relatively stable transcriptional profiles. These findings reveal region-specific associations between extracellular signaling and intrinsic transcriptional stress, highlighting a selective imbalance that underlies the vulnerability of BF cholinergic neurons.

title: Global epidemiological and genetic burden of rare neurological diseases in children
abstract: We assessed the global burden of rare childhood neurological diseases from 1990 to 2021 and projected trends to 2050 using Global Burden of Disease data, alongside an analysis of the genetic burden from ClinVar. Four neurological conditions were classified as rare childhood neurological diseases: motor neuron disease, multiple sclerosis, neuroblastoma and other peripheral nervous cell tumors, and other neurological disorders. From 1990 to 2021, the global age-standardized prevalence and disability-adjusted life-year rates of rare childhood neurological diseases increased, with higher burdens among boys and in low-middle sociodemographic index countries. Our customized forecasting model projected that 110.2 thousand children would be affected by 2050, representing an 11.83% increase from 2021. Annual and cumulative increases in newly reported disease-causing genes and pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants associated with monogenic neurological diseases were observed from 1990 to 2024. The increasing and disparate burden of rare childhood neurological diseases highlights the need for targeted prevention.

title: Enabling climate action: A nexus approach for delivering co-benefits across biodiversity, water, food, and health
abstract: Climate response options rarely affect biodiversity, water, food, and health in uniform ways. This comparative analysis examines why technically viable response options generate uneven cross-nexus outcomes, and how governance and justice conditions shape whether these outcomes become durable co-benefits. Anchored in the IPBES Nexus Assessment, the analysis synthesizes evidence from fifteen response options spanning land, ocean, energy, urban, industrial, and societal transitions. Ecosystem-centered and demand-side pathways more consistently produce synergies because they work through ecological functions that connect several nexus elements. Infrastructure- and technology-centered options deliver mitigation and health gains, but their wider effects are more context-dependent and often shaped by land use, water demand, biodiversity risk, tenure, access, and benefit-sharing. These patterns do not arise from technical design alone. By integrating nexus governance with Earth System Justice, the analysis indicates how cross-sectoral coordination, distributive equity, procedural inclusion, accountable finance, and knowledge pluralism can shape legitimacy and durability. Climate action is more likely to deliver sustained system-wide benefits when institutions align ecological interdependencies with social rights and responsibilities. Otherwise, promising interventions may remain partial, contested or short-lived.

title: Sulfate modification CeO2: A strategy for SF6 photocatalytic degradation
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF 6 ) is extensively employed in high-voltage electrical equipment due to its exceptional dielectric properties, yet its potent greenhouse effect and extreme chemical inertness demand efficient abatement strategies. This study presents sulfate-modified ceria (CeO 2 ) photocatalysts designed to activate robust S–F bonds through surface Brønsted acid sites. Sulfate groups anchored on CeO 2 polarize SF 6 molecules and facilitate photogenerated electron injection into antibonding orbitals, enabling reductive bond cleavage under mild conditions. The optimized 0.5SCe catalyst achieves an SF 6 degradation amount of 7.41 mL g −1 within 24 h under 365 nm LED irradiation, representing a 10.4-fold enhancement over pristine CeO 2 . The catalyst maintains stable performance across consecutive cycles and 96 h of continuous operation. This surface acidity engineering strategy offers a sustainable pathway for controlling fluorinated greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Caloric restriction attenuates NLRP3 inflammasome activation and oxidative stress in leukocytes of patients with obesity
abstract: Obesity promotes chronic low-grade inflammation through metabolic stress and activation of the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome. The effects of caloric restriction on this pathway in humans are poorly understood; therefore, we evaluated the impact of a 6-month hypocaloric dietary intervention in 45 adults with obesity by assessing the metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, and inflammasome-related markers in peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Weight loss improved metabolic parameters, reduced oxidative stress, and decreased the expression of nuclear factor κB (NF-κB), NLRP3, apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD (ASC), and pro-caspase-1, while there tended to be a reduction of active caspase-1. These changes were accompanied by lower circulating interleukin (IL)-1β (IL-1β) and IL-18 levels, suggesting systemic attenuation of inflammasome activity. Baseline adiposity and insulin resistance influenced the magnitude of the response to dietary intervention. These findings support caloric restriction as a strategy to mitigate obesity-associated immunometabolic dysfunction and identify the redox-inflammasome axis as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Targeting host ferroptosis in cancer cachexia: Tumor-immune triggers, tissue wasting, and the therapeutic paradox
abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic wasting syndrome driven by tumor burden, chronic inflammation, disrupted nutrient handling, and neuroendocrine stress. Supportive nutrition, exercise, and symptom management rarely restore lean mass, function, or treatment tolerance once wasting is established. Ferroptosis, iron-dependent cell death caused by phospholipid peroxidation, may connect inflammatory iron redistribution, lipid remodeling, mitochondrial stress, and impaired antioxidant defenses. This review critically evaluates ferroptosis in cachexia from a tumor-host pharmacology perspective, distinguishing causal evidence from associated oxidative signatures. We highlight two experimentally supported mechanisms: neutrophil-derived lipocalin-2 in lung cancer cachexia and tumor exosomal miR-203a-3p in pancreatic cancer-associated muscle wasting. We also examine the paradox that tumor ferroptosis induction may weaken host-tissue resistance and worsen muscle and adipose loss. We propose a "split-ferroptosis" strategy combining tumor sensitization with host-protective iron modulation, lipid peroxide scavenging, endogenous defense reinforcement, and biomarker-guided patient selection to expand the tumor-host therapeutic index.

title: Lipid-based mRNA chimeric antigen receptor T cells for enhanced in vitro antitumor activity
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy provides substantial clinical benefits in hematologic malignancies. However, cell engineering using conventional viral vectors is costly, labor intensive, and prone to safety risks, while electroporation-induced cellular damage limits manufacturing scalability. This study reports a safe, high-efficiency, nonviral platform for generating mRNA-engineered CAR T cells. Herein, eight ionizable lipids are synthesized and formulated into lipid nanoparticles. Systematic screening and structural optimization identified lipid 6 as the lead candidate. Transfection efficiency is validated by delivering enhanced green fluorescent protein ( eGFP ) mRNA into DC2.4, peripheral blood mononuclear, dendritic, and natural killer cells. Murine models confirm robust in vivo expression and a favorable safety profile. Lipid 6-mediated delivery of MUC1 mRNA generates MUC1 -CAR T cells characterized by high surface receptor expression and potent cytotoxicity against MUC1-positive tumor cells. These findings establish lipid 6 as a feasible strategy for primary human T cell engineering, facilitating functional CAR expression with minimal toxicity.

title: Sulfonylurea receptor 1 deficiency alleviates acute lung injury by activating PARP1 in epithelial cells
abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a critical disease with high mortality, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. In this study, we investigated sulfonylurea receptor 1 (SUR1), the regulatory subunit of ATP-sensitive potassium (K ATP ) channels, in the progression of ALI. We observed elevated SUR1 protein levels in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) of patients with sepsis-associated ALI, as well as in BALF and lung tissues of ALI mouse models. Genetic deletion of SUR1, but not Kir6.2 (the pore-forming subunit of K ATP channels), significantly alleviated ALI induced by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) or by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) intratracheal instillation. Mechanistically, SUR1 interacted with poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1), impairing DNA damage repair and promoting apoptosis and NF-κB (nuclear factor kappa B) activation in bronchial epithelial cells. Notably, glibenclamide, a clinically approved SUR1 inhibitor, significantly alleviated ALI, at least in part, by disrupting the SUR1-PARP1 interaction. Our findings identify SUR1 as a new therapeutic target and highlight the potential repurposing of glibenclamide as a therapeutic drug in ALI.

title: Recent advances in medical hemostatic materials: Mechanisms, evaluation, and clinical perspectives
abstract: Uncontrolled hemorrhage remains a major cause of preventable death in trauma and surgery, yet the performance of hemostatic materials varies markedly with wound geometry, blood flow, coagulation status, and tissue sensitivity. This review critically examines natural polymer-based, synthetic polymer-based, inorganic, and composite hemostats by linking material structure to six principal mechanisms: fluid absorption and surface adsorption, coagulation activation, bioactive-factor delivery, photothermal assistance, adhesive sealing, and microstructural regulation. Beyond cataloging materials, we compare class-specific advantages, failure modes, and safety constraints, and analyze how hemodilution, hypothermia, acidosis, anticoagulation, infection, and high-flow bleeding reshape material performance. We further integrate clinically used products, scenario-based material selection, and a staged evaluation framework spanning mechanistic assays, hostile-condition testing, translational bleeding models, rebleeding assessment, and post-hemostasis safety. Finally, we outline stage-matched pathways for responsive and multifunctional systems. This mechanism-scenario-evaluation framework supports more rigorous design, comparison, and clinical translation of next-generation hemostatic materials.

title: Deep white-matter tracts link docosahexaenoic acid status to cognitive performance in human adolescents
abstract: Abstract Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) is a polyunsaturated fatty acid enriched in neuronal membranes and myelin and associated with cognitive performance. However, nutritional interventions show inconsistent cognitive effects, partly due to limited knowledge of the neural pathways linking DHA status to human cognition during sensitive periods of white-matter maturation, such as adolescence. We addressed this gap by studying 99 adolescents drawn from both extremes of performance on a national scholastic examination. Participants completed assessments of scholastic achievement (SA) and intellectual ability (IA), provided erythrocyte DHA samples, and underwent multimodal MRI, including diffusion, T1-weighted, and T2-weighted imaging. Independent component analysis and Bayesian multivariate LASSO models identified brain components jointly associated with DHA and cognition. Across four MRI modalities, a single deep white-matter component consistently emerged as the strongest shared pathway linking DHA with cognition. Tract-resolved analyses highlighted predominant contributions from the fornix and thalamus–temporal fasciculus, with additional subcortical and cortical involvement. In joint models, these components predicted SA and IA after accounting for DHA and other fatty acids, consistent with an indirect, mediation-like pathway. These findings move beyond DHA–behavior correlations by identifying specific neuroanatomical pathways through which a modifiable dietary factor relates to adolescent learning and intellectual performance, offering mechanistic insight relevant to neuroscience, nutrition, and education. Significance Statement Adolescence is a sensitive period for the maturation of white-matter pathways that support learning and reasoning. Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), an essential dietary fatty acid enriched in neuronal membranes and myelin, has been linked to cognitive performance, yet the neural mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. Using multimodal MRI and Bayesian multivariate modeling in adolescents with high or low scholastic performance, identify a specific deep white-matter pathway—centered on the fornix and the thalamus–temporal fasciculus—as the principal route connecting DHA status with scholastic achievement and intellectual ability. Additional subcortical and cortical contributions reveal a coordinated system-level architecture. These findings move beyond correlations by providing mechanistic insight into how a modifiable nutritional factor relates to cognitive development, with implications for neuroscience, public health, and education.

title: IPO5 contributes to cetuximab resistance in colorectal cancer by modulating Ras signaling
abstract: Resistance to cetuximab is a major challenge in colorectal cancer (CRC). Here, we show that IPO5, an importin mediating RASAL2 nuclear import, contributes to cetuximab resistance. Screening six CRC cell lines revealed an inverse correlation between IPO5 expression and cetuximab sensitivity, with higher IPO5 levels in resistant (RKO and SW620) than sensitive (LoVo and Caco2) cells. IPO5 knockdown in resistant cells restored cetuximab sensitivity, induced apoptosis (upregulated active caspase-3/BAX and downregulated BCL-2), and suppressed proliferation and xenograft growth, whereas IPO5 overexpression in sensitive cells reduced sensitivity. Mechanistically, IPO5 facilitates RASAL2 nuclear translocation via its nuclear localization signal, depleting cytoplasmic RASAL2 and increasing GTP-bound RAS to sustain AKT and MAPK activation. Consistently, IPO5 and downstream Ras effectors were elevated in resistant LoVo-CR cells. Collectively, our findings identify the IPO5/RASAL2 axis as a key contributor to cetuximab resistance in CRC by disrupting the cytoplasmic localization of RASAL2 and activating the RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways.

title: A common germline 3′ UTR variant controls DDIT4 translation efficiency and stress responses in cancer cells
abstract: Abstract Relatively few studies have examined the link between SNPs and mRNA translation, despite the established importance of translational regulation in shaping cell phenotypes. We developed a pipeline analyzing the allelic imbalance in total and polysome-bound mRNAs from paired RNA-seq data of HCT116 cells and identified 40 candidate tranSNPs, i.e. SNPs associated with allele-specific translation. Among them, the SNP rs1053639 (T/A) on DNA damage-inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) 3’UTR was identified, with the reference T allele showing a higher polysome association. rs1053639 TT clones generated by genome editing exhibited significantly higher DDIT4 protein levels than AA ones. The difference in DDIT4 proteins was even greater when cells were treated with Thapsigargin or Nutlin, two perturbations that induce DDIT4 transcription. The RNA-binding protein RBMX influenced these allele-dependent differences in DDIT4 protein expression, as shown by RNA-EMSA, RIP, and smiFISH assays. RBMX depletion reduced DDIT4 protein in TT clones to the AA levels. Functionally, TT clones more effectively repressed mTORC1 under ER stress, while AA clones outcompeted TT clones in vitro or when injected in zebrafish embryos. RBMX depletion increased the fitness of TT cells in co-culture experiments. The rs1053639 AA genotype, under a recessive model, correlates with poor prognosis in TCGA cancer data. Key points - Translatome analysis in HCT116 cells revealed allele-specific mRNA translation for 40 SNPs - rs1053639 (T/A) in DDIT4 3’UTR showed allelic differences in mRNA localization & protein expression - AA cells showed weaker mTOR inhibition & higher proliferation; AA individuals had poorer prognosis

title: Corrigendum to “Weak interface strong skeleton shrinkage resistant mix design for large cement stabilized base” [iScience 29 (2026) 117347]
abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.isci.2026.117347.].

title: Microbiota-constrained bacterial density limits phage infection in the gut and allows persistence of susceptible cells
abstract: With the rise of antibiotic resistance, bacteriophage-based treatments against bacterial infections have regained momentum. However, phage therapy has so far shown only moderate success in complex environments like the mammalian gut, where phages are particularly promising tools for microbiome engineering and specific elimination of opportunistic pathogens. Here, we use different murine models of intestinal colonization to quantitatively assess the minimal population size of susceptible Escherichia coli cells that is required for phage replication in the gut (replication threshold). We found that the composition of the intestinal microbiota is a key factor shaping phage–bacteria interactions by restricting the carrying capacity of susceptible host cells. We further demonstrate that the replication threshold enables coexistence of susceptible and resistant bacteria in phage-treated mice, with implications for phage-based applications in complex environments like the gut.

title: Where to improve the European protected areas network to represent threatened fungi?
abstract: To set a global example in biodiversity conservation, the European Union aims to protect 30% and strictly protect 10% of its land by 2030 and to invest in ecosystem restoration. Yet, the megadiverse fungal kingdom remains largely excluded from conservation planning and evaluation. We compiled occurrence data and developed species distribution models for 33 threatened macrofungi identified for potential inclusion under the Bern Convention across Europe. Comparing distributions of predicted habitats with existing protected-area networks provided robust evidence of large, uneven protection gaps among species and countries. We show that regionally coordinated improvements in protection and targeted habitat restoration would be more effective than addressing gaps independently within each country. By developing habitat models into tools for conservation management, spatial planning and monitoring, and by explicitly allocating those efforts across Member States, protection of neglected but threatened and functionally important taxa such as fungi can be systematically improved.

title: Gastroprotective effects of chlorella derived lutein via anti-inflammatory antioxidant and acid enzyme modulation
abstract: Induction of gastric ulcer by ethanol is associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired gastric mucosal defense. The current work was performed to determine the effect of lutein from Chlorella on ethanol-induced gastric ulcers in rats. Lutein caused significant decrease in gastric ulcer index and ulcer area (by 80.8%) and had beneficial effects on hematological and inflammatory status as seen from the 38% reduction in neutrophil, 57% reduction in myeloperoxidase activity, and 83% reduction in neutrophilic infiltration. At a dose of 200 mg/kg, lutein significantly lowered cyclooxygenase activity (50%), C-reactive protein (67%), prostaglandin E2 (55%), and nitric oxide (39%) levels. Lutein caused decrease in oxidative stress evidenced from 75% to 69% reduction in TBARS and hydrogen peroxide, and increase in the activities of superoxide dismutase, catalase, and glutathione peroxidase. Lutein exhibited dose-dependent inhibition of gastric H + K + ATPase activity and preservation of gastric mucosal integrity.

title: Similar aggregate but divergent disaggregate responses in human and AI under sequential reward-penalty incentives
abstract: With the rapid advancement of general-purpose AI, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to simulate human decisions in structured environments. However, whether similarity in aggregate human and LLM responses extends to behavior under sequential reward-penalty incentives remains unclear. We address this question by introducing an established carbon mechanism to a repeated e-commerce delivery task and comparing decision responses between human, DeepSeek-v.3.2, and Qwen3-Max participants, wherein standard and slow delivery options are provided. In baseline settings, all participants predominantly select the theoretically dominant option. Under sequential reward-penalty incentives, all participant types shift toward slow delivery and exhibit comparably large aggregate changes. However, this aggregate-level similarity does not extend to "value of time" (VOT)-stratified response patterns and longitudinal trajectories. Humans exhibit gradual and incomplete adjustment, whereas LLMs display model-specific responses, including more stable or variable adjustment patterns depending on the model configuration. Thus, similar aggregate responses can coexist with divergent disaggregate behavioral patterns.

title: An inverse-protein-folding pre-trained model for predicting the mutational effects in protein-protein interactions
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are fundamental to vast biological processes. Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in PPIs is crucial for protein engineering and drug discovery. Most existing PPI prediction approaches rely on refined physicochemical features or computationally intensive structural sampling. Here, we present delta-G message-passing-neural-network (DGMPNN), a message-passing neural-network framework for predicting the effects of mutations on PPIs. DGMPNN is pre-trained on an inverse protein folding (IPF) task and employs an adaptive residue-level attention pooling mechanism to enable effective transfer learning for predicting mutation-induced changes in protein binding affinity. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmark datasets and deep mutational scanning (DMS) datasets. Experimental validation using computationally selected multi-site variants of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-hACE2 complex showed strong agreement between predicted and experimentally measured binding affinities.

title: An integrated framework for agroclimatic, salinity, and groundwater assessment in the Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan
abstract: Climate change, salinization, and water scarcity increasingly threaten irrigated agricultural landscapes in arid regions. This study developed an integrated framework combining hydro-climatic, soil, and groundwater indicators to assess agricultural landscapes in the Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan. The framework integrated fourteen agroclimatic, soil-quality, and groundwater indicators into a unified scoring system. Results revealed persistent agroclimatic constraints during 2021–2024, with vegetation-period vapor pressure deficit (VPD) ranging from 1.91–1.37 kPa and hydrothermal coefficient (HTC) from 0.40–1.09, indicating high atmospheric water demand and semi-arid conditions. Groundwater mineralization remained predominantly within 1–3 g L −1 , while salinity risks persisted in the areas affected by shallow groundwater and elevated mineralization. Integrated assessment scores ranged from 11 to 16 points, classifying most districts as unsatisfactory in 2021 and satisfactory during 2022–2024. Zafarabad and, occasionally, Sh. Rashidov exhibited the lowest overall scores. The framework provides a practical tool for monitoring landscape vulnerability and supporting irrigation, reclamation, and salinity-management decisions.

title: Revolutionizing drought defense: The water-plant-microbe synergy in climate-smart agriculture
abstract: Global warming-induced water scarcity threatens agricultural sustainability. While precision irrigation and microbial inoculants are recognized as effective individual strategies, their synergistic potential remains under-explored. This review synthesizes recent advances in the "water-plant-microbe" synergy to propose a bidirectional regulatory mechanism for climate-smart agriculture. We demonstrate that irrigation regimes function as a primary filter for rhizosphere microbial assembly, thereby defining the hydraulic niche for colonization. Conversely, functional microbes actively engineer the soil environment via exopolysaccharide production and hormonal modulation, thereby enhancing plant hydraulic status and water use efficiency (WUE). In contrast to previous reviews focusing on single factors, this review constructs an integrated framework linking soil hydrology with microbial ecology, supported by emerging comparative evidence. We conclude that future agricultural water management must shift from solely regulating water supply to managing the holobiont's hydrological interactions, offering a promising systems-level strategy to safeguard food security under climate stress.

title: Comparative efficacy of exercise modalities for mild cognitive impairment in older adults: A network meta-analysis
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represents a critical window for dementia prevention, yet the comparative efficacy of diverse exercise modalities remains unclear. We conducted a frequentist network meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials to identify the optimal exercise intervention for improving global cognition in older adults with MCI. Combined physical-cognitive training ranked first with a 68.0% probability of being the most effective intervention, followed by Tai Chi (15.9%), while single-mode exercises and control groups showed substantially lower benefits. Interventions requiring simultaneous physical exertion and neural engagement confer superior cognitive benefits. This evidence supports tailored dual-component exercise regimens as a robust non-pharmacological strategy to mitigate cognitive decline in aging populations.

title: Harnessing hydrogel technology for advanced periodontitis therapy: A multifunctional approach to oral health restoration
abstract: Periodontitis is a bacterially driven inflammatory disease that can lead to tooth mobility and tooth loss. Conventional non-surgical therapy, antibiotics, and surgery may be limited by residual subgingival biofilms, antimicrobial resistance, and variable clinical outcomes. This review synthesizes recent studies of hydrogel-based systems for local periodontal therapy, focusing on stimuli-responsive release mechanisms, cargo-loading approaches, and regenerative outcomes in relevant animal models. Across these studies, hydrogels function as localized delivery matrices that can prolong retention at periodontal defects, regulate therapeutic exposure, and support tissue repair. We further evaluate translational considerations, including degradation behavior, long-term in vivo stability, and immunocompatibility. These findings position hydrogels as adaptable platforms for more precise periodontitis management and identify priorities for preclinical optimization before clinical translation.

title: Pediatric RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection burden in G20 countries in 2023
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of childhood lower respiratory infections, but updated G20 burden estimates are lacking. Using the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database, we analyzed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for RSV-associated lower respiratory infections in children aged 0-14 years across G20 members from 1990 to 2023, with stratification by sex, age, and country. In 2023, an estimated 5,373 deaths and 483,162 DALYs occurred, with mortality and DALY rates having declined by ∼5.5% annually since 1990. The COVID-19 pandemic drove burden to a historic low in 2021, but a marked rebound followed in 2022-2023, though rates remained below pre-pandemic levels. Infants aged <1 year bore the heaviest burden (mortality 8.688 per 100,000), and India ranked highest, whereas Australia ranked lowest. Burden strongly correlated inversely with Sociodemographic Index. These findings highlight the need for precision prevention, targeting the youngest children and lower-resource G20 members.

title: PFKFB3 inhibition dictates the adaptive responses and cell fates in tumor cells
abstract: 6-Phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase 3 (PFKFB3), a key regulator of glycolysis highly expressed in many tumor cells, has a critical role in promoting glycolysis and tumor progression. Consequently, anti-cancer strategies have sought to inhibit PFKFB3 to exploit this metabolic dependency of tumor cells. In this study, we employed a controlled protein degradation system to manipulate the kinetics of PFKFB3 depletion in investigating its impact on tumor cell growth. We show that, while slow depletion allows metabolic adaptation with a minimal effect on proliferation, rapid depletion or acute inhibition suppresses cell growth despite a similar glycolytic reduction. We show that rapid PFKFB3 loss activates AMPK, which perturbs cell cycle progression through the MAPK/ERK pathway. Importantly, AMPK inhibition was sufficient to rescue the adaptation failure caused by rapid PFKFB3 depletion. Together, our findings document that dynamic targeting of PFKFB3 can drive heterogeneous cancer cell fates, shedding light on cells' potential path toward developing resistance to anti-PFKFB3 treatments.

title: Earth-observation variables identify temperature-centered protein-family covariation across macroalgal genomes
abstract: Macroalgal genome-environment associations are difficult to separate from lineage, geography, and uneven genome quality. We describe nine Arabian Gulf genomes and analyze them with 117 published genomes (126 total). We tested protein family (Pfam) profiles against 13 Google Earth Engine variables. Of 87,123 tests, 84 met global Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.05, and 49 pairs across 30 Pfams retained selected-family q < 0.05 with discovery-consistent direction in all seven post hoc specifications; all 13 pairs meeting global Bonferroni p < 0.05 were retained. The 49 pairs comprised 43 sea surface temperature, five depth, and one distance-to-coast association. PF16087 was positively associated with five temperature summaries, whereas PF12094 and PF01638 were negatively associated with four. A secondary same-site AlphaEarth Foundations crosswalk aligned latent axes A52 and A53 oppositely with five temperature summaries. Together, these analyses place temperature at the center of protein-family covariation in this cohort.

title: Speed-driven transitions between discrete and rhythmic dynamics in walking revealed by kinematic smoothness and muscle synergies
abstract: Humans control movement through motor primitives that generate discrete and rhythmic actions. We investigated whether and how speed may drive a transition between discrete and rhythmic organization in walking, and whether muscle synergy changes are associated with kinematic shifts. Eighteen healthy adults walked on a treadmill during incremental and decremental trials (0.5-5 km/h in 0.5 km/h steps). Kinematics and bilateral lower-limb EMG were recorded. Smoothness was quantified using log dimensionless jerk (LDJ) and spectral arc length (SPARC). Both metrics indicated lower smoothness at low speeds and progressively stabilized as speed increased, with a transition region around 3-3.5 km/h showing inter-individual variability. In parallel, EMG synergies showed speed-dependent increases in dimensionality (2→3→4), consistent with module merging at slower speeds. Overall, these findings reveal coordinated kinematic and neuromuscular shifts with speed, indicating a transition from a discrete-dominated regime at low speeds toward a more stable rhythmic pattern at higher speeds.

title: Plasma proteomic analysis identified potential therapeutic targets for pulmonary arterial hypertension
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains a progressive disease with high mortality. By integrating the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (49,272 participants, 337 incident cases) with drug-target Mendelian randomization, we identified 398 plasma proteins associated with incident PAH and 19 with potential causal relevance, 15 of which are druggable. Then we prioritized 5 candidates for expression validation in the Sugen5416 and hypoxia rat model and confirmed significant upregulation of TNFRSF10A and downregulation of UMOD in lung tissue, consistent with human plasma proteomic trends. Subsequent in vitro functional assays demonstrated that UMOD treatment attenuates PAH-related cellular phenotypes, whereas TNFRSF10A knockdown exacerbates pro-pathogenic progression. These results suggest UMOD as a promising protective therapeutic candidate and indicate the inherent complexity of the TNFRSF10A signaling. This integrative study provides a robust framework for translational research, future studies are warranted to elucidate downstream molecular mechanisms and further evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of these candidates.

title: Loss of the Asn333 high-mannose N-glycan impairs ACP3 folding and drives disease-associated dysfunction
abstract: Missense mutations disrupting N -glycosylation motifs can perturb protein folding and trafficking, yet the site-specific contributions of individual N -glycans to proteostasis remain poorly defined. Here, we delineated the functional hierarchy of three N -glycosylation sites in human prostatic acid phosphatase (ACP3). Glycoproteomic analysis showed that Asn94 and Asn220 carry predominantly complex-type N -glycans, whereas Asn333 is enriched in high-mannose structures. Glycan-deficient N94Q and N220Q variants were efficiently secreted and retained phosphatase activity, whereas N333Q and T335M accumulated intracellularly, formed endoplasmic reticulum aggregates, and lacked enzymatic activity. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the Asn333 high-mannose glycan forms persistent hydrogen-bond networks with surrounding residues and exhibits markedly reduced conformational flexibility, supporting a non-redundant structural role. Individuals harboring a heterozygous p.T335M variant presented severe neurodevelopmental abnormalities, linking Asn333 glycan loss to proteostasis failure in vivo . These findings establish a site-specific glycan-protein stabilizing mechanism with broad implications in glycoprotein folding and human disease.

title: Extensive monolayer formation after transplantation depends on an RPE subpopulation derived from human iPSCs
abstract: Loss of retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) in the eye leads to photoreceptor dysfunction, death, and eventually, vision loss. Cell replacement strategies using RPE cells derived in vitro from pluripotent stem cells are currently evaluated as a potential therapeutic strategy. Generation of polarized monolayers represents an essential prerequisite for proper RPE function; however, monolayer formation following transplantation of RPE suspensions has not been systematically assessed. Using the sodium iodate mouse model of acute RPE depletion, significant increase in monolayer formation capacity of passage 1 vs. 2 human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived RPE cells was observed three weeks post-transplantation. Transplant-derived monolayers showed characteristic apicobasal polarity, RPE marker expression, phagocytosis function, and preservation of the host outer nuclear layer. The cell surface marker panel CD54+/PSA-NCAM − was identified to enrich for an RPE subpopulation with a high potential for monolayer formation following transplantation. Results underline the importance of defining and isolating competent cell subpopulations for successful RPE transplantation.

title: Alternative splicing of a species- and skeletal muscle-specific microexon diversifies the menu of clathrin heavy chains in mice and rats
abstract: Little is known about alternative splicing of microexons in most tissues other than the brain. Humans have two homologous clathrin heavy chains. Ubiquitously expressed, CLTC drives clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Highly expressed in skeletal muscles, CLTCL1 instead regulates glucose metabolism. Previously, we reported that a conserved microexon (exon 31) in the CLTC gene is alternatively spliced during striated muscle development. Here, we identified a novel Cltc microexon (exon 33, hereafter microexon 33), which is only included in mouse and rat adult skeletal muscles. Microexon 33 inclusion shortens the CLTC C-terminus and adds 10 distinct terminal residues. This divergence occurs at the same position at which the human CLTCL1 constitutively includes its penultimate exon (another microexon). CLTCL1 is a pseudogene in mice and rats. Humans diversified the menu of clathrin heavy chains by gene duplication and tissue-specific gene expression, whereas mice and rats might have achieved similar diversification by tissue-specific regulation of Cltc alternative splicing.

title: Volume electron microscopy reveals oligodendrocyte axon selection patterns and spatial assembly of myelin and nodes
abstract: Oligodendrocytes myelinate multiple axons, requiring single cells to coordinate target selection, sheath growth, and node formation across complex cortical geometry. We combined serial block-face electron microscopy, complete segmentation, and three-dimensional reconstruction to analyze early-myelinating oligodendrocytes in the somatosensory cortex of a postnatal day 14 rat at single-cell and nanoscale resolution. Individual oligodendrocytes initiated myelination across all contacted axons, while early ensheathment decreased with increasing process distance from the soma. Each oligodendrocyte also contacted axons within a restricted caliber range, independently of wrapping progression. At prospective nodes of Ranvier, transient cytoplasmic projections extended into axonal domains from adjacent oligodendrocytes and converged near presumptive paranodes. These observations support a structural model in which oligodendrocyte geometry, cell-specific axon selection, and intercellular interactions jointly organize early cortical myelination and nodal assembly, providing testable hypotheses for developmental myelination and repair after demyelination.

title: How far are vision-free medical robots from achieving trustworthy embodied intelligence?
abstract: Embodied Intelligence (EI) is rapidly reshaping the field of robotic surgery, enabling unprecedented levels of clinical precision while liberating surgeons from excessive cognitive and physical burdens. However, for "vision-free" surgical robots incapable of integrating direct visual sensing-such as endovascular robots and untethered swarms-their persistent reliance on external medical imaging fundamentally impedes their evolution toward safe and trustworthy EI-surgery.

title: Lactate as a predictive biomarker and therapeutic target in cardiopulmonary bypass-associated acute kidney injury
abstract: Elevated lactate is a common metabolic perturbation following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). This study evaluates the clinical predictive value of lactate and explores its mechanism involving protein lactylation. Machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to multicenter intensive care databases identified preoperative lactate as a dominant predictor of CPB-acute kidney injury (AKI) risk. To validate these predictions biologically, rat CPB and cellular models were utilized. Experimental results demonstrated that CPB induces glycolytic reprogramming, lactate accumulation, and elevated pan-lysine lactylation. Inhibiting the production of lactate was associated with decreased protein lactylation, lower oxidative stress, and reduced local tissue inflammation, thereby mitigating renal injury. Collectively, our interpretable ML predictive models identify lactate as a top clinical predictor of CPB-AKI, while our experimental data establish the lactate-lactylation axis as a potential mechanistic pathway linking metabolic dysfunction to renal damage. This axis represents a candidate therapeutic target requiring further validation.

title: Patch-seq analysis reveals transcriptomic correlates of neuronal firing rate adaptation across subtypes and species
abstract: Can the transcriptomic profile of a neuron predict its physiological properties? Using a Patch-seq dataset of the primary visual cortex, we addressed this question by focusing on spike rate adaptation (SRA), a well-known phenomenon that depends on small conductance calcium (Ca)-dependent potassium (SK) channels. We first show that in parvalbumin-expressing (PV) and somatostatin-expressing (SST) interneurons, expression levels of genes encoding the ion channels underlying action potential generation are correlated with the half-width (HW) of spikes. Surprisingly, the SK encoding genes are not correlated with the degree of SRA (dAdap). Instead, genes that encode proteins upstream from the SK current, as well as the low-voltage-activated calcium channel, are correlated with dAdap. This general principle is supported by datasets from the mouse primary motor cortex and multiple macaque brain regions. Finally, we generate testable predictions by constructing a minimal computational model.

title: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation boosts evidence accumulation during perceptual decision making
abstract: Ascending arousal systems, including the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine (LC-NE) system, may shape perceptual decision-making by enhancing sensory processing ("gain") or accelerating response commitment ("urgency"). We examined how arousal-related neuromodulatory activity shapes decisions and whether its effects depend on arousal state. We tested 62 participants in three groups, receiving transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) at three timings during a random dot motion task. tVNS increased pupil-linked arousal, with early stimulation producing more sustained dilation into decision-making. Behaviorally, tVNS selectively improved accuracy under initially low performance without affecting response times. Drift diffusion modeling linked this improvement to increased drift rate, consistent with more efficient evidence accumulation. These effects occurred across groups but were most pronounced with early stimulation. Our findings support a gain-related enhancement of evidence accumulation under tVNS and suggest that pupil-linked arousal, potentially involving LC-NE among other ascending arousal pathways, may help stabilize attentional engagement when endogenous control is suboptimal.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: Genetic polymorphisms and early responses predict refractory hyperthyroidism during antithyroid drug therapy
abstract: Antithyroid drugs (ATDs) are the first-line treatment for Graves' disease (GD), but variable outcomes require early risk stratification. We analyzed 578 adults, including 240 in a randomized trial of dose titration versus modified partial block-and-replace therapy and the remainder in a temporal observational cohort. Baseline characteristics, 3-month treatment indicators, and 13 GD-susceptibility single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were evaluated. An ATD-levothyroxine dose-correction method quantified thyroid function and autoantibody changes, informing clinical and SNP risk score-integrated models. The integrated model achieved areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.841 in development and 0.805 in temporal validation, outperforming the clinical model ( p < 0.001) with good calibration and net benefit. Intermediate-risk patients derived the greatest incremental benefit. Baseline free thyroxine (FT4) was the strongest predictor, and the SNP risk score ranked fourth. No inter-regimen efficacy or safety differences were observed. Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested that ATD therapy beyond 3 years may reduce recurrence risk, whereas modified partial block-and-replace showed no advantage over dose titration.

title: Central relaxin-3/RXFP3 signaling potently drives orexigenic behaviors and attenuates cisplatin-induced anorexia and body weight loss
abstract: The relaxin-3 neuropeptide system promotes energy balance by increasing feeding behavior. Here, we investigate the behavioral mechanisms mediating the orexigenic effects of relaxin-3 and the therapeutic potential of relaxin-3 to combat metabolic disorders. We show that central and peripheral administration of relaxin-3 increases high-fat diet intake by increasing meal size in obese rats. Furthermore, we deleted relaxin family peptide receptor 3 (RXFP3) neuronally using RXFP3 fl/fl hSyn-Cre+ mice and show that neuronal RXFP3 is required for the orexigenic effects of relaxin-3. In addition, central relaxin-3 administration augmented food motivation for sucrose and hyperphagia in a binge-like eating model. We then evaluated the potential of relaxin-3 to drive food intake in rats receiving acute maladaptive chemotherapy. Pretreatment of central relaxin-3 attenuated cisplatin chemotherapy-induced anorexia and body weight loss. These findings characterize the behavioral mechanisms by which the relaxin-3 system drives feeding behaviors and highlight its therapeutic potential for metabolic wasting disorders.

title: OGT regulates RNA-binding protein nucleocytoplasmic partitioning, but this fails in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
abstract: O-linked N-acetylglucosamine transferase (OGT) catalyzes the O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification to proteins and has been implicated in a range of diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a rapidly progressive and currently incurable neurodegenerative disorder. However, the precise mechanisms by which OGT influences ALS pathogenesis remain largely unresolved. In this study, we used human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived spinal motor neurons (hiPSC-MNs), the principal cell type that undergoes degeneration in ALS, to systematically reveal that OGT-related mechanisms regulate RNA-binding protein (RBP) nucleocytoplasmic compartmentalization. Using a combination of antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) technology and small molecular pharmacology, we reveal two distinct regulatory mechanisms of RBP compartmentalization, including by intron-retaining transcript-mediated sequestration and O-linked N-acetylglucosaminylation (O-GlcNAcylation)-mediated nuclear transport. We finally examine the tractability of manipulating OGT activity in the ALS context but demonstrate that the OGT-related mechanisms governing RBP localization in healthy hiPSC-MNs are impaired in the context of ALS-causing VCP and TARDBP mutations.

title: CD8+ T cell transcriptional reprogramming toward TCF7-low cytotoxicity drives immune aging in viral ARDS
abstract: Viral acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) exhibits distinct clinical outcomes across age groups, but the immune mechanisms underlying this disparity remain unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomic profiling, T cell receptor repertoire analysis, serum proteomics, and functional validation to characterize age-dependent T cell remodeling in influenza-associated ARDS. Adult ARDS was characterized by reduced T cell receptor diversity, expansion of CD8 + effector memory T cells, and enhanced cytotoxic programs marked by increased granzyme B (GZMB) expression compared with pediatric ARDS. At the transcriptional level, adult CD8 + effector memory T cells displayed a TCF7-low state associated with activation of a TGFB1-related RUNX3/PRDM1 program. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that TGFB1 promoted cytotoxic programming in CD8 + effector memory T cells and increased epithelial injury in a co-culture model. These findings identify age-associated CD8 + T cell remodeling as a potential mechanism contributing to immune dysregulation in viral ARDS.

title: CB1 receptor inhibition restores synaptoneurosomal alternative splicing landscape in fragile X syndrome mice
abstract: Abstract Background Fragile X syndrome (FXS) conveys the most frequent heritable genetic cause of intellectual disability and autism. It is caused by a CGG repeat expansion in FMR1 gene that leads to the loss of fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMRP). FMRP is highly abundant in synapses, where regulates mRNAs to maintain synaptic plasticity. Treatments under development significantly ameliorate neurological and behavioral landmarks in the mouse model of the disorder, the Fmr1 knockout (FX) mouse. Specifically, previous studies revealed that pharmacological and genetic inhibition of cannabinoid type-1 receptor (CB1R) restored phenotypic traits in FX mice. However, the molecular hallmarks associated with this experimental therapeutic intervention are largely unknown. Methods First, we aimed to evaluate the validity of synaptoneurosomes preparations to investigate specific mRNA modifications at synapses. Afterwards, combining in silico high-throughput analysis and biochemical determinations, we analyzed the hippocampal synaptoneurosomal transcriptome after pharmacological inhibition of CB1R with the specific antagonist/inverse agonist rimonabant in FX male mice Results We verified that synaptoneurosomes provide an accurate representation of synaptic composition and function. Then, we found that rimonabant treatment had a limited impact at gene expression level but produced significant modifications in transcript expression. Indeed, detailed analysis of alternative splicing events revealed a relevant number of events in which splicing was reverted from the FX form to the WT form by the treatment. Limitations We demonstrated that rimonabant treatment alters the AS landscape in FX hippocampal synaptoneurosomes; however, further studies are needed to elucidate if other neural components also contribute to the modifications and whether the findings are specific to rimonabant treatment or to CB1R inhibition at synapses. In addition, additional research could be required to clarify whether the changes in AS events could be affected by interindividual variability or technical protocols. Conclusions We determined that the AS landscape is modified in FX hippocampal synaptoneurosomes and that these changes are sensitive to rimonabant treatment which could explain the beneficial effects of this experimental therapeutic approach in FXS. Altogether, our results reveal a new level of complexity in the effect of pharmacological treatment to improve symptoms in the context of FXS.

title: Quantifying land transfer in China: Integrating its impacts on urban economy
abstract: In China's hierarchical land-governance system, the central government establishes the regulatory framework, while provincial and municipal authorities adapt the implementation according to local fiscal capacity, development priorities, and spatial constraints. Despite the importance of land transfer in shaping urban economic development processes, empirical research has long relied on fragmented samples or single-scale observations, and a unified long-term dataset spanning multiple administrative levels remains unavailable. To address this gap, this study constructs a multi-level spatiotemporal dataset of land transfer in China covering the period 2000-2024 at the national, provincial, and city levels. The dataset integrates seven standardized indicators, including land supply area, transaction price, gross floor area (GFA), payment amount, floor area ratio (FAR), building density, and greenery rate. Data are compiled from official land-market disclosure platforms and verified administrative transaction records and undergo systematic quality-control procedures, including cross-source reconciliation, unit harmonization, coverage diagnostics, and outlier screening to ensure temporal consistency and spatial comparability. The resulting database supports analyses of long-term land transfer dynamics, regional heterogeneity, and multi-level governance patterns. In addition, an illustrative empirical application demonstrates the analytical utility of the dataset for examining associations between land allocation and urban economic development indicators. This dataset provides a comprehensive empirical foundation for future research on land governance, land finance, urban spatial development, and regional transformation in China.

title: LncRNA Arsa-DT is required for spermatogenesis and male fertility by regulating G2/M progression
abstract: Male infertility is a major reproductive health burden worldwide, yet its molecular etiology remains largely unknown. The testis expresses numerous long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), although their involvement in the pathophysiology of male infertility remains unexplored. Here, we identified Arsa-DT , a testis-predominant divergent lncRNA of Arsa , and demonstrated its essential role in maintaining male fertility. Loss of Arsa-DT leads to subfertility, characterized by reduced sperm production, increased sperm abnormalities, and decreased serum testosterone levels. Notably, Arsa-DT deficiency alters the testosterone-to-estradiol ratio through upregulation of aromatase expression. Specifically expressed in the nuclei of spermatogonia and spermatocytes, Arsa-DT regulates spermatogenesis in the seminiferous tubules. Mechanistically, Arsa-DT regulates G2/M phase progression and chromosome segregation in male germ cells. Collectively, our findings identify Arsa-DT , a testis-predominant lncRNA, as a regulator of spermatogenesis by controlling G2/M phase progression of male germ cells. This study provides mechanistic insights into the pathogenesis of male infertility.

title: Diversity of fatty acid susceptibility among clinical isolates of Staphylococcus aureus and its role in membrane potential
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus colonizes human skin, nasal cavity, and oral mucosa and causes opportunistic infections. Host-derived fatty acids exhibit antibacterial activity against S. aureus , but the diversity and determinants of fatty acid susceptibility among clinical isolates remain unclear. Here, we evaluated seven C14–C18 fatty acids selected from a physiologically relevant range of host-associated lipids. Linoleic acid (LA), palmitoleic acid (POA), and γ-linolenic acid (GLA) demonstrated significant antibacterial activity. We then analyzed LA and POA susceptibility in 253 clinical isolates. LA minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranged widely from 18.75 to 1,200 μM, whereas POA MICs clustered between 37.5 and 150 μM. Low-LA-susceptibility strains showed higher baseline membrane potential-associated signals and weaker LA-induced depolarization. Anaerobic culture and srrA inactivation reduced both of these signals and LA MICs. These findings indicate that membrane potential contributes to the heterogeneity of LA susceptibility and provide insight into host fatty acid-mediated control of S. aureus.

title: Minibeam radiation therapy supports CAR T therapy in a rat model of CNS lymphoma
abstract: Radiotherapy is increasingly combined with CAR T cell therapy in B cell lymphomas, but treatment outcome may depend on the irradiation modality. We evaluated minibeam radiation therapy (MBRT) as a partner for CD19 CAR T cells in an orthotopic primary central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma model in immunodeficient rats. CAR T therapy prolonged survival compared with untreated controls. MBRT at 30 Gy followed by CAR T cells five days later produced the longest median survival among radiotherapy-containing regimens and improved outcome compared with conventional radiotherapy (CRT) based combinations. Histopathological findings were consistent with these survival differences. However, MBRT plus CAR T therapy did not significantly outperform CAR T monotherapy. These results indicate that MBRT provides a favorable, non-antagonistic radiotherapy context for CAR T therapy and suggest that radiation modality should be considered when designing combinations of radiotherapy with adoptive cellular therapies.

title: Comorbidity patterns and sex differences in late-onset Alzheimer’s disease using electronic records
abstract: In this retrospective study, we applied unsupervised learning techniques to electronic medical records from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to characterize Alzheimer's disease (AD) comorbidity patterns. Given the well-known female predominance in AD, we performed sex-stratified analyses to explore differences in comorbidity patterns based on sex. Findings were evaluated using an independent UC-wide dataset. Among 8,363 patients in the UCSF dataset, we observed five data-driven comorbidity clusters related to cardiovascular conditions, gastrointestinal disorders, and frailty-related conditions such as pneumonia and pressure ulcers, as well as groups with higher and lower overall comorbidity burden. Sex-stratified analyses within clusters identified variation in comorbidity patterns, including circulatory diseases in males in cluster 2 and bladder stones in females in cluster 3. Key results demonstrate partial consistency in the UC-wide dataset. Our study provides a structured characterization of comorbidity heterogeneity in AD and highlights sex-related differences, though findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

title: Multi-omics profiling reveals molecular features of visceral adiposity in autonomous cortisol secretion
abstract: Autonomous cortisol secretion (ACS) from adrenal adenomas increases cardiometabolic risk. Visceral adiposity is a hallmark of ACS. We characterized ACS-associated visceral adiposity using multi-omics profiling of periadrenal adipose tissue and plasma. ACS exhibited higher visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio (VSR), adipocyte hypertrophy, and inflammation-related pathway enrichment than non-functioning adrenal tumors. RNA-seq deconvolution and immunohistochemistry indicated increased macrophage infiltration. Plasma steroid metabolomics identified 11-deoxycorticosterone (11-DOC), a mineralocorticoid metabolite, as positively associated with VSR in premenopausal ACS women independent of cortisol. The 11-DOC-associated gene module correlated with inflammation-related pathways, notably macrophage activation. Lipidomics identified ceramides as ACS discriminators, with Cer(d18:1/16:0) most strongly associated with inflammation- and lipid metabolism-related pathways. Mendelian randomization showed genetically predicted plasma Cer(d18:1/16:0) was positively associated with trunk fat mass. These findings identify circulating 11-DOC and adipose ceramide accumulation as molecular features associated with adipose inflammation and visceral adiposity in ACS, providing hypothesis-generating insights that require functional validation.

title: Probing the role of left inferior frontal gyrus in vocal motor control: Evidence from TMS and causal inference analysis
abstract: Beyond an established role in speech initiation and planning, the left inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) may contribute to sensorimotor control of speech production. We applied continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) over the anterior (aIFG) and posterior (pIFG) regions to investigate their roles in vocal motor control. A causal inference analysis (CIA) framework was developed to characterize source-space network organization. cTBS over both left aIFG and pIFG reduced vocal responses and enhanced P2 responses to pitch feedback perturbations, with no significant differences between two active stimulations. However, global dissimilarity analysis revealed greater P2-related topographic deviation from sham stimulation following aIFG stimulation than following pIFG stimulation. CIA further identified different source-space network patterns associated with aIFG and pIFG stimulation. These findings demonstrate the causal involvement of the left IFG in auditory-vocal integration and highlight the potential of CIA for characterizing distributed network organization underlying vocal motor control.

title: Development of a predictive model and nomogram using CTPA parameters for the identification of group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension
abstract: This study aimed to identify computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA)-derived predictors of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and to develop a prediction model and nomogram for non-invasive diagnosis. We retrospectively analyzed CTPA datasets from 203 patients in the training cohort and 98 patients in the validation cohort, stratified into PAH (confirmed by right heart catheterization) and non-PAH groups. Pulmonary vascular and cardiac structural metrics were measured. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and logistic regression identified interventricular septal angle (IVSA), interventricular septal thickness (IVST), and right ventricular outflow tract wall thickness (RVOTW) as independent predictors. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.964 and 0.969 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively, with excellent calibration and clinical utility. The CTPA-based predictive model and nomogram may serve as a useful reference tool, potentially assisting in the identification of PAH and optimizing clinical workflows.

title: Repeated visual adaptation induces persistent behavioral and neural biases in body size perception
abstract: Body size and shape misperception, notably body size overestimation, is prevalent among young people. It has been proposed that such a bias may stem from adaptation aftereffects caused by exposures to distorted bodies, yet whether adaptation can persistently alter daily body perception remains unclear. This study explored the long-term impacts of body size adaptation by having participants repeatedly view thin or large body images for 7 daily sessions, or comparing participants with varied experiences of exposure to the thin-ideal in life. Behavioral results revealed that repeated exposure to distorted body images persistently shifted participants' perception of body normality toward the adapting shape. ERP data showed that repeated adaptation to thin bodies or higher endorsement of the thin-ideal could enhance the early brain response bias to enlarged bodies. These findings collectively suggest that repeated exposure to distorted bodies contribute to the development of perceptual and neural response bias toward body shapes.

title: Reconstructing the genetic ancestry of the archaeological site in Amiternum: From Roman Imperial to early medieval times in Central Italy
abstract: Central-southern Italy is pivotal for reconstructing the population history of the peninsula, yet the genetic impact of the complex demographic past in the Abruzzo region remains largely unexplored. This study integrates archaeological context with ancient DNA analysis of 16 individuals excavated at the Cathedral of Santa Maria in Civitate in Amiternum. The sample comprises one adult male from the Roman Imperial period and 15 subadults mainly from the early medieval period. Genome-wide data reveal a sharp genetic discontinuity between the two epochs. The Roman individual mirrors other Italians from the same period, characterized by significant Near Eastern ancestry. In contrast, the early medieval group-genetically homogeneous-clusters with late antique and medieval populations from Central and Southern Italy, showing significant genetic influence from Central and Northern Europe. Overall, the medieval genetic structure differs from the Roman one and closely resembles that of modern Central and Southern Italians.

title: Box C/D SNORD116-17 promotes prostate cancer progression by targeting the miR-206/E2F5 axis
abstract: Small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) are single-stranded non-coding RNAs found in eukaryotic nucleolus, and their aberrant expression is closely related to tumorigenesis. Box C/D SNORD116-17, a member of SNORD116 cluster, is highly expressed in prostate cancer tissues, though its biological function in this malignancy remains uncharacterized. Here, we found that SNORD116-17 is evident, stable, and highly expressed in prostate cancer cells and that its overexpression significantly promoted the proliferation, migration, and invasion of cancer cells. Bioinformatics prediction, RIP, RNA dot blot, and RNA-protein pulldown experiments revealed that miR-206 interacted with SNORD116-17, forming a complex with Argonaute 2. Subsequently, PCR and western blot experiments revealed that both miR-206 and SNORD116-17 regulated the expression of E2F transcription factor 5 (E2F5), a commonly studied oncogene in prostate cancer. In summary, SNORD116-17 contributes to prostate cancer progression by sponging with miR-206 through the ceRNA mechanism and upregulating the expression of E2F5.

title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
abstract: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. Most studies examine short-term, individual-level responses, limiting inference on long-term effects. Impacts vary widely by stressor, taxon, and biological outcome. Invertebrates often show positive responses linked to reef effects, though key functional traits are vulnerable. Fish responses are largely neutral except under noise, while marine mammals exhibit the most consistent negative impacts. The impact score developed here highlights taxon-specific vulnerability and offers a scalable risk-assessment tool for data-poor regions. The review calls for standardized, long-term field monitoring to support OWF expansion while safeguarding biodiversity.

title: Targeting BCL11B-mediated JAK2/STAT3 activation: A novel therapeutic strategy for Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder where neuroinflammation is a critical driver of pathology. This study investigates the role of the transcription factor BCL11B in PD pathogenesis. Transcriptome sequencing in an acute MPTP-induced mouse model of PD revealed a significant upregulation of BCL11B. In both cellular and mouse PD models, BCL11B expression increased in a time-dependent manner. Furthermore, BCL11B levels were elevated in dopaminergic neurons exposed to inflammatory conditioned medium. Functional studies demonstrated that inhibition of BCL11B exerted neuroprotective effects, mitigating dopaminergic neuron loss, reducing apoptosis, and improving motor deficits. Mechanistically, we identified that BCL11B contributes to neurotoxicity by activating the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway. Inhibition of BCL11B partially blocked the activation in both inflammatory and MPTP-induced models. Conversely, BCL11B overexpression enhanced JAK2/STAT3 activation, which was suppressed by the inhibitor WP1066. In conclusion, our findings establish BCL11B as a novel regulator of neuroinflammation and dopaminergic degeneration in PD, acting through the JAK2/STAT3 pathway. Targeting BCL11B may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for PD.

title: Harnessing polymeric materials for applications in electric vehicle with sustainability contributions and prospects
abstract: The accelerated global shift to EVs is revolutionizing the field of materials science, thereby making polymeric materials indispensable to all subsystems in EVs. In this context, this review provides a critical analysis of the evolution, classification, and applications of polymeric materials within the different EV subsystems, including structural composites, battery housing, thermal systems, insulation, and interior parts. Building on this classification, this review further highlights the latest advances made in the fields of fiber-reinforced polymer composites, engineering thermoplastic polymers, elastomers, bio-based, and recyclable polymers with specific performance criteria and associated challenges. Beyond their technical role, this review also focuses on aligning the technological advancements of such materials with the United Nations sustainable development goals (UN SDGs). This review also highlights relevant knowledge gaps in scaling up bio-based polymer production, the longevity of polymer housings for batteries subjected to thermal cycling, and the lack of a universally agreed-upon EV polymer recycling protocol.

title: Experimental snowball earth viscosity drives the evolution of motile multicellularity
abstract: Abstract During the 70-million-year span of the Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity up to fourfold. In the absence of adaptation, unicellular organisms living in this viscous environment were limited in their ability to move and acquire nutrients. We experimentally test the hypothesis that multicellularity evolved in order to overcome this viscosity-induced metabolic deficit. In the presence of Snowball Earth viscosities, we find that populations of unicellular green algae evolve motile multicellular phenotypes in addition to other phenotypes that optimize different combinations of size and speed. As the Snowball Earth subsided and warm seas returned, the novelty of motile multicellularity permitted these organisms to take physical control over their local environment for the first time. This innovation may underpin the evolution of dominant multicellular lineages on Earth today. Significance statement Beginning 720-million years ago, two global glaciations — together known as the Snowball Earth — covered the planet with a thick layer of ice for a total of 70-million years. Several groups of complex multicellular organisms independently radiated at this time, including animals, green algae, and red algae. All of these clades include lineages with large bodies made of thousands of cells, multiple cell types, and spatial organization. At first glance, it seems that life merely survived despite the Snowball Earth glaciations. We find experimental evidence that the Snowball Earth glaciations were instead an evolutionary trigger for the diversification of complex multicellular groups.

title: The circulating lipidome in severe obesity
abstract: Abstract Background Severe obesity (SevO; BMI ≥40 kg/m²) is rapidly increasing globally and disproportionately affects minority populations. However, it remains understudied in mechanistic and omics literature. Lipid metabolism plays a central role in obesity-related cardiometabolic disease (CMD), but the relationship between molecular lipid species and SevO is poorly understood, particularly in high-risk groups. Methods We analyzed 578 participants from the Cameron County Hispanic Cohort (CCHC) with fasting plasma lipidomic and genetic data, comparing those living with SevO (n=185) to non-obese controls (n=393). A total of 830 circulating lipid species across 49 classes were quantified. Associations between individual lipids and SevO were assessed using logistic regression and orthogonal projections to latent structures discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA). Potential causal links were assessed using network deconvolution mendelian randomization (NDMR), and influential lipids were correlated with CMD traits and DXA-derived body composition. Results Participants with SevO exhibited statistically significantly more adverse cardiometabolic risk factors than controls. Lipidomic profiling revealed broad alterations: shorter, saturated, and monounsaturated triacylglycerols were markedly elevated, while lysophospholipids, plasmalogens, cholesteryl esters, and long-chain lipids were reduced in individuals with SevO when compared to controls (BMI ≥ 18.5 and > 25 kg/m²). OPLS-DA identified over 300 influential lipid species predictive of SevO status. NDMR analyses implicated specific triacylglycerol species as potentially causally linked with SevO status. Influential lipids correlated with insulin resistance, liver steatosis, body fat measures, and HDL-C (absolute value ranges 0.2-0.4). Conclusions Our findings reveal that SevO is marked by extensive and lipid class-specific dysregulation of the circulating lipidome, with strong links to cardiometabolic risk. Notably, triacylglycerols containing shorter length acyl chains emerged as a distinctive lipid signature of SevO—consistently elevated, strongly discriminative of SevO status, and uniquely exhibiting a consistent causal relationship. Our results provide compelling evidence for a novel lipidomic pathway underpinning severe obesity and underscore critical avenues for future research into its genetic, dietary, and mechanistic determinants.

title: Limited global awareness of invasive alien species and little support for their management
abstract: Invasive alien species (IAS) are one of the main drivers of global change and can cause a wide range of negative ecological and social impacts. Addressing these impacts requires management actions, which can fail to be effective when not supported by the public. Here, we conducted the first global survey on people's awareness and perceptions of IAS and support for their management. Our results revealed low public awareness and understanding of biological invasions, and suggest that these are mainly influenced by people's sociodemographic status rather than the social-ecological contexts. Greater awareness of IAS was associated with more negative perceptions toward them and greater support for their management. A large majority of people did not support the use of most management measures. These results suggest that limited public awareness may represent a major obstacle to successfully managing IAS globally, highlighting the need for broader public communication, outreach, and engagement.

title: Dual impact of EZH1/2-targeted therapy in HTLV-1-associated inflammation: Direct and indirect mechanisms
abstract: Human T cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1)-associated inflammation, including uveitis, lacks effective targeted therapies. Here, we investigated whether epigenetic modulation through EZH1/2 inhibition could influence HTLV-1-related ocular inflammation using in vitro co-culture and infection models. HTLV-1 exposure increased EZH1 and EZH2 expression and the repressive histone mark H3K27me3 in retinal pigment epithelial cells. Treatment with the dual EZH1/2 inhibitor valemetostat reduced H3K27me3 levels. Valemetostat showed limited effects on cell viability and induced only modest, context-dependent apoptosis. Virological analyses showed model-dependent changes in proviral load, accompanied by reduced viral gene expression. Profiling of cytokines and chemokines revealed context-dependent modulation of inflammatory mediators. Functional assessment using p65 nuclear translocation assays indicated partial attenuation of NF-κB activation under inflammatory stimulation.
