Collectively, these findings suggest that EZH1/2-mediated epigenetic regulation is primarily involved in HTLV-1-related inflammatory responses, and that inhibiting EZH1/2 may be a potential approach to modulate inflammatory signaling.

title: Olfactory dysfunction among gas station employees exposed to fuel vapors using digital odor identification testing
abstract: Background: Gas station employees are chronically exposed to benzene, a cancer-causing substance found in gasoline vapors, which can cause neurological symptoms. However, its effect on their sense of smell remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the relationship between long-term exposure to gasoline vapors and olfactory dysfunction among gas station employees using a digital odor identification device. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 116 gas station employees in Brazil completed a questionnaire about their background, job history, health issues, and any self-noticed changes in their sense of smell. Olfactory function was assessed using MultiScent 20, a digital odor identification test. The proportion of workers with olfactory dysfunction and its association with duration of employment were analyzed statistically. Findings: The smell tests revealed that 58·6% had hyposmia, and some individuals had functional anosmia. Only 23·3% of participants noticed changes in their smell themselves. Working more years was linked to higher rates of smell problems (p<0·01). Very few participants reported using personal protective equipment (2·6%), despite 62·8% indicating that PPE should be worn during fuel handling. Interpretation: These findings support regular olfactory testing among workers at risk and reinforce the need for stricter preventive measures, improved exposure controls, and occupational health monitoring that includes olfactory function to protect well-being and safety. Funding: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

title: Gut microbiota-driven imbalance of the gut-brain-immune homeostatic network in constipation: Pathogenic mechanisms and evolving therapeutic prospects
abstract: Chronic constipation (CC) is increasingly recognized as a systems-level disorder that cannot be explained by impaired intestinal motility alone. Here, we integrate evidence from clinical cohorts, animal models, and mechanistic studies to examine how gut microbial dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolites perturb epithelial barrier integrity, immune homeostasis, enteric neural activity, and gut-brain signaling. We propose a "gut-brain-immune homeostatic network" in which short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan metabolites, bile acids, and other microbial signals may sustain self-reinforcing interactions linking dysmotility, inflammation, and neurobehavioral disturbances. We further evaluate microbiota-directed interventions, including prebiotics, probiotics, postbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, engineered bacteria, and multi-omics-guided personalized strategies. This framework reframes CC as a multisystem homeostatic disorder and provides a mechanistic basis for patient stratification, therapeutic target discovery, and precision interventions for constipation and related gut-brain-immune disorders.

title: Cross-species RNA sequencing identifies candidate lateralized genes in teleost brains
abstract: Brain lateralization is widespread across vertebrates and contributes to hemispheric specialization. We compared left-right gene expression in the telencephalon and hindbrain of four phylogenetically distant teleosts: zebrafish, medaka, stickleback, and cichlid. Cross-species RNA sequencing identified five candidate genes with consistent directional expression biases. Although no genes remained significant after within-species FDR correction, Fisher's combined probability test supported directional asymmetry of five candidate genes. Notably, ddc and ntn1b were more highly expressed in the left hindbrain in three species and showed similar trends in the remaining species. GO analysis revealed shared functional categories associated with lateralized expression, including transport-related functions in the right-biased telencephalon and nervous system and developmental functions in the left-biased hindbrain. In situ HCR showed more ddc -expressing cells in the left median and dorsal raphe nuclei of medaka. These findings identify candidate molecular signatures associated with shared patterns of brain asymmetry across phylogenetically distant teleosts.

title: Repressed mTORC1 signaling and transient dendritic pruning support axonal regeneration in adult zebrafish
abstract: Dendrite degeneration is an early pathological feature following axonal damage, yet its role during successful axonal regeneration remains poorly understood. Using sparse labeling of retinal ganglion cells in adult zebrafish, we show that axonal regeneration is accompanied by a transient phase of dendritic pruning following optic nerve crush. Dendritic pruning occurs during axon elongation and is reversed after brain reinnervation. Although insulin-mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling is rapidly upregulated immediately after injury, it is subsequently suppressed, coinciding with dendritic pruning and sustained axonal growth. Prolonging mTOR activation through insulin treatment or direct pathway stimulation reduces dendritic pruning in an mTORC1-dependent manner but significantly delays axonal regrowth. Together, these findings identify dendritic remodeling as a temporally regulated component of axonal regeneration in zebrafish and reveal a functional trade-off between dendritic preservation and axon regrowth. This warrants further investigation on whether temporal modulation of dendritic remodeling could promote axonal regeneration in the mammalian central nervous system (CNS).

title: The IKC-leptin axis functions as a molecular bridge between neurodevelopment and endocrine signaling
abstract: Abstract Kcnb1, a voltage-gated K⁺ channel widely expressed in brain, assembles with integrins to form integrin-K⁺ channel complexes (IKCs) in cortex and hypothalamus. Pathogenic KCNB1 variants cause Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy (DEE), and Kcnb1-null (Null) mice reproduce core neurodevelopmental defects alongside chronic hypoleptinemia, suggesting a leptin-IKC signaling axis. We find that Kcnb1, integrins, and the leptin receptor (LepR) co-immunoprecipitate and co-localize in cortical neurons. Perinatal leptin supplementation in Null mice improves cognition, corrects cortical anatomy, and restores neuronal migration, dendritic arborization, and synaptic functionality. In primary Null cortical neurons, leptin normalizes dendritic growth and actin remodeling via integrin-dependent mechanisms. By contrast, leptin has modest effects in WT animals and neurons; sensitivity is unmasked by pharmacological manipulation of integrins, and, strikingly, LepR blockade in the absence of exogenous leptin is sufficient to induce Null-like defects in WT neurons. These findings argue that hypoleptinemia alone does not drive the Null phenotype. Instead, they reveal a previously unrecognized, dual-mode model in which LepR signaling is regulated by both its ligand and IKCs. This conceptual advance links IKC-LepR coupling to neurodevelopment and DEE and pinpoints their interface as a tractable therapeutic target.

title: Role of olfactory receptor Olfr544 in neuronal cells: Insights into neurite outgrowth and CREB signaling
abstract: Olfactory receptors (ORs) are expressed beyond the nasal epithelium and implicated in brain function, yet their roles remain unclear. This study investigated the function of the OR Olfr544, which has been reported to be highly expressed near amyloid plaques in Alzheimer's disease model mice, using the mouse neuroblastoma N2a cell line. We found that its agonist azelaic acid (AZA) promotes neurite outgrowth and activates the cAMP-PKA-CREB signaling cascade in an Olfr544-dependent manner. Transcriptome analysis of Olfr544 -knockout cells revealed altered expression of genes involved in neuroactive signaling and cytoskeletal organization. Key downstream targets, including Igf2bp3, were identified and validated. These results establish a functional link between an extra-olfactory OR and neuronal morphology via CREB in vitro , providing a mechanistic basis for further studies of OR functions in the nervous system.

title: A phase 3 trial of GB-K02 pegfilgrastim biosimilar for preventing chemotherapy-induced neutropenia in breast cancer
abstract: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia (CIN) constitutes a substantial disease burden globally. Although pegfilgrastim (a long-acting granulocyte-colony stimulating factor) has demonstrated efficacy in preventing CIN, it is not yet available in China. This is the first clinical study to evaluate a pegfilgrastim biosimilar in China. This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled, phase 3 equivalence study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of GB-K02 (a pegfilgrastim biosimilar) in preventing CIN among 250 patients with breast cancer. The primary efficacy endpoint was the duration of grade 4 neutropenia (DG4N) in cycle 1 of chemotherapy. The DG4N (LSMean ± SE) in cycle 1 was 0.58 ± 0.13 days versus 0.80 ± 0.13 days ( p = 0.2139) for the GB-K02 group and the pegfilgrastim group, respectively. Other efficacy endpoints and safety were also similar between the two groups in 4 cycles of chemotherapy. Overall, GB-K02 demonstrated proper equivalence to pegfilgrastim and might offer an option in preventing CIN in China.

title: Diversification and hybridization within the Spirochona gemmipara complex driven by gammarid host range shifts
abstract: Hybridizing multispecies complexes represent understudied genetic systems within unicellular eukaryotes. Using integrated morphological, morphometric, and multilocus phylogenetic data, we show that Spirochona gemmipara , a widespread ciliate epibiont of European freshwater gammarids, constitutes a hybridizing network of at least nine lineages forming a sympatric multispecies syngameon. Time-calibrated phylogenies indicate that its five main lineages originated in the Miocene through allopatric divergence on isolated European paleoislands colonized independently by freshwater gammarids. Subsequent reconnection of continental freshwater systems following the regression of the Paratethys Sea enabled secondary contact and hybridization among emerging S. gemmipara -like species, with later Pleistocene range shifts likely maintaining compatibility within the syngameon. Discordant mitochondrial signals within the syngameon are consistent with heteroplasmy and may also reflect phylogenetic noise or nuclear mitochondrial pseudogenes (NUMTs), and only tentatively suggest the possibility of mitogenome recombination. This added complexity underscores the need for whole-genome analyses to clarify mechanisms driving mitochondrial diversity and hybridization in ciliates.

title: Oxidation-regulated wide-temperature tribological behavior and mechanism of a Mo/Mo tribopair lubricated by Ga-based liquid metal
abstract: Gallium-based liquid metals combine fluidity with high thermal and electrical conductivity, making them attractive for lubrication in demanding environments. We investigated the tribological behavior of a Mo/Mo self-mated pair lubricated with Ga-In-Sn (GIS) from room temperature to 300°C in air and argon. Friction and wear tests, together with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses, were used to examine interfacial behavior and tribofilm formation. In air, GIS reduced the Mo-disk wear rate by 90.9%–99.4% compared with the unlubricated pair, accompanied by the formation of a Ga-O-rich tribofilm. In argon, localized Ga retention, tribofilm delamination, and lamellar spalling became more pronounced at elevated temperature, leading to a wear rate of 15.6 × 10 −5 mm 3 /(N·m) at 300°C. These results provide insights into the effects of environmental conditions on liquid-metal lubrication and support the selection of suitable lubrication conditions for high-temperature sliding systems.

title: Polymerase iota coordinates adaptation to replication stress in BRCA2-deficient mammary epithelial cells
abstract: BRCA2 deficiency induces chronic replication stress, yet how epithelial cells adapt to this stress prior to malignant transformation remains poorly defined. Mammary epithelial cells from BRCA2 mutation carriers exhibit early replication-associated genome instability, suggesting that stress-tolerance mechanisms operate before overt cancer development. Here, we identify polymerase iota (Pol ι) as a context-dependent regulator of replication stress processing in BRCA2-deficient mammary epithelium.Analysis of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic data from BRCA2 mutation carriers revealed a selective upregulation of POLI, which we mechanistically validated using primary and non-transformed mammary epithelial cells with experimentally reduced BRCA2 expression. We show that BRCA2 loss induces Pol ι expression and creates a selective dependence on Pol ι for mitotic DNA synthesis (MiDAS), a pathway that completes replication of under-replicated DNA.Unexpectedly, loss of Pol ι in BRCA2 deficient cells does not exacerbate genome instability but instead reduces canonical markers of replication-associated damage, including 53BP1 nuclear bodies, micronuclei, and chromosomal breaks. Mechanistically, Pol ι restrains replication fork progression under stress in BRCA2-deficient cells, increasing the persistence of under-replicated DNA carried into mitosis and promoting MiDAS engagement. Loss of Pol ι releases this constraint, accelerating fork progression and reducing reliance on mitotic replication.Together, these findings define a previously unrecognized, BRCA2-dependent replication stress program in which Pol ι governs how under-replicated DNA is processed across the S-phase-to-mitosis transition. This work reveals a context-specific vulnerability in BRCA2-deficient mammary epithelium that precedes malignant transformation and reshapes our understanding of early genome instability in BRCA2 mutation carriers.

title: Bispecific antibodies targeting TL1A and IL-12/23p40 suppress pathogenic Th1/Th17 responses and ameliorate colitis in mice
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remains a substantial therapeutic challenge, largely due to the limitations of single-target monotherapies. Here, we engineered two bispecific antibodies, KA-4316 and its half-life-extended derivative KA-5817, which co-target TL1A and IL-12/23p40 utilizing a common light chain design and knobs-into-holes Fc engineering. To improve clinical translatability, KA-5817 was modified with YTE Fc mutations to enhance FcRn binding. KA-4316 exhibited high binding affinity for both targets, high monomer purity, and favorable thermal stability. In vitro functional assays demonstrated that KA-4316 potently blocked TL1A-DR3 and IL-12/23p40-IL-12Rβ1 interactions, suppressing downstream signaling and pro-inflammatory cytokine release. In vivo , KA-5817 alleviated pathological severity in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in TL1A/IL23A/IL12B triple-humanized mice and showed a prolonged serum half-life in FcRn-humanized mice. KA-4316 and KA-5817 exhibit beneficial manufacturability and favorable biological activity. Our results support dual inhibition of TL1A and IL-12/23p40 as a potential therapeutic strategy for IBD.

title: Context shapes action understanding in social interactions
abstract: In social interactions, individuals anticipate what others are about to do next, enabling smooth social interactions and coexistence in daily life. Here, we examined how kinematic and contextual cues are weighted and integrated to predict an interactor's actions during dynamic, real-time competitive interactions. We analyzed 76 participants (38 dyads) freely playing 300 games of rock-paper-scissors each while tracking their kinematics using motion capture. Although movement kinematics consistently conveyed intention-related information, successful action selection depended primarily on how this information influenced predictions. Reinforcement-learning based contextual inference emerged as the strongest predictor of single-trial success and modulated the degree to which movement-derived predictions guided behavior. When contextual and movement-derived information afforded different actions, prioritizing contextual inference consistently outperformed movement-derived predictions. Thus, successful social action understanding depends not on maximizing sensitivity to movement cues, but on adaptively arbitrating between movement-derived and outcome-based contextual information during ongoing social interaction.

title: Large cranial windows distort auditory cortical maps and degrade feature integration in secondary auditory cortex
abstract: Understanding how sensory information is transformed along cortical hierarchies requires reliable measurement of sensory representations across areas. In vivo two-photon calcium imaging through chronic cranial windows has become an essential approach for characterizing cortical sensory representations with cellular resolution and spatial registration across experiments. However, cortical computations, particularly in higher-order cortices, depend on intricate intracortical circuitry and can be sensitive to subtle tissue perturbations introduced during surgical preparation. Here, we report that implantation of large cranial windows can mechanically compress the intrinsically curved cortical surface, producing systematic distortion that is usually not recognized as overt tissue damage. By comparing sensory maps in the mouse auditory cortex before and after window implantation, we show that larger windows commonly used across laboratories are associated with distorted sensory maps away from the center of the window. Furthermore, both macroscopic and cellular-level imaging reveal a deterioration of feature-selective responses in the secondary auditory cortex (A2) following such distortion. Together, these findings identify an overlooked but controllable surgical factor that can bias measurements of sensory representations and highlight an important consideration for enhancing reproducibility across studies.

title: Lipid metabolism remodeling in human cardiomyocyte differentiation and maturation
abstract: Cardiac development involves extensive metabolic remodeling, yet dynamic changes of endogenous lipid species during human cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation remain poorly characterized. In this study, we systematically performed high-coverage lipidomic profiling across five consecutive CM differentiation stages, using high-performance liquid chromatography. MYL2 expression confirmed ventricular lineage specification in late-stage CMs. Ceramide levels peaked at the cardiac progenitor cell (CPC) stage, suggesting a stage-specific association with the mesendoderm (MES)-to-CPC transition. Meanwhile, lipid categories such as monosialodihexosylganglioside, phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophosphatidylcholine, and lysophosphatidic acid were markedly elevated in mature CMs. Integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility analyses further delineated the temporal regulatory landscape underlying stage-dependent lipid remodeling during cardiogenic differentiation. Functional assays revealed that PC promotes the expression of mature CM marker genes and improves CM viability. Collectively, these findings establish a comprehensive, high-resolution dynamic lipidomic atlas of in vitro hESC-derived CM differentiation, providing a valuable resource for understanding lipid-associated mechanisms in heart development.

title: Gamma irradiation shapes high value metabolite responses across microbes microalgae and plants
abstract: Gamma irradiation can function either as an acute physical elicitor that alters redox and metabolic regulation or as a mutagen that generates selectable genetic variation. We compared evidence from bacteria, fungi, microalgae, plants, and plant cell systems using a common framework that links absorbed dose and exposure context to response mode, evidence strength, phenotype stability, and productivity. Across these systems, irradiation can increase metabolite accumulation or support recovery of improved strains and lines, but responses remain strongly dependent on biological material, dosimetry, selection, and cultivation conditions. Heterogeneous dose reporting, inconsistent productivity denominators, limited causal validation, and scarce scale-up data prevent definition of a universal effective dose or mechanism. We therefore distinguish concentration from total yield and volumetric productivity and propose a stage-gated workflow integrating dosimetry, molecular characterization, stability testing, bioprocess evaluation, and safety and economic assessment to support defensible translation.

title: Palaeoproteomic and genetic insights into millennial-scale dairy consumption in Armenia
abstract: Dairy products are a key component of diet in Armenia today, yet the origins of milk consumption, its historical development, and genetic adaptations related to milk digestion remain understudied. Here, we investigate the co-evolution of dairying practices and lactase persistence in Armenia through combined palaeoproteomic and genetic analyses spanning prehistory to the present. Our palaeoproteomic results provide direct evidence of milk consumption in prehistoric Armenia and, with existing regional data, indicate that dairying was an established component of the South Caucasus subsistence economy at least from the 4th millennium BCE. Milk proteins were predominantly recovered from high-altitude sites, suggesting that dairy consumption may have served as an adaptive strategy in highland environments. In contrast, genetic findings indicate that lactase persistence-associated variants never reached high frequencies throughout Armenian prehistory. This may reflect cultural adaptation to fermenting dairy products, reducing lactose content and enabling dairy consumption in genetically lactose-intolerant populations.

title: L-Histidine alleviates tacrolimus-induced islet dysfunction via the gut-pancreas axis
abstract: Tacrolimus is widely used after organ transplantation but can impair pancreatic β-cell function and glucose homeostasis. Using rodent models, antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation, 16S rRNA sequencing, metabolomic profiling, and MIN-6 cells, we examined whether microbiota-associated L-histidine contributes to β-cell protection. Tacrolimus altered gut microbial composition and increased histidine-associated microbial and metabolic signals. L-histidine supplementation improved glucose tolerance and insulin secretion, reduced β-cell apoptosis, and increased PI3K/Akt/mTOR/p70S6K signaling and PDX-1, NeuroD1, and MafA expression. Microbiota depletion attenuated several protective effects of L-histidine, supporting a contribution of the gut microbiota to this response. These findings connect a microbiota-associated amino acid with tacrolimus-related β-cell dysfunction and provide a framework for investigating microbiota-metabolite contributions to metabolic complications of immunosuppression.

title: Dissociable pupil-linked arousal during overt and inner speech
abstract: Inner (covert) speech, the silent production of language in one's mind, plays a central role in human cognition and engages speech-related cortical networks partly overlapping with those for overt speech. Because cortical language processing unfolds within arousal states set by the ascending systems, we asked whether inner and overt speech are accompanied by similar pupil-linked arousal patterns. Using pupillometry across three counting-task experiments, we found a dissociation between inner and overt speech. While overt speech consistently elicited pupil dilation across conditions, inner speech produced a variable dilation profile relative to baseline: pupil constriction (simple counting), no deviation (noun-phrase counting), and clear dilation (step counting; high cognitive load). Importantly, pupil size during inner speech remained smaller than that during overt speech despite task-dependent dynamics. These findings suggest that task-elicited inner speech is accompanied by lower pupil-linked arousal than overt speech, adding a state-level physiological dimension to cortical accounts of verbal processing.

title: Aquifer-differentiated process-guided GRU for multi-timescale groundwater-level prediction
abstract: Groundwater-level prediction supports water-resource management in overexploited aquifers, yet conventional data-driven models often struggle to represent pumping disturbances and contrasting shallow- and deep-aquifer responses. Using groundwater levels, meteorological variables, and agricultural pumping data from four shallow and four deep wells in Guantao County, North China Plain, we developed an aquifer-differentiated process-guided gated recurrent unit model for daily and dekadal (10-day) prediction. Compared with a conventional gated recurrent unit model, the process-guided model reduced group-mean root-mean-square error by 7.2% and 6.1% for shallow and deep wells at the daily scale and by 4.0% and 2.1% at the dekadal scale, respectively. Deep-well performance depended on the pumping-response window, with 60-day averaged pumping providing a stable configuration. These incremental gains show that incorporating pumping disturbances and aquifer-specific response differences as process guidance can improve groundwater-level representation and provide a modeling approach for groundwater management in agricultural abstraction areas.

title: IκBζ target genes in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
abstract: IκBζ, an atypical IκB protein induced downstream of Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling, is pivotal in orchestrating inflammatory responses and modulating inflammation-associated B cell malignancies. However, the transcriptional and epigenetic programs regulated by IκBζ in both normal and malignant B cells remain poorly described. Here, we analyzed chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) cells by epigenomic profiling to dissect the molecular function of IκBζ in leukemia. In primary human B cells and CLL samples, chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) and cleavage under targets and tagmentation (CUT&Tag) analyses delineated a comprehensive genome-wide landscape of IκBζ binding sites. Key genes, including NFKB2 , BATF , and FOXP1 , gained IκBζ binding after TLR stimulation in both CLL and B cells, whereas CXCR5 was mainly bound in CLL cells. Pharmacological or genetic inhibition of IκBζ signaling disrupted the induction of these molecules, highlighting its potential role as a central transcriptional tuner that integrates TLR-mediated inflammatory pathways with B cell receptor (BCR) signaling and migration.

title: A source-target transfer learning framework with physics priors for subsurface chlorophyll reconstruction in the Northwest Pacific Ocean
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) distributions provide a foundation for understanding upper-ocean ecosystem dynamics and biogeochemical variability. We developed the source-target coupled network (ST-CoupleNet), a physics-guided transfer learning framework that combines Earth system model simulations with observation-constrained reconstructions to estimate subsurface Chl-a in the Northwest Pacific Ocean. The framework first learns large-scale spatiotemporal vertical representations from long-term CMIP6 simulations and then adapts them using reconstructed fields constrained by BioGeoChemical-Argo (BGC-Argo) observations, reducing simulation biases while preserving regional variability. By integrating dual-attention, residual learning, and convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) architectures, ST-CoupleNet substantially improves reconstruction accuracy over a conventional convolutional neural network (CNN). This framework demonstrates how transferable knowledge from climate simulations can be combined with autonomous observations to generate continuous 3D Chl-a fields, enabling large-scale investigations of subsurface marine ecosystems and biogeochemical change.

title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

title: The immunophenotypic landscape of newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia: Associations with genotype and outcomes
abstract: Despite widespread immunophenotyping in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), its immunophenotypic heterogeneity remains incompletely understood. Here, we applied state-of-the-art computational modeling to >50 million single cells from diagnostic bone marrow aspirates of 502 AML patients. Jointly modeling leukemic and non-malignant cells, we identified seven patient clusters with distinct immunophenotypic signatures. These clusters showed strong concordance with recurrent mutations, including NPM1 , IDH1/IDH2 , CEBPA , and t(8;21)(q22;q22); RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusions, and enabled accurate prediction of genomic subgroups. Although these immunophenotypic signatures were not associated with therapy responses, loss of HLA-DR expression on leukemic blasts at diagnosis was independently associated with inferior outcomes in patients with chromatin-spliceosome mutations. In addition, we identified an immunophenotypic patient cluster comprising ∼11% of patients characterized by significant bone marrow lymphocyte enrichment where outcomes diverged depending on genetic risk. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive single-cell characterization of AML bone marrow and reveal clinically relevant genotype-phenotype relationships.

title: Drosophila Appl loss disrupts proteins in mitochondrial oxidative and glycosylation pathways conserved in Alzheimer's disease
abstract: The physiological functions of the amyloid precursor protein (APP) remain unclear due to genetic redundancy and complex phenotypes. For decades, Drosophila amyloid precursor protein-like ( Appl ) research has relied on Appl d , a presumed null allele generated by irradiation. Here, we show that Appl d contains complex chromosomal rearrangements and background mutations confounding the interpretation of gene function. To address this, we created a precise CRISPR toolkit, including a clean null and a reporter allele. Deep proteomic profiling reveals that true Appl loss affects proteins associated with N-linked glycosylation, mitochondrial, and metabolic functions in a distinct signature from the background of Appl d . This conserved metabolic signature mirrors alterations in human patients and mouse Alzheimer's models and is associated with disrupted sleep and locomotion in flies. Our findings correct the genetic understanding of Appl , establishing it as a conserved regulator of metabolic balance essential for neuronal function.

title: Mechano-electric response of tribopositive, fluoropolymer-free polyvinyl acetate nanogenerators in multiple contact electrification
abstract: Polyvinyl acetate (PVAc) is a highly polar, fluorine-free polymeric adhesive that combines strong interfacial adhesion with good processability. Despite this, PVAc has rarely been investigated as an active layer in mechano-electric nanogenerators, even though its strong adhesion facilitates effective interfacial contact, thereby eliminating the need for auxiliary conductive layers. Electrical measurements revealed that the electrical output of PVAc arises from the interplay of triboelectric charge transfer, electrostatic induction driven by residual polarization, and deformation-induced interfacial polarization. The nanogenerators achieved an open-circuit voltage up to 350 V, a short-circuit current density of 1.8 μAcm −2 , and power density of 0.07 mWcm −2 at a maximum power point of 4.4 MΩ. Stable output over 10 4 cycles demonstrated that PVAc is a suitable polymer for a new generation of fluoropolymer-free nanogenerators and flexible pressure sensors.

title: Climate change and sexual and reproductive health: A mixed methods scoping review of possible mechanisms
abstract: This scoping review synthesized empirical evidence on the relationships and possible pathways through which climate change could impact sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Eligible sources had to investigate climate change and SRHR using any study design. Two independent reviewers conducted screening; data extraction captured exposures, outcomes, associations/relationships, and possible mediators and contextual moderators. From 40,503 database-identified sources, we included 256 peer-reviewed publications across 108 LMICs. We identified 14 potential pathways and developed a typology of mediators and contextual moderators to inform the mechanisms. Five mediator domains were identified: (1) systems and infrastructure, (2) demographic shifts, (3) socioeconomic resources, and (4) behavioral and (5) biological. Six contextual moderator types were isolated: (1) patriarchal norms, (2) cultural power structures, (3) socioeconomic realities, (4) gender-inequitable climate governance, (5) place-based factors, and (6) pre-existing systems/infrastructure. As climate shocks intensify, advancing a mechanistic understanding will be critical to designing responsive, inclusive, and sustainable systems of protection.

title: Graphene-oxide-microfiber aptasensor for dynamic neutrophil monitoring: Bridging cytokine release syndrome and point-of-care sepsis diagnosis
abstract: Neutrophil granule release is critical for host defense, yet its dysregulation underpins cytokine release syndrome (CRS) in both acute (such as sepsis) and sustained inflammatory states. Distinguishing these phases requires real-time monitoring of early markers like neutrophil elastase (ELANE) and lactoferrin (LF), but conventional assays lack requisite sensitivity. Here, we developed a graphene-oxide-functionalized optical microfiber biosensor with high-affinity DNA aptamers (NE-AP and LF-AP) to quantify ELANE and LF via aptamer-protein binding-induced spectral red shifts. The sensor achieved ultralow detection limits (3.57 × 10 −20 M for ELANE and 1.28 × 10 −19 M for LF), eight orders below ELISA, with excellent selectivity. In a lipopolysaccharide-induced murine model, it resolved distinct temporal release profiles of ELANE and LF, and in clinical validation, it showed distinct spectral responses between septic patients and healthy controls in a preliminary clinical cohort. This platform provides a highly sensitive, real-time tool for decoding neutrophil dynamics, with preliminary translational potential for early sepsis diagnosis.

title: Key genes and pathways of pulmonary hypertension identified by integrating bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive vascular disease, yet the underlying cell-type-specific molecular networks and diagnostic biomarkers remain incompletely defined. Integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, we identified 14 pulmonary cell types in PH, with smooth muscle cells (SMCs) as a central communication hub interacting with monocytes and macrophages. High-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) revealed 4 SMC modules enriched in extracellular matrix organization, TGF-β, and HIF-1 pathways. A five-gene diagnostic signature distinguished PH from controls with an area under the curve of 0.895. Immune infiltration and enrichment analysis showed that activated CD4 memory T cells, activated dendritic cells, and resting mast cells increased in the PH group, while angiogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition pathway were upregulated. In hypoxic human pulmonary artery SMCs, milk fat globule-epidermal growth factor-8 (MFGE8), secreted frizzled-related protein 2 (SFRP2), S100 calcium-binding protein A11 (S100A11), and procollagen C-endopeptidase enhancer 2 (PCOLCE2) were upregulated, and their knockdown suppressed proliferation, highlighting them as potential biomarkers and drivers of vascular remodeling, revealing a new molecular mechanism for PH and providing insights for potential therapeutic targets.

title: Protocol for fabricating immune-regulatory bone organoids via plant-based bioinks
abstract: Bone organoids offer three-dimensional systems for studying skeletal development, disease, and regeneration. However, many existing bone organoid systems do not adequately incorporate immune-regulatory cues, despite their central role in bone repair. Their translational potential is further limited by the use of animal-derived matrices such as Matrigel, which are xenogeneic, poorly defined, and subject to batch-to-batch variation. To address these limitations, we developed a Matrigel-free and exogenous cytokine-free bioink composed of Aloe vera gel (AV), gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA), and Laponite. This formulation supports the fabrication of immune-regulatory bone organoids by providing both a printable extracellular matrix-like scaffold and intrinsic immune-regulatory signals. In vitro , the bioink promotes sustained macrophage reprogramming and helps establish an immune microenvironment that supports bone organoid maturation. Here, we describe a step-by-step protocol for preparing the plant-containing bioink, fabricating immune-regulatory bone organoids, and evaluating their performance in cranial bone defect models. This defined and reproducible platform provides a practical alternative to conventional Matrigel-based systems and may be adapted for the engineering of other immune-responsive tissues.

title: Symbolic and non-symbolic geometric abilities across development and in individuals with dyscalculia and dyslexia
abstract: Geometry is fundamental to mathematical thinking, yet its foundations and difficulties in learning disorders remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the development of geometric abilities and their relationship with developmental dyscalculia and dyslexia. Seventy-nine children and adults, including individuals with and without learning difficulties, completed behavioral measures of non-symbolic geometry and a paper-and-pencil assessment of symbolic geometry. Geometric abilities continued to develop from early adolescence into young adulthood and non-symbolic geometry predicted symbolic geometry independently of age, verbal reasoning, non-verbal reasoning and visuospatial working memory. Adults with dyscalculia, most of whom also had dyslexia, showed impairments in both non-symbolic and symbolic geometry that persisted after controlling for visuospatial working memory, whereas individuals with dyslexia without dyscalculia performed comparably to controls. These findings suggest that non-symbolic geometry contributes to formal geometric competence and that geometric difficulties may be a persistent feature of developmental dyscalculia, with implications for education and clinical assessment.

title: Quantitative systems pharmacology modeling of class I–III BRAF-mutant NSCLC enables subgroup treatment analysis and combination therapy design
abstract: BRAF-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comprises three functional classes (I–III) with distinct driving mechanisms, yet effective therapies for classes II and III remain limited. To address this, we developed a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model that mechanistically recapitulates signaling networks and drug responses across all three classes, integrating multiscale preclinical-to-clinical datasets. The model enabled high-throughput prediction of clinical efficacy for monotherapies and combination therapies across diverse dosing regimens, and we identified that combining MEK and ERK inhibition represents a novel strategy for class II/III mutants, validated by original in vivo MiniPDX data using NSCLC patient tumors. Simulations further revealed that only triple blockade of EGFR, IGF1R, and FGFR pathway initiation can potently reduce tumor growth and overcome resistance in these classes. Our work is the first multiscale QSP platform mechanistically addressing class I–III BRAF mutations at the systems level for disease-centric translational combination therapy discovery and precision medicine design.

title: A dual recombinant strategy to quantify PreS1 antibody in hepatitis B patients with genotype B or C virus by ELISA
abstract: Elevated levels of anti-preS1 antibodies in patients correlate with faster hepatitis B virus (HBV) clearance, since preS1 is vital for viral entry. However, accurate quantification of preS1 antibodies is hindered by the variation of HBV genotypes. Herein, a quantitative preS1 antibody assay was developed for Chinese patients with predominant HBV genotypes B and C. First, to address genotype diversity, we constructed a dual recombinant protein combining genotype B and C preS1. Second, a mouse-human chimeric antibody with high and comparable affinity for both B and C preS1 is developed as the standard for quantification by screening and cloning. An optimized ELISA kit using these components demonstrated good specificity, accuracy, reproducibility and stability, with a linear range of 10-100 ng/mL. This approach extends the patient coverage in China to over 95%, providing a valuable diagnostic tool. This work demonstrates a proof-of-concept model for developing broad-coverage assays for other multi-genotype viral diseases.

title: Single-cell mapping of human plasma cell fate reveals a commitment checkpoint and Cav-1β expression associated with mTORC1 machinery
abstract: Human B cell differentiation into antibody-secreting plasma cells (PCs) requires coordinated transcriptional and organelle remodeling. Using single-cell transcriptomics in an in vitro human B cell differentiation system, we identified a Day-8 commitment checkpoint separating PC, memory B cell, and germinal center-like trajectories and defined an XBP1-associated transcriptional program linked to organelle remodeling. Within this program, CAV1 was induced during PC commitment and encoded a non-caveolar Cav-1β isoform expressed in plasmablasts and PCs. Proteomic analyses showed that Cav-1β associates with endoplasmic reticulum, secretory, and nutrient-sensing proteins, including components of the V-ATPase-RAGulator-RAG complex. CAV1 silencing had modest effects on PC differentiation but did not alter acute mTORC1 activation or antibody secretion. These findings place Cav-1β within the membrane and organelle remodeling program of human PCs and highlight how intracellular architecture may be coupled to metabolic and secretory adaptation during plasma cell differentiation.

title: Potential molecular links between triclosan exposure and osteoarthritis: An integrative systems toxicology study
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic disease affecting the entire joint, influenced by a combination of inflammatory, metabolic, immune, and environmental factors. Triclosan (TCS), a commonly used antimicrobial compound, has been linked to oxidative and immune disturbances; however, its molecular relevance to OA remains to be elucidated. This study integrated network toxicology, bulk transcriptomics, cross-cohort machine learning prioritization, immune infiltration analysis, single-cell transcriptomic analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and primary chondrocyte experiments. Thirty candidate genes related to both TCS and OA were identified, with CBR3, MAOA, MMP13, and AVPR1A being prioritized. Among these, CBR3 exhibited the most stable contribution to model predictions, widespread expression across OA chondrocyte subpopulations, and significant associations with inferred immune-cell composition. Supporting molecular docking and dynamics analyses indicated structural compatibility and dynamic feasibility between TCS and the four candidate proteins. In primary rat chondrocytes, low-dose TCS heightened reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, upregulated Cbr3 and Mmp13, downregulated Col2a1, Maoa, and Avpr1a, and increased CBR3 protein levels, with specific redox-related and matrix-related alterations becoming more pronounced under IL-1β stimulation. These findings contribute to a model that links TCS-associated redox disturbances to OA-relevant chondrocyte stress and matrix remodeling, providing candidate molecular connections for future mechanistic validation.

title: NAT10 exacerbates aortic valve calcification via PCSK9 mRNA ac4C acetylation
abstract: N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C) is an epitranscriptomic regulator involved in diverse pathological processes. This study investigates the role of N-acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10), the primary enzyme responsible for ac4C deposition, in aortic valve calcification (AVC). NAT10 expression and global ac4C levels are upregulated in calcified aortic valves from human patients and murine models. Clinically, elevated NAT10 expression correlates with increased disease severity. Functionally, NAT10 promotes human valvular interstitial cells (hVICs) osteogenic differentiation. In high-cholesterol diet (HCD)-fed ApoE −/− mice, pharmacological NAT10 inhibition (via remodelin) or targeted degradation (via PROTAC NP1192) ameliorates AVC. Mechanistically, we identified the pro-calcific gene proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) as a downstream target of NAT10. NAT10 catalyzes the ac4C modification of PCSK9 mRNA, thereby enhancing its transcript stability. Collectively, our findings reveal a NAT10-ac4C-PCSK9 regulatory axis that amplifies AVC, establishing the NAT10/ac4C machinery as a promising therapeutic target for calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD).

title: Potential role of platelet-derived growth factor D in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk
abstract: A considerable residual cardiovascular risk persists despite contemporary therapies, highlighting the urgent need to identify potential targets for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) onset and progression. Accumulating evidence suggests that platelet-derived growth factor D (PDGFD) may be involved in the development of ASCVD. Herein, we leveraged 20-year longitudinal data from the Chinese Multi-provincial Cohort Study-Proteomics Project, with up to four repeated PDGFD measurements per participant, to estimate the serum PDGFD-ASCVD association. We then emulated the effectiveness of hypothetical reductions in PDGFD serum levels on ASCVD prevention. Our findings suggest that elevated circulating PDGFD levels are associated with higher ASCVD risk and that hypothetical PDGFD-lowering strategies may be associated with reduced long-term ASCVD risk, with an estimated absolute risk reduction of up to approximately 9% under the most intensive intervention scenario. We anticipate that these findings may motivate further investigation of PDGFD-lowering strategies as a potential approach for ASCVD risk reduction.

title: Gammaherpesvirus infection of myeloid cells reveals divergent outcomes regulated by host and viral factors
abstract: Summary The gammaherpesviruses establish a lifelong infection, with the cellular outcome of infection intimately regulated by cell type. Though myeloid cells are an early infection target, infection results in widely divergent outcomes without a clear explanation. Here we use murine gammaherpesvirus 68 to demonstrate that macrophages are readily infectable, resulting in three divergent infection outcomes dictated by viral and host factors. Infection in vivo and in a cell culture model results in a high frequency of viable cells characterized by restricted viral transcription and unexpected transcription of the ORF75 locus, with rare cells initiating but failing to complete lytic replication. Restricted infection can be fully converted to productive lytic replication by pre-treatment with the host cytokine IL-4. Finally, infection with a high viral dose also results in productive infection, but triggers increased cell death. These studies demonstrate stepwise regulation of virus infection and identify virus and host factors that dictate divergent outcomes in a single cell type.

title: Chemical modifications to enhance the stability of DNA nanoparticles for biological applications
abstract: Synthetic DNA nanoparticles offer unique modularity and chemical versatility to build systems for biomedical applications. Extensive research into DNA nanoparticles has led to superior control over loading therapeutic cargo, adding targeting and imaging moieties, and designing desired geometries. One of the main barriers to translating DNA nanoparticles into clinical therapies, however, is their stability in biological environments. Introduction of DNA nanoparticles in biological environments exposes them to various stressors such as nuclease enzymes, depleted salt conditions, and alterations in oxidizing conditions. It is therefore necessary to develop strategies to protect DNA nanoparticles against such stressors to preserve their structural integrity and function. In this review, we highlight dominant chemical modifications that have been optimized to secure DNA nanoparticles against stressors with a focus on biological applications. We provide comprehensive accounts of notable examples from recent results and discuss aspects of DNA nanoparticle stability that require the community's attention.

title: Gas gill respiration enhances underwater copulation in a water scorpion
abstract: To overcome physiological constraints during submergence, many air-breathing aquatic animals utilize an air store. If this store functions as a gas gill for dissolved oxygen uptake, this will extend underwater copulation when atmospheric oxygen is inaccessible. We tested this hypothesis using water scorpion Nepa hoffmanni (Hemiptera: Nepidae). Our field surveys showed that, although N. hoffmanni typically inhabit shallow water, males cannot access atmospheric oxygen via their respiratory siphon during underwater copulation. Laboratory experiments revealed active oxygen use from the air store beneath the wings during submergence. Furthermore, under higher dissolved oxygen treatments, males copulated longer and more frequently, while mate-guarding behavior remained unaffected. These findings provide the first direct evidence that dissolved oxygen uptake via a gas gill enhances copulation efficiency in air-breathing aquatic insects, highlighting the importance of environmental oxygen availability for aquatic reproductive strategies, especially in the context of ongoing climate-driven changes to freshwater ecosystems.

title: What modern genomes overlook: Ancient DNA rewrites the phylogeography of European atlantic salmon (Salmo salar)
abstract: Conservation plans for declining species often rely on contemporary genetic/genomic data to infer historical population structure and evolutionary history of the species. However, modern samples alone may not accurately reflect historical genetic variation, especially after severe population declines or intensive management, and need reference baseline data prior to anthropogenic impact. We analysed whole-genome sequences dating to 18,800-16,700 years ago from Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), that experienced major declines over the past century. Comparing Paleolithic and modern genomes, we found that ancient salmon from the Iberian glacial refugium were genetically closer to present-day northern European populations than to modern Iberian salmon, consistent with southward displacement of northern lineages during glacial periods, postglacial decline of Iberian populations and contemporary human impacts. We identified ancient SNPs linked to reproduction and age at maturation in modern salmon populations, while high ancient mitochondrial effective population size suggests greater prehistorical female lineage diversity. These genetic discontinuities between ancient and modern Iberian salmon, not evident in modern samples alone, highlight the value of ancient genomics in conservation.

title: Acarbose differentially affects gut microbial metabolism of maltose and sucrose, distinctly modulating host metabolism
abstract: Gut microbiota act as beneficial symbionts of the hosts. Administration of α-glucosidase inhibitors (α-GIs) is considered to promote the microbiota's carbohydrate availability, modulating short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production. However, it remains unclear whether host-microbiota interaction differs depending on α-GI types (e.g., acarbose versus miglitol) and carbohydrate types co-administered. In this study, we demonstrate that acarbose is transported through bacterial outer membrane porins, LamB and ScrY, and inhibits maltose metabolism in Escherichia coli . Furthermore, studies using Klebsiella pneumoniae reveal that acarbose suppresses utilization of maltose, but not that of sucrose. When co-administered with acarbose in mice, sucrose, relative to maltose, enhances SCFA production, suppresses glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) secretion, and protects against high-fat diet-induced obesity, underscoring the importance of sucrose as a microbiota-dependent beneficial factor, but not a culprit in host metabolism. In conclusion, acarbose regulates host metabolic processes partly by modulating gut microbial metabolism in a carbohydrate-type-dependent manner.

title: Optical pulling force in carbon nanotubes: Manifestation of non-local conductivity
abstract: We develop a new theory of an optical force exerted on a carbon nanotube (CNT) with a non-local conductivity. To determine the optical force, we employ an integral-equation-based approach in terms of the current density. The analysis is constructed for a finite-length cylindrical CNT by rigorously accounting for edge effects. In addition to numerical solutions of the integral equation, we obtain an approximate analytical expression for the optical force acting on the CNT, which shows good agreement with numerical simulations. We also demonstrate the existence of some frequency ranges in which the optical force becomes negative, corresponding to the optical pulling effect. Such a pulling behavior is shown to originate from the non-locality of the conductivity. This work advances theoretical understanding of optomechanical interactions in low-dimensional conductors and clarifies the role of spatial dispersion in the emergence of optical pulling forces.

title: No practice and still perfect: Different routes for promoting offline gains in perceptual learning
abstract: Visual perceptual learning is thought to require extensive training, but a few reminder trials can sometimes replace daily practice. In a 5-day texture discrimination learning experiment, we showed that both accounts need amendment. Following an initial training session, we found that further skill acquisition can be accomplished either with repeated daily administration of a few reminder trials or by offline learning without any further training, depending on attentional context and task demands. In dual-task conditions involving the simultaneous discrimination of a peripheral texture target and a central fixation target, reminders were as effective as daily training, whereas no learning occurred without reminders. In contrast, in a single-task condition without a fixation task, learning emerged without reminders or training. Hence, attentional context and task demands may determine the ability of reminders or protracted consolidation to yield offline learning gains that are comparable to those delivered by daily training.

title: Cats and humans show correlated affiliative physiological states
abstract: Cats are among the world's most popular companion animals. Owner-pet hormonal synchrony is documented in dogs but untested in cats. We measured oxytocin and cortisol in 19 owners and 29 pet cats over one month, and examined owner mood and owner-cat proximity via Bluetooth beacons. Owner and cat oxytocin were positively associated, whereas their cortisol concentrations showed little association. Higher cat oxytocin was linked to lower owner cortisol and less negative mood, while higher owner cortisol was linked to more negative mood. Closer proximity predicted higher owner vigor, and exploratory behavioral testing linked cat oxytocin to social approach and cortisol to reduced approach toward strangers. Unlike the cortisol-centered synchrony reported in human-dog dyads, human-cat relationships may center on oxytocin, extending interspecies hormonal findings to a species with a distinct domestication history. These correlations may partly reflect shared household environments rather than dyad-specific interactions, an issue that future studies should address.

title: AI-driven environmental performance index using deep autoencoders for monitoring sustainable development goals
abstract: This study develops an autoencoder-based environmental performance index (AE_EPI) to assess environmental performance across 38 countries in five regions. Using a deep autoencoder, AE_EPI captures complex nonlinear relationships in high-dimensional, multi-region data and is benchmarked against a principal component analysis-based index (PCA_EPI). Linear Regression, Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost, combined with SHAP analysis, are used to identify key environmental drivers. Results show that AE_EPI outperforms PCA_EPI in reconstruction accuracy, stability, and robustness to noise, while RF yields the most consistent predictions. Globally, electricity access and renewable energy are the dominant drivers. Regionally, governance and innovation are most important in East Asia; urbanization in South Asia; renewable energy in Central Asia; digitalization in MENA; and economic capacity, electricity access, and governance in Sub-Saharan Africa. These findings support region-specific, data-driven policies that advance energy transitions, strengthen institutional capacity, and address local environmental priorities for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Long COVID is associated with lipoxygenase-catalyzed metabolism of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids
abstract: Long COVID (LC) represents a failure of healthy resolution mechanisms for inflammation after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Dietary essential polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and their downstream metabolites can orchestrate inflammation resolution, suggesting these pathways may be altered in LC. In this study, plasma samples from two independent participant cohorts totaling 106 participants (designated by chart review as LC or Recovered) were collected longitudinally in the 12 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection and analyzed by mass spectrometry for targeted PUFA metabolites. In the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, upregulation of PUFA metabolites downstream of 12-lipoxygenase was associated with later development of LC. In the months following infection, LC participants displayed uncoupling of PUFA-related lipid metabolism and altered lipoxygenase-driven metabolism over time compared to recovered participants. These results provide new mechanistic insights for the development of LC and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for this prevalent and debilitating disorder.

title: Overexpression of endoplasmic reticulum acetyl-CoA transporter AT-1 alters neuronal metabolism, growth, and synaptic activity
abstract: The metabolite acetyl-CoA plays a central role in cellular metabolic homeostasis. As part of the secretory pathway, acetyl-CoA is imported into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) by a membrane-bound transporter AT-1 (SLC33A1). AT-1 has been linked to peripheral neuropathy (heterozygous mutations), developmental delay with premature death (homozygous mutations) and intellectual disability with progeria (duplication). These phenotypes can be reproduced in the mouse. Here, we show that AT-1 overexpression in primary neurons impacts diverse phenotypes related to neuronal function and plasticity. At the gene level, AT-1 induces brain aging signatures, and key differences in ribosomal and synaptic processes were identified in both the transcriptome and the proteome. Changes in mitochondria-associated pathways were reflected in an increase in expression of mitochondrial master regulator PGC-1α and its target genes. Functionally, marked differences in mitochondrial membrane potential, architecture, and respiration were detected. Tracing experiments indicated altered glucose utilization in glycogen storage and nucleotide production. Shifts in redox metabolism were linked to differences in levels of NAD-dependent SIRT1 and CtBP2, with consequences for acetylated lysine modification. Depletion of lipid stores was associated with greater plasticity in fuel substrate utilization and a major shift in cellular lipid composition. These broad-scale changes in metabolism were coincident with reduced expression of synaptic proteins and reduced activity among synaptic networks, indicating that neuronal electrophysiology and network communication are coordinated at least in part through neuronal acetyl-CoA metabolism.

title: Phototrophs trade growth for defense through graded regulatory states under escalating oxidative stress
abstract: PCC 7942, we profiled steady-state growth, photophysiology, and transcription across a dissolved oxygen gradient (0-374% air saturation). Independent component analysis of these transcriptomes within a 407-sample compendium resolved 78 regulatory modules (iModulons) explaining 72.3% of variance. Growth rate followed a graded, sigmoidal dose-response, which we divide into low, moderate, and severe stress regimes (14% and 47% decline, then arrest). Stress-responsive module activities shifted across these regimes: low stress activated SufR and PerR at minimal growth cost; moderate stress modulated three RpaB states, then ManR, CopR, and Rre1; and severe stress triggered a dual-control checkpoint with a fourth RpaB state linking redox sensing to the stringent response and growth arrest. Protein oxidation, pigments, and energy transfer tracked these transitions, suggesting cells trade growth for defense through discrete regulatory states.

title: PFOS exposure and periodontitis from adolescent burden to genetic and multiomics evidence
abstract: Periodontitis can develop early in life and may be influenced by persistent environmental exposures. We integrated Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, Mendelian randomization, transcriptomics, machine learning, immune profiling, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and in vitro validation to investigate links between perfluorooctane sulfonate exposure and periodontitis. Periodontal disease burden remained substantial among individuals aged 5–20 years and varied across sociodemographic strata. Genetically predicted PFOS exposure was associated with increased periodontitis risk by inverse-variance weighted Mendelian randomization. Multi-omics analyses identified 151 shared targets enriched in immune-inflammatory pathways and prioritized a ten-gene signature with strong diagnostic discrimination. Single-cell analysis implicated migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-centered immune communication, whereas molecular modeling supported stable PFOS-STK17B interactions. PFOS exposure in human gingival fibroblasts increased expression of the ten prioritized genes. These findings connect population burden with genetic, molecular, and experimental evidence supporting immune-inflammatory mechanisms linking PFOS exposure to periodontitis.

title: Stathmin 1 regulates mitophagy and non-proliferative cellular function in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells
abstract: Abstract Stathmin 1 is a cytoplasmic phosphoprotein that regulates microtubule dynamics via promotion of microtubule catastrophe and sequestration of free tubulin heterodimers. Stathmin 1 is highly expressed in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), and overexpressed in leukemic cells, however its role in HSCs is not known. Herein, we found that loss of Stathmin 1 is associated with altered microtubule architecture in HSCs, and markedly impaired HSC function. Transcriptomic studies suggested alterations in oxidative phosphorylation in Stmn1 -/- HSCs, and further mechanistic studies revealed defective mitochondrial structure and function in the absence of Stathmin 1 with increased ROS production. Microtubules associate with mitochondria and lysosomes to facilitate autophagosome formation and mitophagy, and indeed we found that this critical mitochondrial quality control process is impaired in Stathmin 1-deficient HSCs. Finally, stimulation of autophagy improved the colony forming ability of Stmn1 -/- hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. Together, our data identify Stathmin 1 as a novel regulator of mitophagy and mitochondrial health in HSCs. Key Points The microtubule regulating protein Stathmin 1 is highly expressed in HSPCs and promotes normal microtubule architecture. Loss of Stathmin 1 in HSPCs leads to impaired autophagy with abnormal mitochondrial morphology, decreased respiratory capacity, and impaired cellular function.

title: Breast cancer burden risk attribution and productivity loss in Chinese women aged 25 to 49
abstract: Breast cancer among Chinese women aged 25-49 years has substantial clinical and societal consequences. We integrated Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates for 1990-2023 with Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2022, United Nations population projections, International Labour Organization labour-force participation, and World Bank indicators. Incident cases rose from 50,064 to 87,221, while the weighted death rate declined from 9.25 to 4.72 per 100,000. Demographic changes explained 63.0% of additional cases. In exploratory extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) analyses interpreted with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), the fasting-plasma-glucose-related population attributable fraction (PAF) ranked first in several formulations but weakened after removing age and temporal structure; the selected high-body-mass-index (BMI) PAF series was constant at zero and unrankable. Potential mortality-related productivity loss was US$6.161 billion in 2023. Status-quo projections suggested increasing incidence through 2050 with very wide uncertainty, supporting surveillance and individual-level validation rather than immediate screening policy changes.

title: Ancient Inuit dogs conform to a short-legged phenotype biomechanically advantageous for sledding
abstract: Dog-powered transport is considered a key adaptation of Indigenous populations to Arctic life, but scarce bioarchaeological evidence makes it difficult to trace the origins and early spread of this practice. We hypothesized that selection for sledding might have favored certain skeletal traits over others and approached the question from a biomechanical perspective. We constructed a biomechanical model of forces acting on the dog skeleton during traction, showing that lowering the center of mass or shifting it forward is advantageous for traction. We therefore tested whether limb bones in modern and ancient sled dogs show relative shortening consistent with biomechanical expectation. Modern sled-dog groups, including Chukotka and Greenland dogs, differed from non-sled dogs and wolves by exhibiting a short-legged phenotype consistent with the biomechanical prediction. Archaeological samples of ancient Inuit dogs from Chukotka showed that most, including three ritually buried dogs, possessed the same phenotype as modern sled dogs.

title: The carbon neutrality effect of green fiscal stimulus policy: City-level insights from the decarbonization-greenization nexus
abstract: Growing evidence from decarbonization practices suggests that carbon neutrality requires policies that curb emissions and strengthen carbon sequestration. However, the nexus of decarbonization policies on carbon reduction and carbon sequestration remains underexplored. Based on China's comprehensive fiscal policy pilot for energy conservation and emissions reduction, this study develops a decarbonization-greenization nexus efficiency indicator to measure the prefecture-level carbon neutrality effect and provides the first assessment of green fiscal stimulus policy (GFSP) from this perspective. The results show that GFSP has a positive carbon neutrality effect. Through annual and final evaluations, the policy generates discontinuous effects. By linking performance evaluation to incentive funding, GFSP enhances government and public green attention, thereby contributing to carbon neutrality. Additionally, the policy produces composite effects with new energy, national forest, and carbon trading pilots, whereas no significant composite effect is observed with the low-carbon pilot. Finally, differentiated optimization strategies are proposed for pilot cities.

title: Standing genetic variation facilitates climatic adaptation in the invasive grapevine pathogen Plasmopara viticola under demographic bottlenecks
abstract: Invasive pathogens often experience demographic bottlenecks during colonization, yet how they rapidly adapt remains unclear. Plasmopara viticola , the causal agent of grapevine downy mildew, provides a model to address this question. Using β-tubulin sequences and whole-genome data, we reconstructed its invasion history and adaptation in China. Our analyses support a North American ancestral origin of Chinese P. viticola , while demographic modeling and ABBA-BABA tests indicate historical connections between Chinese and European-related lineages, suggesting a complex invasion history. Chinese populations showed reduced genetic diversity and regional bottlenecks, with the low-latitude population showing the most pronounced reduction in effective population size. Despite these constraints, candidate adaptive variants were frequently retained as polymorphisms in other populations and occurred at relatively high frequencies, supporting an important role for selection on pre-existing genetic variation during climatic adaptation. These findings highlight how invasive pathogens can retain adaptive potential despite severe founder effects.

title: β motifs and molecular flux promote fibril growth at condensate interfaces
abstract: Biomolecular condensates are increasingly implicated as intermediates in the formation of pathological amyloid assemblies, yet the mechanisms by which sequence-encoded structural motifs and non-equilibrium molecular transport cooperate at condensate interfaces remain incompletely understood. Here, we introduce Flux-Driven Molecular Dynamics (FD-MD), a simulation framework that combines sequence-encoded β -prone interactions with sustained molecular influx to examine fibril formation at condensate interfaces. Within this framework, we establish three main results. First, a scaling analysis of orientational entropy suggests that condensate interfaces can enhance nucleation relative to the bulk by as much as two orders of magnitude, by reducing the entropic cost of coalignment of rigid β -prone segments. Second, varying segment rigidity and molecular supply rate organizes a non-equilibrium phase diagram with four interfacial growth morphologies, ranging from uniform wetting to fibrillar protrusions and inter-condensate bridging networks. Third, directional fibril elongation displays an inverse relationship with drift velocity, consistent with a mechanism in which higher transport rates to the interface favor planar saturation over directed tip incorporation. Together, these results support a picture in which condensate interfaces can act as kinetically favorable nucleation environments, sequence-encoded rigidity helps determine whether interfaces remain liquid-like or become fibrillar, and molecular flux emerges as an additional control axis in the model for condensate aging trajectories.

title: The smooth muscle titin filament system regulates uterus contractility and implantation
abstract: Coordinated uterine peristalsis positions embryos for implantation, but the mechanotransduction pathways controlling uterine wave coordination are not well defined. We combined smooth-muscle-specific deletion of titin M-band exons 1 and 2 with vertical agarose gel electrophoresis, mass spectrometry, uterine ring myography, imaging, transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, and targeted immunoblotting. We show that the myometrium expresses smooth-muscle titin and low-abundance full-length titin including the M-band kinase region. Conditional M-band deletion increased oxytocin-evoked force and area-under-the-curve while reducing coordinated wall motion, yielding fewer as well as crowded/mislocalized implantation sites and heavier placentas. Proteomics and immunoblotting identified disruption of an NBR1/p62 autophagy hub with downstream remodeling of excitability, metabolism, and wall mechanics. Reduced telokin and MLCK levels are consistent with impaired relaxation and increased Ca 2+ -sensitization. Together, these findings establish the titin M-band as a mechanotransductive signaling hub regulating peri-implantation motility with potential clinical relevance for optimizing implantation after in vitro fertilization and preventing ectopic pregnancy.

title: Circadian misalignment associates with inflammation, gut barrier, and microbiome composition in humans with obesity
abstract: Circadian disruption has been linked to metabolic syndrome, but the biological links between circadian phenotypes and metabolic inflammation in humans remain incompletely characterized. We analyzed 87 adults with obesity from a randomized clinical trial to examine whether gut microbiome features and intestinal permeability relate to circadian misalignment and metabolic inflammation. Circadian phenotype was assessed using chronotype and meal timing, metabolic inflammation through a composite score of multiple biological measures, and gut permeability using sugar absorption testing. Late chronotype was associated with greater metabolic syndrome burden, while circadian misalignment was associated with increased gut permeability and inflammation, an association stronger among participants with higher permeability. These patterns co-occurred with lower abundance of short-chain fatty acid-associated bacteria, and intervention-related changes in permeability corresponded with changes in these taxa. These findings link circadian phenotypes with gut barrier and microbial features relevant to metabolic risk in obesity.

title: Circulating tumor DNA in body fluids for molecular characterization of cancers beyond tissue and blood
abstract: Liquid biopsy using circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is increasingly used for cancer profiling and monitoring, but blood-based analysis may not capture tumor heterogeneity across anatomical compartments. We evaluated cell-free DNA from cerebrospinal ( n = 7), pleural ( n = 11), pericardial ( n = 1), and ascitic ( n = 26) fluids from 45 patients with advanced cancer, comparing molecular findings with matched tissue, blood, and cytology where available. Oncogenic alterations were detected in 87% of body fluid samples, with a median variant allele frequency of 3.15%. TP53 (49%), EGFR (18%), and KRAS (18%) were the most frequently altered genes, and ESCAT tier IA alterations occurred in 31.1% of patients. In six patients (13.3%), potentially targetable alterations were detected in body fluids but not in blood and/or tissue. Among five cytology-negative samples, four were ctDNA positive. These findings support body fluid ctDNA profiling as a complementary approach to tissue, plasma, and cytology, thereby warranting prospective validation.

title: ATG16L2 as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma
abstract: Kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) carries substantial clinical challenges. This study examined ATG16L2 , an autophagy-related gene family member, across TCGA, CPTAC, GEO, and an independent cohort to assess its expression patterns, clinicopathological associations, and prognostic relevance. Immune landscapes were characterized through CIBERSORT, ESTIMATE, xCell, and single-cell analyses. Functional investigations employed shRNA-mediated knockdown in KIRC cell lines and xenograft models, with attention to the Notch signaling pathway. ATG16L2 was elevated in KIRC and associated with advanced disease and poorer survival. Its expression correlated with altered immune infiltration and immune checkpoint levels. Silencing ATG16L2 attenuated proliferative, migratory, and invasive capacities, partly through Notch pathway modulation. These findings position ATG16L2 as a prognostic indicator and immune microenvironment modulator in KIRC, with implications for therapeutic strategies targeting the ATG16L2-Notch axis.

title: Serum Olink proteomics-based exploration of novel predictive biomarkers for necrotizing enterocolitis
abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, yet reliable serum candidates for presymptomatic risk stratification remain lacking. In this exploratory study, serial pre-diagnostic serum samples from a prospective discovery cohort were profiled using the Olink proteomics platform. NEC cases and controls were individually matched for gestational age, birth weight, and sampling time. Top-ranked proteins were assessed via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in an independent validation cohort and examined in surgical intestinal tissues.
