Fibroblast growth factor 5 (FGF5) showed the highest discriminative performance with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.848. Lower circulating FGF5 levels were reproduced in the validation cohort, although the apparently perfect discrimination was imprecise because of the small sample size. Intestinal FGF5 expression was also reduced in NEC specimens. These findings support FGF5 as a promising exploratory biomarker for early NEC risk assessment, warranting larger multicenter validation and mechanistic investigation.

title: Stable truncating mutations in plakophilin-2 induce arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy-like phenotypes in adult zebrafish
abstract: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is an inherited cardiac disorder characterized by arrhythmias and fibrofatty myocardial remodeling, often leading to heart failure and sudden cardiac death. Mutations in plakophilin-2 ( PKP2 ) represent the most prevalent genetic cause of ACM. Here, we establish zebrafish ( Danio rerio ) as a complementary vertebrate model for PKP2 mutation-based ACM. Comparative single-cell RNA-seq analyses revealed distinct cardiac expression patterns of PKP2 and its homologs across species. Using CRISPR-Cas9, we generated two truncating mutations in zebrafish pkp2 , resulting in frameshifts and premature terminations (p.Glu250Glyfs∗17 and p.Glu31Glyfs∗72, respectively). Mutant zebrafish exhibited impaired cardiac contractility, arrhythmias, lipid accumulation on the ventricular surface, ultrastructural abnormalities of intercalated discs, and increased susceptibility to swimming exercise-induced sudden death. Transcriptomic analyses identified transcriptional alterations in genes involved in muscle contraction and lipid metabolism. Together, these data establish zebrafish as a useful complementary vertebrate model for studying PKP2 -based ACM and gene-environment interactions underlying disease progression.

title: Health inequalities in the global reproductive-age population: GBD 2021 trends and female-male differences, 1990–2021
abstract: Socioeconomic health inequality among reproductive-age populations remains insufficiently characterized globally. Using GBD 2021 data for individuals aged 15-49 years in 204 countries and territories, we assessed disability-adjusted life year (DALY) rates and quantified absolute and relative socioeconomic inequality using the slope index of inequality (SII) and concentration index (CI), with female-male comparisons and sensitivity analyses. In 2021, the global DALY rate was 22,377.4 per 100,000 population. From 1990 to 2021, SII changed from -17,755.23 to -13,789.27 and CI from -0.15 to -0.13. CI for communicable, maternal, neonatal, and nutritional diseases improved from -0.51 to -0.38, whereas injury CI worsened from -0.06 to -0.12. Injury SII was -824.23 in females and -2,749.96 in males. Overall socioeconomic health inequality declined but remained heterogeneous across causes and between females and males, supporting cause-specific and sex-sensitive health equity strategies.

title: EGaIn-based thermal management for high heat flux electronics
abstract: The increasing power density of modern electronic systems makes efficient thermal management essential for maintaining device performance, reliability, and operational lifetime. Among emerging thermal management materials, eutectic gallium-indium (EGaIn) has attracted attention because it uniquely combines metallic thermal conductivity with room-temperature fluidity, enabling efficient heat transfer and conformal contact with interfaces. In this review, we examine EGaIn as an adaptive thermal management platform and connect its material properties with the thermal functions they enable, their implementation in cooling systems, and the associated engineering challenges. We discuss how EGaIn enhances heat dissipation through interfacial heat transfer, liquid metal cooling, and thermally conductive composites, and review applications in batteries, high-performance electronics, electronic packaging, and flexible devices. We discuss challenges including oxidation, leakage, corrosion, electrical insulation, and long-term reliability, together with engineering strategies to address them. Finally, we provide perspectives for developing reliable EGaIn-based thermal management technologies for next-generation electronic and energy systems.

title: Hyperglycemia induces endothelial mitochondrial dysfunction and myeloperoxidase dysregulation in PCOS iPSCs
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with increased risks of cardiovascular disease (CVD), driven in part by endothelial dysfunction. Using patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), we established an endothelial model to examine cellular responses to metabolic stress independent of the complex systemic environment. We demonstrate that PCOS iPSC-derived endothelial cells (PCOS iPSC-ECs) exhibit a disease-specific susceptibility to hyperglycemia, resulting in impaired angiogenesis, mitochondrial fragmentation, and bioenergetic impairment. This stress-induced injury is accompanied by aberrant intracellular myeloperoxidase (MPO) expression. Consistent with these findings, clinical data revealed elevated systemic MPO levels in women with PCOS that correlate with diastolic blood pressure (DBP), glucose levels, and low-density lipoproteins (LDLs). Our results identify an intrinsic metabolic-oxidative defect, a latent mitochondrial vulnerability triggered by hyperglycemic stress, in the PCOS endothelium. These findings position MPO as a potential biomarker and putative mediator for cardiovascular risk stratification in PCOS.

title: Phase-dependent EEG decoding of continuous visual stimuli
abstract: Neural oscillations support cognition and perception by organizing information across oscillatory cycles. Although animal studies support this view, evidence in humans is mixed and largely based on transient stimuli. We tested whether alpha oscillations, the dominant human brain rhythm, periodically modulate the strength of visual representations. EEG was recorded while participants viewed long-lasting (2 s) Gabor patches. Using a phase-dependent decoding approach, we quantified stimulus decoding accuracy at specific alpha phases. Decoding performance varied systematically with alpha phase, following a smooth unimodal profile that peaked over occipito-parietal electrodes. These effects emerged well after stimulus onset and generalized to earlier time points, indicating a modulation of visual processing during continuous input. Our findings demonstrate that visual information is represented more accurately at specific alpha phases. This provides strong evidence that sensory processing is shaped by intrinsic brain dynamics and introduces a generalizable decoding pipeline for linking oscillatory phase to neural information processing.

title: Offensive unpredictability and defensive tracking in intergroup conflict show sex-differentiated patterns
abstract: Intergroup conflict poses asymmetric strategic demands: acquiring resources through offense benefits from behavior that opponents cannot easily anticipate, whereas protecting resources through defense requires monitoring opponents and adjusting to threats. Analyzing behavioral data from 528 adults in a real-time offense-defense game, we found that offensive and defensive success were predicted by different decision patterns. Offensive success was associated with greater within-person contribution variability, a potential source of unpredictability, whereas defensive success was associated with stronger adaptive state-tracking of opponent behavior. These strategies aligned with sex-differentiated behavioral patterns: male participants showed greater variability and performed better in offense, whereas female participants showed stronger tracking and performed better in defense. Together, these findings identify dissociable behavioral strategies to success in offense and defense, offering a behavioral framework for understanding sex-linked variation in competitive social behavior.

title: Low-cost geometry-tunable PDMS intraocular lenses fabricated using LCD 3D-printed molds for canine ophthalmic applications
abstract: This study demonstrates the feasibility of fabricating geometry-tunable polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) intraocular lens (IOL) prototypes using consumer-grade liquid crystal display (LCD) 3D-printed molds and PDMS casting. A reusable mold fabrication strategy incorporating a PMMA barrier layer successfully eliminated PDMS curing inhibition while preserving the mold geometry for repeated casting. The fabrication workflow accurately replicated a plate-haptic lens with a 6 mm optic and dimensional deviation below 1.5%, while enabling optical power to be tuned from 18 to 42 D by varying mold curvature alone. The fabricated PDMS IOLs exhibited high visible-light transparency (>95%), preliminary focusing ability, resolving power and image contrast comparable to a commercial IOL, acceptable post-treatment cytocompatibility, successful injector-assisted delivery with recovery of the original geometry, and preliminary hydrolytic stability and leachability performance. These results establish a reproducible, low-cost, and customizable fabrication platform for PDMS intraocular lenses and provide a foundation for future optimization toward customizable veterinary ophthalmic applications.

title: A systematic approach to quantitative nanoscale mass spectrometry using atomic force microscopy
abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) enables mass sensing through resonance-frequency changes of microcantilevers, but quantitative measurements can be affected by calibration and environmental factors. Here, we investigated whether a calibrated AFM cantilever and controlled mass loading could provide nanogram-scale mass estimation. Cantilevers were cleaned and calibrated by force-distance measurements, and resonance acquisition parameters were optimized under ambient conditions. UV-curable resin droplets were locally deposited on the cantilever to generate mass loading, and resonance-frequency shifts were measured and analyzed using a mass-spring model and finite-element simulations. Increasing resin mass produced progressive decreases in resonance frequency, demonstrating a consistent relationship between mass loading and cantilever resonance behavior. Finite-element simulations reproduced the resonance responses and supported the mass estimates obtained from the experimental measurements. These findings establish a calibration and modeling framework for resonance-based mass quantification using conventional AFM cantilevers and provide a basis for extending quantitative mass analysis to microstructures and biological assemblies.

title: Ancient somatosensory circuit architectures employ flexible molecular strategies
abstract: Summary The extent to which conserved neural circuit architectures depend on shared molecular specification programs remains unclear. Here, we address this question by examining the somatosensory system of the little skate, Leucoraja erinacea , an early-diverging vertebrate that retains ancestral features of both finned and limb-based body plans. We show that core features of somatosensory circuit organization, including laminar organization of the spinal cord and dorsally restricted targeting of sensory afferents, are deeply conserved. Unexpectedly, the molecular programs specifying dorsal root ganglion (DRG) sensory subtypes diverge extensively from those of mammals. Although DRG neuron subtype specification and spinal connectivity rely on target-derived cues, skates employ distinct neurotrophin receptor and transcription factor identity codes. These findings support a model in which conserved spinal circuit architectures provide a stable scaffold that leverages flexible sensory neuron specification programs, enabling the evolutionary diversification of vertebrate somatosensory systems.

title: Short-term indoor fine particulate matter exposure impedes cognitive performance and autonomic nervous system in adults
abstract: Evidence suggests short-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) air pollution can impact health, yet its wider cognitive effects and underlying mechanisms are unknown. In this randomized single-blind crossover lab-based study, 90 working-age adults were exposed to two stable indoor PM2.5 conditions generated by candle-burning: low concentration (1.70 μg/m 3 , representing clean air) achieved via an air purifier, and high concentration (31.22 μg/m 3 , representing global average exposure) using a sham filter in the purifier. Participants' cognitive performance across various domains was assessed, alongside heart rate variability (HRV) and electrodermal activity (EDA) to appraise potential mediating mechanisms of autonomic nervous activity on cognition. Higher PM2.5 exposure resulted in lower HRV and poorer cognitive performance in attention and memory, but not in coordination or reasoning. Decreased HRV partly mediated declines in some cognitive functions. The findings could have broader implications for workforce productivity beyond direct effects on ill health.

title: Core needle biopsy-derived breast cancer microtumors enable functional drug-response testing for precision oncology
abstract: To predict neoadjuvant chemotherapeutic outcomes, breast cancer organoids have been developed. However, low yields from small tissue specimens and the high cost of niche factor-enriched medium remain barriers to clinical translation. Here, breast cancer patient-derived microtumors (PDMs) from core needle biopsies and small tissue specimens were established using a modified culture protocol and an optimized fetal bovine serum (FBS)-based culture medium, achieving a 75% success rate (6 of 8 cases). PDM characteristics mostly agreed with the tissue origins, according to growth evaluation, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and genetic profiling. As a proof of concept, PDMs were tested with neoadjuvant chemotherapy alongside the patients' treatment. Notably, the PDM results were positively correlated with the patient outcomes and were obtained within a clinically relevant time frame (∼2-3 weeks). Collectively, our protocol and FBS-based medium efficiently generate breast cancer PDMs from core needle biopsies and small tissue specimens, with promising potential to guide neoadjuvant chemotherapy decisions.

title: Automated evaluation of basketball skills using multimodal data fusion for improving shooting training efficiency
abstract: Reliable basketball shooting assessment requires integration of complementary movement signals and actionable feedback. This study developed the multimodal shooting evaluation and efficiency model (MSEEM) and evaluated it in 156 players assigned to MSEEM feedback or standard coaching. RGB video, pose, inertial measurement unit signals, ball trajectories, and shot outcomes were fused to estimate rubric-based total and component scores. MSEEM achieved lower mean absolute error (4.82 ± 0.31) and stronger rank agreement ( ρ = 0.824) than SlowFast (6.24 ± 0.41; ρ = 0.702). MSEEM feedback also produced steeper training improvement and higher 14-day retention ( d = 0.68), supporting standardized component-targeted feedback.

title: Design and validation of a GMP-compliant manufacturing platform of extracellular vesicles from mesenchymal stromal cells
abstract: There is growing interest in mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) as key components in the development of next-generation regenerative cell-free therapies; however, their clinical translation remains limited by a lack of validated clinical-grade manufacturing platforms. Thus, we have established a good manufacturing practice (GMP)-compliant, semi-automated, mid-scale manufacturing workflow that couples the single-use stirred-tank bioreactor expansion of Wharton's jelly-derived MSCs with tangential flow filtration and automated size-exclusion chromatography, featuring in-line monitoring of critical process parameters. The MSC-EV-based product meets pre-specified critical quality attributes (CQAs), co-expresses parental-cell- and EV-specific markers, and complies with standardized quality and safety regulations. Moreover, the final product CQAs-including CD73-associated immunomodulatory activity-remained within acceptable limits for 12 months of storage in PlasmaLyte 148 at -80°C. Overall, our integrated platform yields MSC-EVs with high batch-to-batch reproducibility, in alignment with current GMP and regulatory standards, thereby providing a robust foundation supporting their potential clinical applicability.

title: An experimental study on HRM combined with multiplex PCR for the identification of single and mixed diatom species
abstract: Diatoms are research subjects in both ecological environments and forensic science. The identification of mixed diatom samples has always been a challenging issue. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction-high-resolution melting (PCR-HRM) provides a potential solution, but the effectiveness of this method in analyzing single and mixed diatom samples remains unclear. This study focuses on eight species of marine diatoms, identifying and designing corresponding primers to preliminarily explore the HRM technique combined with multiplex PCR for species identification of marine diatoms. By using two primer combinations, we achieved rapid identification of single diatoms. The experiments revealed that the HRM technique showed reduced identification capability for mixed diatom samples, whereas the multiplex PCR-HRM technique could enhance the identification accuracy for mixed diatom samples. By using a mixture of three primers, we identified four species of diatoms in mixed samples. This method can improve the identification capability of mixed diatom samples and provides a new approach for diatom species identification.

title: Migraine burden inequities and 2050 projections in Africa based on global burden of disease 2023
abstract: This study analyzes migraine burden and health inequalities across 53 African Union countries from 1990 to 2023 using Global Burden of Disease data, with projections to 2050. Inequality was quantified via the slope index of inequality, health system efficiency via stochastic frontier analysis, and future trends via Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average modeling. In 2023, prevalent cases reached 180.4 million (95% uncertainty interval [UI]: 152.2-211.3), disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) 6.1 million (95% UI: 4.1-8.5), with an age-standardized prevalence rate of 13,385.8 per 100,000. From 1990 to 2023, rates increased steadily (estimated annual percentage change: 0.16 for prevalence; 0.18 for DALYs). The burden peaks in young adults and women, with widening regional disparities. Cases are projected to nearly to 375.7 million by 2050. These findings establish migraine as an escalating public health priority in Africa, underscoring the urgent need for targeted policy interventions and health system strengthening across the continent.

title: Bridging soil resistome and clinical inference: A four-tier evidentiary framework
abstract: Soils support a varied range of microbial communities and are important repositories of antimicrobial resistance genes. Sequence-based techniques, such as quantitative polymerase chain reaction and shotgun metagenomics, have substantially aided soil-resistome cataloging. Nevertheless, discovery alone does not indicate activity, transferability, exposure, or clinical relevance. This review contends that better clinical inference requires tying presence-based signals to function, mobility, and exposure routes, rather than just increasing survey volume. We offer a four-tiered evidentiary paradigm that distinguishes between detection, functional or expression-based evidence, mobile genetic element context, and exposure-linked evidence in environmental, animal, and human compartments. Because activity, mobility, and cross-compartmental similarity support several claims, layered, claim-aligned approaches are required for careful One Health interpretation.

title: Intestinal microbiota-associated LysoPC(16:0) promotes endometriosis via PPARγ-mediated M2 macrophage polarization and IL-10 secretion
abstract: Both gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered pelvic immune microenvironment have been linked to endometriosis (EM), but the metabolites connecting the two remain undefined. Combining 16S rDNA sequencing with non-targeted metabolomics in a murine EM model, we found altered gut microbiota composition alongside a marked rise in peritoneal lysophosphatidylcholine (LysoPC(16:0)), linked to the microbiota shift by correlation analysis and fecal transplantation. LysoPC(16:0) promoted M2 macrophage polarization through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ), an effect observed in two mouse strains. Clodronate-mediated macrophage depletion blocked LysoPC(16:0)-driven lesion growth. LysoPC(16:0) further induced PPARγ-dependent IL-10 transcription, and IL-10 neutralization in vivo reduced lesion weight. Conditioned medium from LysoPC(16:0)-stimulated THP-1 macrophages promoted migration of primary endometrial stromal cells from patients with EM, an effect reversed by GW9662 or IL-10 neutralization. Together, these results outline a gut microbiota-LysoPC(16:0)-PPARγ-M2-IL-10 axis in EM pathogenesis, a mechanistic and therapeutic target for future clinical study.

title: Negative regulation of TH17-mediated inflammation by the nuclear receptor REV-ERBβ
abstract: SUMMARY T H 17 cells play a central role in several human autoimmune diseases. We and others reported the nuclear receptor, REV-ERBα, as a cell-intrinsic repressor of T H 17-mediated pathogenicity. REV-ERBβ, REV-ERBα’s closely related family member, is thought to be functionally redundant to REV-ERBα, which we sought to explore in T H 17-mediated immunity. Our data indicate that deletion of REV-ERBβ enhances T H 17-mediated pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and exacerbated disease in mouse models of multiple sclerosis and colitis. RNA-sequencing indicates REV-ERBβ and REV-ERBα do not have similar transcriptional profiles. REV-ERBβ does not appear to regulate gene expression through interaction with the classic co-repressor NCoR1, which is in contrast to REV-ERBα in T H 17 cells, nor does it utilize heme, its known endogenous ligand for its repressive functions. Our results establish that while REV-ERBβ also acts as a negative regulator of T H 17-cell function and pathogenicity, it does so in a manner that is non-redundant, independent, and unique to REV-ERBα.

title: Habitat informed 3D deep learning predicts immunochemotherapy response in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: Immunochemotherapy (ICT) is a critical treatment for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), yet predicting individual response remains challenging. We developed a three-channel 3D deep learning framework integrating tumor habitat analysis for predicting ICT response. In this multicenter retrospective study of 277 patients, voxel-level clustering of pretreatment CT images segmented tumors into habitat subregions reflecting microenvironmental heterogeneity. A ResNet-50 model incorporating habitat maps, cropped tumor images, and ROI masks achieved an AUC of 0.927 (95% CI, 0.850–0.951) in the independent external test cohort, compared with 0.869 for habitat radiomics (DeLong p = 0.343). SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified texture features, particularly gray-level co-occurrence matrix correlation in habitat 3, as the primary contributors. This framework provides a noninvasive approach for predicting ICT response in LA-ESCC.

title: NOSE-OE: A molecular signaling map of the olfactory epithelium
abstract: The olfactory epithelium (OE) is a dynamic and complex sensory tissue in which continuous regeneration, neuronal differentiation, and tissue maintenance depend on coordinated molecular and cellular signaling. We developed NOSE-OE (Network of Signaling Events in the Olfactory Epithelium), an open-access knowledge resource that integrates mechanistic evidence from more than 300 publications into a standardized, computer-readable signaling network. NOSE-OE comprises over 500 molecular elements and 1,000 curated interactions and is implemented within the MINERVA platform for interactive exploration and network analysis. By connecting fragmented experimental evidence within a unified molecular framework, NOSE-OE enables the systematic investigation of signaling processes governing OE homeostasis and responses to perturbation. The resource provides a foundation for hypothesis generation and systems-level investigation of olfactory epithelial biology across physiological and disease contexts.

title: Knifefish-inspired robotic fish enhances locomotion performance by undulatory anal fin propulsion and flexible body
abstract: Complex underwater terrains require robots that can maneuver efficiently through confined, vegetation-rich spaces while minimizing hydrodynamic disturbance. Inspired by the black ghost knifefish, we developed Naiad, a bio-inspired robotic fish that combines a flexible body with a servo-actuated anal fin. Coordinated body deformation and undulatory ribbon-fin propulsion enabled forward and reverse swimming, turning, and vertical maneuvering. In experiments, Naiad reached 0.20 body lengths per second (BL/s) and a minimum cost of transport (COT) of 3.42. It also achieved a maximum turning rate of 23.67°/s (0.41 rad/s) and a minimum turning radius of 0.31 body lengths (BL). Demonstrations in a confined obstacle-rich channel and an outdoor lake further showed multi-gait maneuverability under aquatic conditions. These results demonstrate that integrating body flexibility with undulatory fin propulsion enhances locomotor versatility. This approach provides a design strategy for agile underwater robots in confined environments and supports applications in exploration and environmental monitoring.

title: Proteomic and extracellular particle changes in preterm neonates with suspected late-onset sepsis
abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality in neonates. In this prospective, multisite observational study, proteomics and extracellular particle analysis were performed on platelet-poor plasma from neonates at the point of clinical suspicion for sepsis ( n = 110). Neonates were then classified by their clinical teams into three groups: culture-proven sepsis, culture-negative sepsis, or non-sepsis. Neonates with culture-proven sepsis demonstrated statistically significant differences in their analyzed proteome compared to neonates deemed to have non-sepsis, while those with culture-negative sepsis did not. Extracellular particle concentration and type, as determined by flow cytometry, did not differ between the three groups. This study provides further evidence that culture-proven sepsis and culture-negative sepsis are not equivalent diagnoses in the neonatal population without a consensus definition for sepsis. The proteins identified in the culture-positive group may be of utility in determining neonatal sepsis endotypes, but this would require further validation.

title: Antibiotic resistance genes in aquaculture: Molecular detection, environmental dynamics, and biological control strategies
abstract: Antibiotic resistance in aquaculture is a major threat to sustainable fish production and global public health. This review provides a comprehensive and critical synthesis of studies on antibiotic resistance in aquaculture published between 2005 and 2025, identified through a systematic and reproducible literature search. It clarifies the molecular basis of resistance, characterizes the environmental distribution of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and evaluates current and emerging control strategies in aquaculture systems. Evidence is organized into thematic domains encompassing molecular mechanisms, environmental reservoirs and drivers, diagnostic and surveillance tools, and biological alternatives to antibiotics. In parallel, vaccines, probiotics, and bacteriophage therapy show promising, context-dependent potential when embedded in multifaceted biocontrol frameworks. This review highlights priorities including protocol standardization, rapid farm-deployable diagnostics, and optimized synergistic biocontrol strategies, supported by artificial intelligence and big data analytics, to facilitate a transition from reactive treatment to preventive, system-level resistance management in aquaculture.

title: Effect of the end-of-life care education program on improving oncology nurses’ knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors: A quasi-experimental study
abstract: Education can strengthen nurses' capabilities in end-of-life care. Existing training programs have shortcomings such as monotonous content, unsatisfactory intervention effects, and limitations in research design. This single-center, quasi-experimental study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of an educational program based on the supportive care strategy list for end-of-life cancer patients in improving oncology nurses' knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors. Participants from a tertiary cancer hospital in Beijing were allocated into a training group and a non-training group (N1 = N2=27) using matched-pair sampling. The non-training group received no intervention, while the training group underwent an 18-class (45–60 min per class), 7-week education. At the 8-month follow-up, post-intervention assessments showed that the training group demonstrated significantly better knowledge and attitudes than the non-training group ( p < 0.05). Intra-group comparisons showed the training group exhibited superior knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors than at baseline ( p < 0.05). The end-of-life care education program effectively enhanced oncology nurses' knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors.

title: Epidemiological modeling of African swine fever in wild boars—A systematic review
abstract: African swine fever (ASF) is a viral disease that poses a major threat to swine production, with wild boars contributing to virus persistence and transmission. We systematically reviewed global epidemiological modeling studies published from 2014 to 2024 to assess modeling approaches, transmission pathways, methodological patterns, and factors associated with ASF occurrence and spread in wild boar populations. Fifty-four studies from twenty-nine countries were grouped into five categories based on research objectives. Risk-factor and spatiotemporal analyses were the most common approaches, supporting targeted surveillance and risk mapping. Carcass-mediated transmission, wild boar density, movement, habitat conditions, and seasonal variation were important factors influencing ASF occurrence and spread. As modeling approaches differ in their assumptions, data requirements, and applicability, we developed a framework linking model choice to surveillance capacity, outbreak stage, data availability, and management objectives. This framework provides a structured basis for selecting appropriate approaches to strengthen ASF surveillance and control strategies.

title: Senescence and tumor immunology: A multifaceted interplay of influence
abstract: Medical advances and global population aging have propelled aging and cancer research into a new period of discovery. Senescent cells, which exert context-dependent tumor-suppressive and tumor-promoting effects, are central to this progress and engage in complex crosstalk with tumor proliferation. This review critically examines the multidimensional interplay between aging and cancer by synthesizing genetic, cytokine signaling, and tissue microenvironment evidence. We discuss how senescent cells influence immune surveillance, therapy response, tumor progression, metastasis, and age-related cancer risk, while cellular diversity, molecular complexity, immune balance, tumor heterogeneity, treatment resistance, and individual aging variability further complicate this relationship. We conclude that aging and cancer are intertwined through dynamic, context-specific mechanisms. By integrating these insights, this review aims to inspire novel research directions and transformative advances in cancer therapy and healthy longevity.

title: Distinct electrophysiological correlates of low- and high-level visual consciousness with minimized post-perceptual processing
abstract: Conscious visual phenomenology comprises multiple representational levels, from basic features to integrated percepts, raising the question of how the neural correlates of consciousness (NCC) differentiate accordingly. Event-related potential (ERP) studies identified early occipitotemporal negativities as reliable NCC; yet, it remains unclear whether these capture conscious content beyond low-level features and extend to higher-order representations. Moreover, whether later ERP components index higher-level conscious percepts independent of task-related processing remains contested. The present study addresses this question using an inattentional blindness (IB) paradigm that isolates three representational levels of conscious perception (no, low- or high-level awareness) for an identical stimulus under minimized post-perceptual processing. Across 85 healthy participants, low-level line perception was indexed by an enhanced early occipital negativity, whereas high-level face perception additionally recruited a right-lateralized occipitotemporal negativity, followed by medial posterior positivities. These findings reveal systematic spatiotemporal differentiation of awareness-related potentials across representational levels of consciousness under task-irrelevant conditions.

title: Longitudinal associations of screen time with brain development and expressive language skills in early childhood
abstract: Screen-based media may reduce reciprocal social interactions that support expressive language development, but little is known about how early language abilities, later screen use, and brain structure are related during toddlerhood. We examined 70 toddlers with structural magnetic resonance imaging and standardized developmental assessments at age 2, along with parent-reported screen time at ages 2 and 3. Greater weekday and weekend screen time at age 2 were associated with poorer concurrent expressive language skills. Right pars triangularis volume did not explain additional variance in these cross-sectional associations. Longitudinally, right pars triangularis volume moderated the association between expressive language skills at age 2 and screen time at age 3. Among toddlers with relatively smaller right pars triangularis volumes, poorer expressive language skills were associated with greater subsequent weekday and weekend screen time. These findings support guidance to limit screen use during toddlerhood, a sensitive window for language and brain development.

title: Paleogenomics reveals leprosy at the late antique burial site of Fallward in northern Germany
abstract: The coastal settlement of Fallward in northwestern Germany (3 rd –5 th century CE) is renowned for exceptionally preserved wooden and textile grave goods, yet the genetic and pathogen landscape of its inhabitants has remained unstudied. We conducted metagenomic analyses on skeletal samples from 11 individuals to investigate their genetic affinities and infectious disease history. Three individuals yielded sufficient data for population genetic analysis: two clustered with northwestern European Iron Age and Anglo-Saxon groups, while one adult male might have originated from a Roman frontier population. This man was also infected with a strain of Mycobacterium leprae belonging to phylogenetic branch 4 and was buried in a boat accompanied by Roman-influenced grave goods, including carved furniture and a military belt. Together, these findings point to possible long-distance connections linking remote communities, such as Fallward, to the wider Roman world during Late Antiquity.

title: A hierarchical framework of representational emergence: From feature binding to supramodal emergence
abstract: Multisensory integration is traditionally conceptualized as transient, stimulus-driven feature binding. Here, we propose a hierarchical framework that reconceptualizes multisensory processing as a continuum of representational emergence across three distinct levels: level I (multimodal binding), where features are integrated via probabilistic causal inference; level II (supramodal representation), where recurrent co-activation and value-guided selection establish consolidated, perceptual-semantic engrams that act as emergent modalities; and level III (amodal concepts), where meaning becomes increasingly detached from sensory form and is represented within transmodal semantic networks. Drawing on recent mammalian evidence for cross-modal associative memory neurons and experience-dependent network reorganization, this framework proposes how local synaptic selection may scale into increasingly autonomous cognitive modules. Finally, we delineate an empirical roadmap and outline implications for supramodal AI, toward architectures capable of more autonomous semantic representation and generation.

title: Rapid screening of ancient DNA extracts through uracil detection
abstract: Paleogenetic studies provide invaluable insights into past populations. However, the success of ancient DNA retrieval remains difficult to predict. Ancient DNA workflows are time consuming and costly, motivating methods to assess preservation at an early stage. One defining molecular feature of ancient DNA is the accumulation of uracil residues through postmortem cytosine deamination. Here, we leverage a uracil-DNA-specific labeling assay, originally developed for modern DNA, to evaluate whether extracts contain ancient DNA molecules. The assay, which requires only two days to complete, quantifies uracil residues using a uracil-DNA-binding protein and antibody-based labeling. After demonstrating reliable immobilization of short DNA fragments, we applied the assay to twenty archaeological samples spanning diverse contexts. Extracts with the highest inferred uracil contents were more likely to contain ancient DNA, whereas the lowest-ranked extracts were consistently negative. This assay may facilitate early prioritization of promising extracts and deprioritization of samples unlikely to yield informative sequencing data.

title: Evidence for climate-mediated range expansion of hybrid wood ants
abstract: Climate change challenges many species. To persist, species can shift ranges, respond plastically, and adapt, which all require variation. Hybridization can quickly increase genetic variation, potentially facilitating climate adaptation; however, it is unclear how hybrids respond to climatic changes. Here, we combine whole-genome, life-history, acute heat-shock, and climatic data of 69 wood ant populations across Finland to assess whether F. aquilonia × F. polyctena hybrids outperform their cold-adapted parent F. aquilonia in warming climates. Compared to F. aquilonia , hybrids are active and their offspring emerge earlier in spring, and they withstand acute temperatures relevant in nature better. Further, the hybrids' border has shifted 200 km northwards, coinciding with the expansion of climatic conditions suitable for hybrids. Our results provide evidence that hybrids have an adaptive advantage over F. aquilonia due to their admixed ancestry, and recent climatic changes can lead to range expansion of hybrids.

title: A machine learning classifier reveals hidden rare biallelic heterozygous variants in the coding regions of Meniere disease genome
abstract: Meniere disease (MD) is a rare inner ear disorder with a significant genetic contribution. We developed the MD classifier, an ML tool to distinguish familial from sporadic MD cases using rare variants in coding regions. We have generated a disease-specific gene variant score incorporating gene, variant, and disease-specific features. A gradient boosting classifier achieved the highest performance, with a test AUC of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.702-0.948) and an accuracy of 81.5%. Reclassification of sporadic cases into the familial group ranged from 16.6% to 28.3%. The model identified a burden of biallelic heterozygous variants suggesting hidden recessive inheritance that may affect up to 38% of MD patients. Gene-enrichment analysis using major classifier features revealed distinct biological pathways between familial and sporadic MD. This ML-based framework integrates unique genetic features that may improve the diagnostic yield of rare disorders and is universally applicable to conditions with both familial and sporadic phenotypes, enabling the identification of compound heterozygous recessive inheritance.

title: Cortical substrates of perceptual confusion between pitch and timbre
abstract: Pitch and timbre are two fundamental perceptual attributes of sound that help us distinguish voices in speech and appreciate music. Brightness, one of the primary dimensions of timbre, is governed by different acoustic parameters compared to pitch, but the two can be confused perceptually when varied simultaneously. Here we combine human behavior and fMRI to provide evidence of a potential neural substrate to explain this important but poorly understood perceptual confusion. We identify orderly mappings of both pitch and brightness within auditory cortex and reveal two independent lines of evidence for cortical confusion between them. First, the preferred pitch of individual voxels decreases systematically as brightness increases, and vice versa, consistent with predictions based on perceptual confusion. Second, pitch and brightness mapping share a common high-low-high gradient across auditory cortex, implying a shared trajectory of cortical activation for changes in each dimension. The results provide a cortical substrate at both local and global scales for an established auditory perceptual phenomenon that is thought to reflect efficient coding of features ubiquitous in natural sound statistics.

title: Biomechanics-guided computational design of virtual terrestrial vertebrate morphogenesis
abstract: To date, experimental development biology still faces challenges to efficiently model the morphogenesis of cross-species vertebrates, spanning from the embryonic development to postnatal growth. No effective computational methods are yet available to reproduce this complex and long-term process. However, recent advancements in large-scale computation and multi-voxel assembly theory have created unprecedented opportunities for establishing a virtual platform to simulate these morphomechanical processes. In this context, we propose a spatiotemporal topological evolution (STTE) method that can investigate the morphogenesis and postnatal growth of three-dimensional multi-voxel virtual embryoids. In this model, the optimization goal is to achieve extensive motion capabilities for the heads of virtual organisms in the vertical direction, thereby facilitating the formation and maintenance of conserved morphological structures characteristic of vertebrates. This proposed theory can rapidly and massively generate digital vertebrates with diverse adult body shapes, and this virtual morphogenesis pipeline offers novel perspectives and technologies for developmental biology.

title: Condensin upregulation induces intestinal stem cell senescence, driving cell death and increased intestinal permeability
abstract: Intestinal stem cell maintenance ensures the integrity of the continuously renewing intestinal barrier, promotes repair, and prevents immune cell activation in the underlying tissue. Intestinal barrier defects contribute to the development of Crohn's disease (CD), a type of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We show that expression of subunits of the genome-organizing complexes, condensins, is upregulated in intestinal epithelial cells of patients with ileal CD. Using cultured intestinal epithelial cell lines and the in vivo model of Drosophila melanogaster , we show that overexpression of condensin proteins rearranges heterochromatin and induces senescence of intestinal stem cells, which leads to cell death in both stem and non-stem cells. In Drosophila , this increases intestinal permeability. These findings suggest that restriction of condensin expression maintains ileal stem cell homeostasis, providing support for future mechanistic exploration of pathologic roles for condensins and senescent stem cells in CD and other diseases involving intestinal barrier dysfunction.

title: Distinct neural oscillatory patterns underlying music-evoked emotions: Evidence from MEG and subjective reports
abstract: Music has a powerful capacity to evoke emotional responses. This study explored the neural and subjective correlates of pleasant and unpleasant emotions elicited by music. 30 volunteers (15 women) listened to 60 film musical excerpts (30 unpleasant and 30 pleasant) from the Film Music Stimulus Set (FMSS) while their neural activity was recorded using magnetoencephalography (MEG). Participants gave self-reports of hedonic valence, emotional arousal, happiness, fear, and musical preference on nine-point Likert scales. Results showed that pleasant music was evaluated as more pleasant, happier, and preferred compared to unpleasant music, which was rated as more arousing and as evoking higher levels of fear. Neural activity revealed greater source-level oscillatory power for pleasant music in theta and beta frequency bands, with distinct regional patterns in the brain. These findings enhance understanding of music-induced emotions and suggest potential clinical applications for treating mood disorders and emotional dysregulation.

title: Low-frequency parasitized cells in bone marrow alter myelopoiesis following immunization with the live attenuated Leishmania major Cen−/− vaccine
abstract: Leishmaniasis lacks an effective vaccine. We developed a live-attenuated Leishmania major Centrin-deficient strain ( LmCen −/− ) that is safe and protective in murine and canine models through IFN-γ-producing effector T cells. Because persistent low-level infection supports durable immunity, we investigated latent parasites and immune remodeling in the bone marrow. Dual single-cell RNA sequencing detected parasitized bone marrow cells 28 days after intradermal inoculation with either virulent LmWT or attenuated LmCen −/− . Flow cytometry showed increased myelopoiesis following LmCen −/− immunization compared with LmWT infection. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated enhanced granulin-Sort3 signaling as a potential driver of this response. Bone marrow monocytes from LmCen −/− -immunized mice efficiently cleared virulent LmWT parasites in co-culture, consistent with the induction of trained innate immunity. These findings identify the bone marrow as an active site of anti- Leishmania immune programming and suggest that LmCen −/− vaccination promotes durable protection through coordinated adaptive and innate mechanisms.

title: Single-cell-resolved dynamic immune remodeling following Omicron infection and recovery in vaccinated individuals
abstract: Breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 Omicron infections occur despite vaccination, yet post-infection immune recovery remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and targeted proteomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy individuals and vaccinated patients during infection, early recovery, and 3-month post-recovery. Omicron infection induced coordinated immune remodeling with contraction of T and B cell compartments; expansion of plasma, regulatory T, and dendritic cells; and suppression of inflammatory and metabolic pathways, including TNFα-NF-κB and mTORC1 signaling. Innate populations rebounded rapidly, whereas adaptive compartments recovered slowly with sustained suppression of IL-2 , IL-12 , and IL-15 modules. Chemokine surges ( CXCL1 , CXCL5 , and CXCL8 ) resolved during convalescence, whereas selective cytokines ( CCL5 and CCL8 ) and interleukins ( IL-6 , IL-18 , and IL-24 ) persisted. Trajectory analysis revealed non-uniform remodeling of T cell states with persistent differentiation signatures across naive, effector, and memory compartments. Overall, vaccination tempered early immune collapse and accelerated innate rebound, highlighting interleukin-linked checkpoints and metabolic regulation underlying post-vaccination immune resilience.

title: Avoiding spiders: Affective context shapes tactile sensitivity during movement
abstract: Tactile sensitivity is typically reduced during voluntary movements, a phenomenon known as tactile suppression. While affective context is known to modulate tactile processing, it remains unclear how it influences tactile suppression. In a virtual reality (VR) environment, we investigated tactile sensitivity during movements to avoid threatening (spider) or approach non-threatening (rabbit) stimulus, involving arm flexion or extension and during the limb at rest (baseline). Tactile sensitivity was measured using brief vibrations delivered through the VR controller. Detection thresholds were higher during movement than at baseline, confirming tactile suppression. Both affective context and movement type modulated suppression: avoiding threatening stimulus and extending the arm, each increased suppression. A control experiment using neutral, geometric objects showed similar tactile sensitivity for arm extension and flexion. These findings demonstrate that affective context shapes tactile suppression during movement.

title: Deep TMS modulates neurovascular responses and enhances dual-task computation in healthy adults
abstract: Dual-task performance requires coordination between cognitive control and motor systems. This study examined how deep transcranial magnetic stimulation (DTMS) influences cortical responses and computational performance during dual-task processing. In a randomized crossover study, 19 healthy adults underwent DTMS targeting the bilateral prefrontal cortex and anterior cingulate cortex and sham stimulation in separate sessions, with functional near-infrared spectroscopy and dual-task assessments performed before and after each intervention. Compared with sham stimulation, DTMS increased task-related cortical activation in regions involved in cognitive-motor processing and improved computation number without affecting accuracy. Activation changes involving the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, secondary motor cortex, and language-related regions were associated with dual-task performance. These findings suggest that DTMS may modulate distributed cortical dynamics supporting cognitive-motor coordination and inform its potential application in populations with cognitive-motor impairments.

title: Epigenetic age acceleration enhances prediction of overall survival in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer
abstract: Epigenetic age, influenced by environmental factors like smoking, predicts mortality in general populations but remains under-explored in early-stage lung cancer. We analyzed blood DNA methylation from 75 Boston Lung Cancer Study participants with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), of whom 63 died during follow-up. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was estimated using Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, and GrimAge2 clocks and assessed using Cox models and random survival forests (RSFs). Across clocks, EAA significantly predicted survival in early-stage NSCLC. GrimAge2 EAA achieved the highest predictive accuracy (C index = 0.73±0.04) and emerged as the dominant predictor of survival among RSF models (variable importance = 5.7%), surpassing smoking and age. GrimAge2 EAA showed a non-linear association with mortality in which current smokers had >10% higher predicted mortality risk than former or never smokers at equivalent EAA, a pattern confirmed in Kaplan-Meier analyses. GrimAge2 EAA is a promising biomarker for personalizing risk stratification alongside traditional clinical factors.

title: Single-cell dissection of self-derived versus donor-derived T cell exhaustion niches in patients with acute myeloid leukemia
abstract: Relapse remains the main cause of death in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and T cell exhaustion is related to relapse in both non-allografting and allografting settings. However, differences in exhausted T cells (T ex ) across different disease contexts remain incompletely understood. We performed single-cell RNA and T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing to systematically characterize T ex in AML. Both self-derived T ex in non-transplantation and donor-derived T ex in post-transplant settings express similar surface markers, but NFATC1/NFATC3 with downstream TOX and EOMES are enriched in self-derived T ex , while NFATC2 with downstream NR4A2 predominates in donor-derived T ex . Both self-derived and donor-derived bone marrow environments are enriched with immunosuppressive monocytes, dendritic cells, and regulatory T cells. Cell-cell interaction analysis reveals strong direct and indirect interactions between T ex and AML cells, primarily mediated by galectin-9, MIF, and TGF-β1. These findings highlight differences and commonalities between self-derived and donor-derived T ex and identify potential therapeutic targets for reversing T ex in AML.

title: GClnc1 as an emerging oncogenic regulator with mechanistic insights and clinical implications in human cancers
abstract: Gastric cancer-related long non-coding RNA1 ( GClnc1 ) is an emerging oncogenic regulator in multiple malignancies, including gastric, colorectal, ovarian, and bladder cancers, as well as osteosarcoma. It promotes proliferation, inhibits apoptosis, and enhances drug resistance and metastasis. Mechanistically, GClnc1 dysregulates key cancer-related regulators and pathways, such as p53, MYC, NF-κB, and the SIRT3/SOD2 axis. Clinically, GClnc1 shows diagnostic and prognostic potential across cancers, with aberrant expression in tissues and altered circulating levels. Notably, exosomal GClnc1 serves as a circulating biomarker for early gastric cancer detection and predicts response to fluorouracil-based chemotherapy. This review summarizes current evidence on GClnc1 's regulatory mechanisms and discusses its translational applications. GClnc1 may serve as a multi-cancer biomarker and a promising therapeutic target.

title: Enhancing cervical squamous cell carcinoma diagnosis under distribution shift via domain-adaptive representation learning
abstract: Automated whole-slide image (WSI) analysis for cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) is challenged by limited pathological specificity in general models and poor cross-center generalization. We propose CSCC-PAG (pre-training, adaptation, generalization), a framework integrating domain-specific pre-training with self-supervised domain adaptation. Utilizing 8,041 CSCC WSIs, we applied the self-supervised pre-training for CSCC (SPC) feature extractor, which significantly outperforms pan-cancer baselines in the typing, grading, and segmentation tasks. To address domain shift, we developed representative sample domain adaptation (RSDA), combining masked autoencoders (MAEs) with a k -means buffer strategy for label-free adaptation. The results demonstrate that SPC captures fine-grained CSCC morphology, while RSDA effectively recovers performance degradation across centers without requiring target-domain annotations. This study provides a comprehensive solution for automated CSCC diagnosis, covering the entire pipeline from large-scale pre-training to few-shot generalized deployment, demonstrating its immense potential for real-world clinical implementation.

title: Microbiome-dependent phytosterol sulfates production and tissue distribution in mice
abstract: Microbial biotransformation of dietary lipids, such as cholesterol, influences host homeostasis. Despite extensive studies on animal sterols in host-microbiota interactions, the role of phytosterols in homeostasis remains unclear. In this study, we characterized phytosterol sulfates as microbiota-derived metabolites using untargeted lipidomic data mining. The levels of sitosterol sulfate (SIS), campesterol sulfate, and stigmasterol sulfate, the three major phytosterol sulfates, along with coprostanol sulfate, were reduced in the feces of germ-free mice compared with those of specific pathogen-free mice. We characterized a series of Bacteroidota species and their sterol sulfotransferases that produced phytosterol sulfates more efficiently than mammalian enzymes. Furthermore, SIS significantly accumulated in host tissues in a microbiota- and age-dependent manner, whereas unconjugated phytosterols were mostly undetectable. Our work provides insights into host-microbiome interactions via gut bacterial phytosterol metabolism.

title: Dual roles of AXIN1 as a β-catenin p-S60-dependent cytokinesis machinery and an ESCRT component
abstract: AXIN1 functions as a scaffolding protein in several signaling pathways, including TGF-β, SAPK/JNK, and Wnt; however, as there have been no reports on the function of AXIN1 in cytokinesis, we investigated this link to determine if this scaffold coordinates cell division. Here, we demonstrate that AXIN1 is located in the central dark zone of the intercellular bridge, known as the Flemming body, where it forms a midbody ring structure. We also demonstrated that AXIN1 functions in coordination with β-catenin p-S60-dependent cytokinetic machinery during early telophase. Furthermore, AXIN1 regulates the hierarchy of the ESCRT complex by positioning itself between MKLP1 and CEP55 in late telophase cells. Based on our findings, we propose that AXIN1 has dual functions in cytokinesis by facilitating ECT2 recruitment during early telophase and promoting recruitment of abscission components during late telophase, highlighting the transformative role of this signaling scaffold as structural machinery in coordinating cell division.

title: Integrative genomics and experimental validation identify a mechanosensitive gene signature associated with colorectal cancer liver metastasis
abstract: The mechanical tumor microenvironment critically influences colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastasis, yet the underlying molecular mediators remain poorly defined. By integrating single-cell transcriptomics, bulk RNA-seq, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and 117 machine learning algorithms, we identified a six-gene mechanosensitive signature ( SNX7 , SDC1 , CDCP1 , PTGES , EMP2 , and CALB2 ) associated with CRC liver metastasis. This signature demonstrated superior prognostic performance (mean C-index 0.68) across multiple independent cohorts compared to 74 published CRC signatures. Among these genes, SDC1 was consistently upregulated in CRC cells and tissues, and its expression was further induced by increased matrix stiffness in tunable hydrogel culture systems. These findings support a mechanosensitive gene signature with robust prognostic value and identify SDC1 as a stiffness-responsive candidate regulator, providing insights into the mechanobiological regulation of CRC metastasis.

title: Linking nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal microbiota to immune responses during influenza-like illness in an aging population
abstract: Older adults are vulnerable to influenza-like illness (ILI). To study how infection shapes the respiratory microbiota, we profiled nasopharyngeal (NP) and oropharyngeal (OP) communities alongside local immune mediators in adults aged 60–88, comparing asymptomatic, ILI, and recovery states. NP communities clustered into three community state types (CSTs): Moraxella -dominated (CST-1), Haemophilus/Streptococcus/Staphylococcus -associated (CST-2), and Corynebacterium/Dolosigranulum -dominated (CST-3). During infection, compositional shifts were restricted to the NP niche, where CST-1 and CST-2 were more frequent. Streptococcus, Haemophilus and Moraxella were positively associated with inflammatory and interferon-related mediators, including IL-6, CXCL9 and CXCL10, while Corynebacterium showed negative associations. Immune activation was strong in the NP but limited in the OP, and stayed above healthy levels at follow-up, suggesting incomplete recovery. NP composition was also associated with symptom burden, viral and bacterial co-detection and smoking status. These site-specific microbiota-immune relationships identify the nasopharynx as the primary site of immune modulation during ILI in older adults.

title: Wearable-derived sleep and circadian features associated with electronic health record-documented persistent postsurgical pain
abstract: A substantial percentage of surgical patients develop persistent postsurgical pain, and sleep disruption is an established, modifiable contributor. We examined temporal dynamics linking sleep and circadian rhythms to persistent postsurgical pain, using longitudinal Fitbit and electronic health record (EHR) data from the NIH All of Us Research Program to track sleep and circadian changes preceding EHR documentation of pain beyond expected surgical recovery. Patients later documented with persistent pain showed systematic shifts in wake timing and in heart rate circadian rhythms (elevated amplitude and mesor), with wake timing decoupled from heart rate circadian timing. These changes were absent in a comparison cohort without persistent pain documentation, indicating specificity to persistent postsurgical pain rather than a postoperative or clinical-encounter effect. Findings align with evidence linking altered sleep to pain outcomes and identify cardiac circadian disruption as a distinct marker, suggesting wearable-derived features could capture physiological changes before documentation and inform intervention.

title: S-adenosylmethionine ameliorates spermatogenic dysfunction and sperm DNA damage via transsulfuration pathway
abstract: Male infertility is a global concern, with high sperm DNA fragmentation linked to oxidative stress. Untargeted metabolomics in 111 men revealed downregulated S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) in patients with high sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI). In vitro experiments demonstrated that SAM supplementation effectively reduced oxidative stress-induced DNA damage of human sperm and restored motility. In vivo , SAM administration in cyclophosphamide-induced oligoasthenozoospermia mice improved testicular structure, sperm quality, and DNA integrity. SAM restored glutathione levels and upregulated the expression of key transsulfuration enzymes, cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) and cystine/glutamate transporter (xCT), thereby enhancing glutathione biosynthesis and mitigating oxidative stress. RNA sequencing and protein analysis further revealed that SAM attenuated the expression of proapoptotic markers caspase-3 and caspase-8 and reduced germ cell apoptosis. These findings suggest that SAM may alleviate spermatogenic dysfunction and DNA damage, an effect that may involve enhancement of the transsulfuration pathway and improved redox homeostasis. This offers mechanistic insights and supports further exploration of its therapeutic potential on male infertility.

title: Pharmacological AhR activation attenuates airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling in a mixed allergen asthma model
abstract: Airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling are major features of asthma. We investigated whether pharmacological activation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) modifies these responses in a mixed allergen (MA) mouse model of asthma. MA exposure increased airway resistance, contractility, inflammation, and remodeling, with elevated AhR expression in whole lung and airway smooth muscle but limited canonical AhR target gene activation. Treatment with the high-affinity AhR agonist 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) improved lung mechanics, reduced inflammatory cell and cytokine accumulation, attenuated airway remodeling, and decreased airway narrowing in precision-cut lung slices. Bulk lung RNA sequencing further showed suppression of inflammatory, neutrophil-associated, and remodeling pathways following TCDD treatment, together with induction of canonical AhR target genes. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that AhR activation suppresses inflammatory gene networks, limits airway remodeling, and improves airway mechanics in experimental asthma, supporting the therapeutic potential of targeting AhR signaling to mitigate airway dysfunction and structural remodeling.

title: Metabolic network restoration, not donor microbial engraftment, associates with resolution of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection
abstract: infection (rCDI). However, the mechanisms underpinning FMT efficacy are incompletely understood. We used proximity-ligation metagenomics, metaproteomics, and metabolomics to profile dynamic changes in rCDI. We analyzed samples collected from the first 7 responders during a clinical trial comparing two donor-based treatments (lyophilized FMT [LFMT] or lyophilized sterile fecal filtrate [LSFF], free of intact microorganisms) to prevent rCDI. LSFF is enriched in Caudoviricetes, lipids, fatty acids, and human and extracellular bacterial proteins compared with LFMT. LFMT recipients had donor microbial engraftment, while LSFF recipients achieved only partial microbial community recovery without donor's contribution. Our multi-omics analyses identified a functional convergence following both treatments, shifting away from oxidative and antibiotic stress survival pathways toward enhanced carbon-nitrogen utilization pathways, suggesting that FMT mechanisms may involve metabolic reprogramming and host-microbial amino acid co-metabolism. Our findings provide important hypothesis-generating insights that warrant further validation.

title: Similar degenerative patterns of olfactory receptor genes in the giant panda and marine carnivores
abstract: Olfactory receptor (OR) genes constitute the largest mammalian gene family and are critical for olfactory perception and ecological adaptation. OR gene variation is associated with interspecific differences in habitat, diet, and sensory reliance, yet the relative contributions of these ecological factors to OR evolution remain unclear. Here, we systematically analyzed OR repertoires across 25 carnivoran species occupying diverse niches. Marine carnivorans exhibit convergent OR degeneration, with fewer intact genes and ancestral orthologs, higher pseudogene ratios, and relaxed purifying selection compared with terrestrial species. Notably, bamboo-specialized giant pandas display identical degenerative signatures, possessing the smallest intact OR repertoire and most lost ancestral OR groups among terrestrial carnivorans. Our models show habitat primarily shapes intact OR quantity, while dietary specialization governs pseudogenization and selective constraints. These findings reveal convergent OR functional decay under aquatic adaptation and extreme dietary specialization, illustrating complex links between lifestyle and chemosensory genome evolution in mammals.

title: H3K18 lactylation promotes Treg/Th17 imbalance via PTPRM-STAT3 axis in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits elevated lactate levels and Treg/Th17 imbalance, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We found that HCC patients show increased serum lactate correlated with expanded Tregs and reduced Th17 cells. Lactate treatment promoted FOXP3 while suppressing RORγt in vitro . Western blot revealed significantly elevated histone lactylation in HCC PBMCs, with H3K18la showing the most pronounced increase. Genome-wide H3K18la profiling by CUT&Tag identified global epigenetic reprogramming at immune-related loci. Integrating epigenomic and transcriptomic data revealed PTPRM as a key gene with enhanced H3K18la enrichment and elevated expression. H3K18la enrichment at the PTPRM locus was significantly increased in HCC samples compared with controls, whereas treatment with the LDHA inhibitor oxamate markedly reduced this enrichment. PTPRM knockdown decreased Tregs, increased Th17 cells, and promoted STAT3 Y705 phosphorylation in vitro and in a murine HCC model. Targeting this lactate-H3K18la-PTPRM axis may offer valuable therapeutic strategies for HCC.

title: CD147 drives keloid formation by promoting fibroblast proliferation via the CENPF signaling pathway
abstract: Keloids are benign dermal tumors, and keloid fibroblasts (KFs) play a critical role in their formation through hyperproliferation. However, the mechanism underlying this excessive fibroblast growth in keloids remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that CD147 is upregulated in KFs and promotes their pathological activities, while its inhibition reverses these abnormalities. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis revealed that CD147 played an important regulatory role in controlling the cell cycle of KFs, and centromere protein F (CENPF) expression was substantially downregulated following CD147 inhibition. Furthermore, CENPF knockdown attenuated the proliferation-inducing effects of CD147 in KFs, potentially promoting cell apoptosis via the p53 signaling pathway. These findings uncover the CD147-CENPF signaling pathway in keloid pathogenesis, suggesting targeting this pathway as a promising therapeutic strategy.

title: A linear calibration method for scattering semiconductors using the Kubelka-Munk function
abstract: Absorption spectroscopy of solids is hindered by strong scattering, which violates assumptions underlying the Beer-Lambert (BL) law. Although calibration approaches have been reported for scattering solids, their mechanistic basis in terms of the absorption and scattering coefficients remains unclear, and their applicability to semiconductors has not been well documented. Here, we measured ultraviolet-visible diffuse reflectance spectra for nine inorganic semiconductors. From reflectance, we calculated pseudo-absorbance and the Kubelka-Munk function (KMF). The results show that absorbance departs from BL linearity but is well described by an expression derived from KMF with mixture additivity of the coefficients. In contrast, KMF increases linearly with mass fraction within a low-loading regime, and the relation persists across distinct morphologies. Compositions of mixtures recovered from KMF agree closely with preparation values. This work underscores a simple, rapid, and non-destructive calibration strategy for scattering semiconductors that uses KMF as a linear axis for composition.

title: Generation of hypoimmunogenic cardiomyocytes from human induced pluripotent stem cells with TAPBP knockout
abstract: Immunological rejection is a challenge for the transplantation of cardiomyocytes (CMs) derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). TAP-binding protein knockout (TAPBP-KO) hiPSC-derived CMs (hiPSC-CMs) were used to reduce human leukocyte antigen class I expression and their hypoimmunogenic potential was determined. TAPBP-KO hiPSC-CMs exhibited CM differentiation efficiency and functional properties comparable to those of controls. The immunological responses against cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) or natural killer cells (NK cells) were measured using the production of inflammatory cytokines, the expression of degranulation markers, and cell viability upon co-cultivation with hiPSC-CMs. The CTL-mediated cytotoxicity was lower in TAPBP-KO hiPSC-CMs than in controls. TAPBP-KO hiPSC-CMs did not induce cytotoxicity from NK cells. This approach can preclude immunological rejection from CTLs without initiating the innate immune response from NK cells, thereby expanding the access to cell therapy for patients with heart failure.

title: Alteration of empathy-related behaviors in two strains of mice expressing mutations of the α5 cholinergic nicotinic receptor subunit
abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) of the alpha5 subunit of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) increases human risk for nicotine dependence, alcohol use disorders (AUDs), and schizophrenia. Here, we used transgenic mice carrying either this SNP (rs16969968; α5SNP/α5KI) or a Chrna5 knockout (α5KO) to examine the role of α5-containing nAChRs in affective state discrimination and prosocial, rescuing-like behaviors. α5KO mice failed to recognize a negative affective state in a familiar peer and displayed severely altered prosocial, empathy-related behaviors, at times assaulting distressed peers. In contrast, α5KI mice discriminated affective states normally and showed increased rescuing-like behavior. Effects of α5 mutations on affective state discrimination were sex stratified. These findings demonstrate the critical implication of α5∗nAChRs in affective state discrimination and prosocial-like behaviors, revealing sex-stratified patterns of these social-emotional deficits in α5KI and α5KO mice, which are reminiscent of the behavioral features of two characterized subtypes of AUD in humans.

title: “Locking” CDK9 inhibition by activating integrator function in HIV transcription
abstract: The positive transcription elongation factor b (P-TEFb) is a critical host factor for HIV transcription, yet pharmacological inhibition of its CDK9 subunit yields transient suppression with cytotoxicity. We identify that the integrator-PP2A complex enhances the potency and durability of CDK9 inhibition without added toxicity. Activation of PP2A with the small-molecule SMAP-2, combined with a low dose of the CDK9 inhibitor AZD4573, suppresses HIV transcription in CD4 + T cells, persisting for 7 days after drug withdrawal. Mechanistically, the drug combination increases integrator recruitment and repressive chromatin marks, decreases RNA polymerase II occupancy and C-terminal domain (CTD) phosphorylation at HIV promoter, and reduces short and long HIV transcripts, without global T cell activation, proliferation or broad transcriptome changes. The drug combination's HIV-inhibiting effect is somewhat resistant against elevated HIV activity in the presence of cocaine or morphine. These findings reveal cooperative P-TEFb inhibition and integrator activation as a promising strategy for durable HIV silencing.

title: Lactate-driven histone lactylation by AARS1 promotes pulmonary arterial hypertension
abstract: Glycolytic reprogramming drives lactate accumulation in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). We used a monocrotaline-induced rat PAH model and platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-stimulated pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), together with oxamate intervention and molecular assays, to investigate lactate-mediated histone lactylation. PAH tissues exhibited increased lactate, MCT4, and histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), accompanied by reduced HDAC1. Oxamate reversed these alterations and alleviated pulmonary vascular remodeling. Manipulating MCT4 expression modulated H3K18la levels. Upregulated alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (AARS1) displayed enhanced nuclear localization after lactate exposure; AARS1 depletion suppressed lactate-triggered H3K18la and PASMC proliferation. H3K18la was enriched at the Ctnnb1 promoter and correlated with enhanced Ctnnb1 transcription. These findings suggest that lactate may act as an epigenetic signal, linking glycolysis to Ctnnb1 activation through AARS1-associated H3K18la, thereby offering a potential target for PAH treatment.

title: LPS and quorum sensing protect Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteria from phagocytosis and destruction by Dictyostelium discoideum amoebae
abstract: Free-living amoebae like Dictyostelium discoideum and environmental bacteria like Pseudomonas aeruginosa are engaged in complex predator-prey interactions. Amoeba can notably ingest and kill bacteria. In this study, we report that three different strains of the opportunistic pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa are protected from amoebal phagocytosis. Analysis of P. aeruginosa mutants revealed that OSA-type lipopolysaccharides (LPS) allow these P. aeruginosa strains to escape phagocytosis by amoebae. Amoebae can also kill extracellularly un-ingested P. aeruginosa bacteria. Our results indicate that induction of the Las quorum sensing (QS) makes P. aeruginosa resistant to reactive oxygen species, to bacteriolytic factors secreted by D. discoideum , and ultimately to extracellular destruction by amoebae. Together, these observations suggest that LPS and QS probably play a key role in P. aeruginosa escape strategies against phagocytic amoebae in the environment and shed new light on the transition of infectious P. aeruginosa from the environment to the human body.

title: Spatial epigenomics reveals stromal niche-associated regulatory programs across pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor grades
abstract: Non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (NF-PanNETs) account for the majority of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms and exhibit substantial clinical and biological heterogeneity, yet their epigenetic regulation and spatial architecture remain poorly understood. Here, we present an integrative analysis of NF-PanNETs across multiple tumor grades using single-nucleus advent of transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (snATAC-seq) and spatial ATAC-seq. snATAC-seq identified grade-associated chromatin accessibility programs characterized by distinct transcription factor activities, including HNF1A and FOXA2 in low-grade tumors, ETS family factors in intermediate-grade tumors, SNAI-associated regulatory programs in high-grade tumors, and CEBPB- and TOX-associated immune states. Spatial ATAC-seq revealed spatially coordinated tumor-stroma interactions, with stroma-proximal regions enriched for MYC/FOX-associated proliferative programs and distal regions exhibiting SNAI-enriched invasive programs. Together, our study provides a spatially resolved epigenomic atlas of NF-PanNETs across tumor grades, offering a resource for understanding epigenetic heterogeneity and generating hypotheses regarding regulatory programs and tumor-stroma interactions for future functional and clinical investigation.

title: BMP2, transcriptionally regulated by GATA6, accelerates the proliferation and invasion of lung squamous carcinoma cells
abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) has a high mortality rate, creating an urgent need to identify novel therapeutic targets. Aberrant expression of bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) is associated with the progression of several cancers. Previous reports demonstrated that BMP2 is highly expressed in tumor tissues and serum of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the pathological roles and mechanisms of BMP2 in LUSC progression, and the mechanism underlying the overexpression of BMP2 remain to be elucidated. In this study, we found that a high level of BMP2 is correlated with poor prognosis in patients with LUSC, and that BMP2 promotes the growth and metastasis of LUSC cells in vitro and in vivo by activating the MAPK-ERK1/2 signaling pathway. The expression of BMP2 is transcriptionally repressed by the transcription factor GATA6. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that BMP2 may serve as a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of LUSC.

title: StrokeTime: A comprehensive longitudinal scRNA-seq atlas of the ischemic mouse brain
abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers profound, dynamic changes in the brain's cellular landscape.
