Genetic analyses indicate that DBT and CK2 act through distinct pathways that have additive effects on temperature compensation. DBT acts through the per Short phosphorylation cluster and the S47 phosphodegron of the core clock protein PER, both of which are required for normal thermal compensation. In contrast, CK2 acts through a phosphocluster in TIM as well as PER S45 residue. Interestingly, simultaneous disruption of both pathways causes accumulation of hyperphosphorylated PER, which is inefficiently cleared from the nucleus of circadian pacemaker neurons. Combined with previous work, our findings support a central and unifying role for nuclear PER phosphorylation dynamics in buffering circadian period against environmental temperature fluctuations.

title: FDX1 suppresses acute myeloid leukemia progression and reverses cuproptosis resistance via the ROS/p53/ME1 axis
abstract: Cuproptosis, a copper-dependent cell death mechanism, holds therapeutic potential in cancer, yet its regulatory pathways in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remain poorly defined. We demonstrate that elevated serum copper levels correlate with poor prognosis in AML patients. Screening reveals that ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) is significantly downregulated in AML and associated with adverse outcomes. FDX1 loss promoted AML cell proliferation and cuproptosis resistance. Mechanistically, FDX1 enhanced mitochondrial damage and ROS/p53 signaling, which transcriptionally suppressed malic enzyme 1 (ME1). ME1 disrupted mitochondrial NAD + /NADH homeostasis and modulated lipoylated DLAT delipoylation, thereby limiting cuproptosis. ME1 was highly expressed in AML and supported leukemic cell growth, while its inhibition restored cuproptosis sensitivity in FDX1-low cells. Given the elevated serum copper levels in AML and the capacity of ME1 inhibition to reverse cuproptosis resistance induced by low FDX1 expression, the combination of copper ionophores with ME1 inhibitors may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for AML.

title: Pre-season bare-soil spectral proxies complement pod-filling canopy indices for field-scale soybean-yield prediction from UAV imagery
abstract: Field-scale soybean-yield models based on canopy imagery may miss soil-surface variation. We evaluated a two-flight drone framework combining pre-season bare-soil and pod-filling multispectral imagery at 101 locations in four slope units in Northeast China. Five random-forest scenarios were compared using nested feature selection and repeated outer-test evaluation. Adding the bare-soil proxy pool to pod-filling vegetation indices increased mean outer-test predictive R 2 from 0.240 to 0.325 and reduced mean absolute error from 573.06 to 518.76 kg ha −1 ; this error decreased in all 10 repeats. Model attribution showed contributions from canopy and bare-soil predictors. Predictions overestimated low yields and underestimated high yields. For this combined scenario, pooled predictive R 2 declined to 0.161 when each slope unit was excluded from model development. Pre-season bare-soil imagery therefore provided modest complementary information beyond a pod-filling acquisition, but the framework remains a field-scale proof of concept requiring multi-year and multi-site validation.

title: Neural substrates related to memory consolidation of learning multiple motor sequences during wakeful rest
abstract: Abstract Motor learning has been thought to be independent of the hippocampus since the landmark experiment of the patient H.M. However, recent studies have provided cumulative evidence of the hippocampus's role in motor memory consolidation during both sleep and wakeful rest. Motor memory consolidation due to hippocampal plastic changes could occur faster than previously thought, even during short wakeful rest periods interleaved with practice periods. However, it remains unclear to what extent hippocampal replay or reactivation contributes to motor memory consolidation during wakeful rest. We investigated the fMRI evidence of motor memory consolidation of learning multiple motor sequence during wakeful rest. We found that while sensorimotor regions exhibited sequence-specific activity patterns during practice, these were not reliably discriminable in the sensorimotor regions and hippocampus during brief interleaved rest periods. In contrast, neural activity patterns in the right hippocampus, right putamen, and sensorimotor regions during interleaved rest periods showed greater similarity to post-learning rest patterns than pre-learning rest patterns. These findings suggest that hippocampal reactivation may not be related to a specific sequence as previously claimed, but rather to a more generalized or abstract representation of sequences, potentially to stabilize and integrate newly acquired skills when learning multiple sequences simultaneously.

title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization
abstract: Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with static microenvironment analysis to identify enzyme variants compatible with biomimetic cofactors. Applied to P450BM3, a widely used biocatalyst for chiral synthesis and pharmaceutical precursor production, HelixWings identified a variant with a 404% improvement in catalytic efficiency toward cytochrome c under NMNH-supported conditions. The platform was further validated with CYP116B46, achieving a 217% improvement in NMNH utilization efficiency. HelixWings reduced screening time by 23-fold compared with rational design.

title: Metabolic regulation of ATM-KAT8-RPA1 axis in DNA damage repair and chemoresistance
abstract: Post-translational modifications are recognized as critical regulators of the DNA damage response. In this study, we determined that replication protein A1 (RPA1), a modulator of homologous recombination (HR) repair, is lactylated at lysine 167 (K167) in response to DNA damage. This modification is catalyzed by the histone acetyltransferase KAT8 and is dependent on ATM-mediated phosphorylation of KAT8. Lactylation at K167 enhances the DNA-binding capacity of RPA1, which in turn facilitates HR repair. The inhibition of KAT8 or lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), which increases intracellular lactate level, markedly reduces RPA1 lactylation, impairs HR repair, and increases the sensitivity of tumor cells to chemotherapy in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. Furthermore, a cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) that selectively disrupts this modification can sensitize tumors to genotoxic treatment. These findings establish RPA1 lactylation as a critical regulator of HR repair and reveal a potential therapeutic strategy in which this modification can be targeted to overcome chemoresistance.

title: An engineered α-1,3-glucanase-derived probe enables sensitive detection of α-1,3-glucan and reveals its soluble release by Aspergillus
abstract: α-1,3-Glucan is a major component of the Aspergillus cell wall. However, unlike β-1,3-glucan and galactomannan, α-1,3-glucan was not previously considered to be released in a soluble form. Therefore, its potential as a diagnostic biomarker has remained largely unexplored. In this study, we engineered α-1,3-glucanase mutants to develop α-1,3-glucan-specific binding proteins and detection systems. Mutants derived from the endo-type α-1,3-glucanases, AGN1 and AglKA, were generated, among which AglKA-CatD-D1090A lacked enzymatic activity but retained strong binding affinity for α-1,3-glucan. Using this probe, we established a split luciferase assay to detect α-1,3-glucan in Aspergillus hyphae and conidia without prior purification. Soluble α-1,3-glucan was substantially released by major Aspergillus species, as indicated by results of a sandwich ELISA-like assay with AglKA mutants. These findings suggest that soluble α-1,3-glucan has potential as a complementary diagnostic biomarker for aspergillosis.

title: Fault diagnosis of rotating machinery under imbalanced samples based on outlier-removal HCAB-SMOTE-LOF
abstract: In rotating machinery fault diagnosis, the original feature space often suffers from anomalous outliers, limited sample availability, and imbalanced class distributions. These issues severely hinder the accurate recognition of minority-class samples and lead to suboptimal diagnostic efficiency. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid method named HCAB-SMOTE-LOF, which integrates the Hybrid Clustered Affinitive Borderline Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique with the Local Outlier Factor (LOF) algorithm. To extract the fault-relevant time-frequency features, the high-pass filtering is applied to the raw vibration signals to remove low-frequency components. The LOF is introduced to eliminate samples that are clearly abnormal or mislabeled in the feature space. On this basis, the HCAB-SMOTE algorithm is employed to synthetically generate minority-class fault samples, thereby improving the quality and distributional plausibility of the generated samples and alleviating the adverse impact of data imbalance on classifier performance. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using both a laboratory dataset and the Ottawa motor dataset. Furthermore, a comparative analysis is conducted between the proposed method and several oversampling strategies applied during data processing, including the use of original data, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, and HCAB-SMOTE. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms all existing oversampling methods across all evaluation metrics, confirming its marked advantages in outlier removal and sample-distribution optimization and thus its capability to effectively detect rotating machinery faults.

title: Recurrent latent dynamics in spinal circuits enable a digital twin of autonomic state transitions
abstract: Physiological signals underlying homeostasis, such as blood pressure, are dynamic and nonlinear, shaped by interactions among diverse neurons. During blood pressure transitions, neurons in the spinal intermediolateral nucleus (IML), a sympathetic hub, show heterogeneous monotonic increases or decreases in firing. Such diversity is intrinsic to homeostatic control but hampers accurate decoding of internal state dynamics. Here, we introduce a manifold-based model that addresses this challenge by directly mapping IML population activity onto physiological state transitions. Individual neurons responded independently with increases or decreases in firing, but these patterns alone did not align with the nonlinear trajectory of blood pressure. Focusing instead on recurrent population dynamics, we derived a low-dimensional circular manifold that captured the cyclical temporal evolution of state transitions. Embedding this manifold as a dynamic reservoir in a recurrent neural network reproduced both trial-by-trial variability in neural population activity and nonlinear blood pressure dynamics, establishing a circuit-level framework for autonomic state decoding.

title: Design, modeling, and validation of a computer-vision-enabled 3D-printed soft robotic glove for stroke telerehabilitation
abstract: Post-stroke rehabilitation for upper-limb mobility faces challenges such as limited availability, high costs, and insufficient insurance coverage. This work addresses these challenges by integrating soft robotics with computer vision. A lightweight soft robotic glove (159 g), featuring five three-dimensional (3D)-printed soft pneumatic actuators that function as fingers, is designed and optimized using finite element modeling (FEM) in terms of bending behavior and force output. The fingers demonstrated durability, bending deformation repeatability, force repeatability, and reliable holding force capability. The proof-of-concept system comprises a wearable robotic glove for the patient and a computer vision interface for the therapist. The therapist performs hand gestures captured by a camera to control the glove through the computer vision interface. The soft robotic glove and integrated computer vision interface were experimentally validated on healthy participants. This validation demonstrates the feasibility of controlling the glove using computer vision and its potential for future telerehabilitation applications.

title: Therapeutic HPV16 E7 vaccination with CD137 agonism induces tumor regression and durable immunity in mice
abstract: Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines prevent new infections but do not treat established HPV-associated lesions, highlighting the need for therapeutic strategies targeting viral tumor antigens. We developed a recombinant overlapping peptide-based HPV16 E7 vaccine (ROP-E7) and evaluated its immunogenicity and antitumor activity, alone or combined with CD137 (4-1BB) agonism, in C57BL/6 mice. In tumor-free mice, ROP-E7 induced greater helper and cytotoxic T cell responses than wild-type E7. In tumor-bearing mice, ROP-E7 reduced tumor burden and improved survival, while combination treatment induced complete tumor regression and tumor-free survival beyond 100 days. These effects were associated with increased intratumoral cytotoxic T cells and reduced regulatory and exhausted T cell populations. These findings provide preclinical support for combining therapeutic HPV16 E7 vaccination with T cell co-stimulation in HPV-associated cancers.

title: Efficacy and safety of trans-fornix conjunctival retrobulbar block in a prospective randomized controlled trial
abstract: Retrobulbar block is widely used for vitreoretinal surgery, but the conventional transcutaneous technique advances a sharp needle blindly through the lower eyelid. We evaluated a trans -fornix conjunctival approach in which a curved blunt-tip needle is advanced into the muscle cone under the operating microscope. In a two-center randomized trial, 196 patients were stratified by expected surgical duration and allocated to the transcutaneous or the trans -fornix technique, and pain was graded at predefined procedural stages. The trans -fornix approach reduced pain during anesthetic injection in both cohorts and during scleral indentation in longer procedures, and fewer patients required supplemental anesthesia. Ocular akinesia was better with the trans -fornix technique, and periorbital hemorrhage and ecchymosis occurred only in the transcutaneous group. These findings support the trans -fornix block as a practical and reproducible option for regional anesthesia in vitreoretinal surgery.

title: Temporal patterns of melanopsin-evoked calcium signaling engage NF-κB-associated transcriptional and phosphoproteomic responses
abstract: Abstract Cells continuously experience fluctuating intracellular calcium (Ca²⁺) signals that orchestrate diverse processes such as transcription, proliferation, and apoptosis. Temporal features of Ca²⁺ dynamics, including oscillation frequency, are hypothesized to encode information, allowing cells to discriminate between relevant and stochastic signals. However, the mechanisms of frequency decoding and their transcriptional consequences remain incompletely understood. To address this, we investigated how defined Ca²⁺ oscillation frequencies are translated into signaling cascades and gene expression programs in human non-excitable cells. Using optogenetic control of melanopsin-mediated Ca²⁺ influx, we induced slow (8 mHz) or fast (15 mHz) oscillations with identical single-pulse kinetics to isolate the effect of frequency. We found that TNF and IL8 transcription via NF-κB displayed sigmoidal frequency dependence, strictly requiring regular periodic stimulation, while random or low-frequency inputs with equal cumulative Ca²⁺ exposure were ineffective. Bulk RNA sequencing revealed a MYC -centered transcriptional response, with 116 of 215 differentially expressed genes predicted as MYC targets, despite unchanged MYC mRNA levels. Label-free phosphoproteomics identified PRKDC, CHEK2 and ATM as the top upstream kinases, forming a network linking Ca²⁺ oscillations to cell cycle and stress signaling. These findings demonstrate that cells can decode Ca²⁺ oscillation frequency through a multi-kinase network that tunes transcription via NF-κB and MYC, providing mechanistic insight into how temporal dynamics of second messengers shape cellular decision-making.

title: EEG-based deep learning estimates preterm infants’ cerebral age: Contribution of slow-wave and cross-frequency coupling
abstract: Reliably estimating cerebral maturation in preterm newborns is crucial for early identification of atypical neurodevelopment. We developed a deep-learning framework using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict postmenstrual age (PMA) from spontaneous neural activity in EEG recordings of 165 healthy preterm infants (28–38 weeks PMA). The model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.75 ± 0.60 weeks, with 73.9% of prediction errors within one week. To identify key neurophysiological drivers, we systematically manipulated signal components. Results showed that removing low-frequency activity (<4 Hz) significantly degraded performance and disrupting phase-amplitude coupling selectively impaired prediction accuracy before 34 weeks PMA, while high-frequency activity (>12 Hz) had minimal impact. Our results demonstrate that maturation signatures are primarily driven by slow-wave dynamics and their hierarchical coupling with faster oscillations, which are fundamental hallmarks of early neurodevelopment.

title: Critical analysis of the new European framework for non-fossil flexibility and the questions left unanswered
abstract: The 2024 Electricity Market Design Reform introduced a new European framework for non-fossil flexibility. The first national flexibility needs assessments were published in July 2026, and indicative objectives and support schemes for non-fossil flexibility will soon be introduced. However, we argue that this new framework, which will influence the development of European power systems as they transition to low-carbon resources, is based on a flawed theoretical foundation and exhibits significant overlap with the European resource adequacy framework. No flexibility metric has been defined for the flexibility needs assessment. No flexibility standard/target has been calculated based on the economic equilibrium between the cost of additional flexibility and the cost of not relying on it. We identify three underlying metrics for flexibility needs, we present alternative approaches to define flexibility products and identify open questions that need to be addressed before the new flexibility framework moves to the implementation phase.

title: Diatom-based treatment of geothermal brines to selectively remove silicon, retain lithium for downstream recovery, and produce omega-3 fatty acids
abstract: Silica (SiO2) scaling has an adverse impact on geothermal brines processing, hindering both energy production and resource recovery. Here we developed a novel bioprocess to selectively remove silicon (Si) from brines to support downstream recovery of lithium (Li), applying circular bioeconomy principles. Diatom screening identified the best performance to aid Si removal from the marine diatom Halamphora sp. To enhance biomass productivity and increase the rate of Si removal, a feeding approach involving controlled semi-continuous urea feed (SCUF) was employed. Urea-fed cells cultured in geothermal brine produced 0.45 g L−1 of biomass, removed 34 mg L−1 of Si (97.14%) within 48 h, while retained over 99% of Li (75 mg L-1) in solution and co-produce eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA, 47 mg g-1) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA, 24 mg g-1). These findings underscore the dual potential of Halamphora sp. for simultaneous Si removal and production of high-value nutraceutical compounds.

title: NR2F6 functions as a key transcriptional checkpoint enforcing dysfunction of human CD3+ T cells and limiting CAR-T cell potency
abstract: Although nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 6 (NR2F6) regulates lymphocyte activation in murine models, its function in human T cells remains incompletely defined. Here, we identify NR2F6 as a T cell receptor (TCR)-inducible transcriptional checkpoint that limits effector potency in human CD3 + T cells, including chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells. In an anti-EGFR CAR-T cell-A549 co-culture model, enforced NR2F6 expression, mimicking its upregulation in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, markedly impairs killing under repeated tumor challenge. In polyclonal T cells, NR2F6 overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated ablation produced directionally opposing effects, supporting its role as a negative regulator of activation, differentiation-associated programs, and cytokine production. Mechanistically, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and nuclear protein analyses are consistent with suppression of NFAT-, AP-1-, and NF-κB-associated pathways and reveal context-dependent changes in TCF-1-associated readouts. Collectively, these findings position NR2F6 as a signaling-integrated transcriptional checkpoint that contributes to dysfunctional T cell states and may promote tumor immune evasion in humans.

title: Frequency-dependent thalamocortical transfer limits sustained cortical expression of sensory drive
abstract: Frequency-dependent sensory drive must pass through thalamocortical pathways before being expressed in cortex, yet how high-frequency input is transformed into sustained cortical activity remains unclear. We combined 11.7-T fMRI, pathway-specific optogenetic stimulation, tuned-burst thalamic drive, and dynamic causal modeling in dexmedetomidine-sedated rats to examine the forepaw VPL-to-S1FL pathway. Peripheral forepaw stimulation revealed intermediate-frequency cortical tuning, whereas thalamic nuclei remained responsive at high frequencies. Direct S1FL activation evoked sustained high-frequency BOLD responses, indicating that cortex can express high-frequency drive when upstream relay is bypassed. In contrast, direct VPL activation produced strong local thalamic responses but weak, onset-dominated cortical responses at high frequency, and tuned-burst stimulation showed temporal compression before cortical expression. Dynamic causal modeling indicated preferential enhancement of VPL-to-S1FL effective connectivity at intermediate frequencies. These findings identify a frequency-dependent bottleneck in VPL-to-S1FL transfer, rather than local cortical responsiveness, as a constraint on sustained cortical expression of temporally dense sensory input.

title: Expanding the galactose oxidase substrate repertoire via a multi-modal computational strategy
abstract: Biocatalysis offers a greener alternative to chemical processes, yet industrial adoption is bottlenecked by the prohibitive cost of enzyme engineering. Here, we report a multi-modal computational framework that integrates synergistic descriptors of substrate binding, protein stability, and aggregation traits. Using galactose oxidase as a model system, this approach achieves 77% precision in identifying active variants across 13 structurally diverse secondary alcohols despite being trained exclusively on a single substrate. By implementing sequence conservation-based filtering, we demonstrate that training data can be reduced by 41% without compromising predictive fidelity. Furthermore, the multi-modal model generalizes to combinatorial variants (2–5 mutations) with 100% precision on a limited library. Experimental validation yields a curated panel of starting points for the synthesis of high-value functional ingredients, including optical brighteners and fragrance stabilizers. Our multi-modal approach facilitates more cost-effective enzyme engineering, supporting the development of biocatalytic routes for sustainable chemical manufacturing.

title: Comments on “surface-based brain age index reflects hematological impacts on cognitive development in children with beta-thalassemia major”
Ultrasound-based breast nodule malignancy diagnosis using CNN enhanced by knowledge distillation
abstract: Accurate discrimination of benign and malignant breast lesions is essential for early diagnosis, yet remains challenging due to lesion heterogeneity and interobserver variability in ultrasound assessment. We developed a deep learning (DL) framework integrating dual inverted bottleneck blocks (Dual-IB), adaptive hierarchical feature fusion, and knowledge distillation (KD) for breast ultrasound lesion classification. The model was trained and evaluated on public datasets and validated on an independent external cohort to assess its generalizability. Results demonstrated superior performance compared with baseline methods and resident radiologists, while maintaining robust performance across diverse datasets and imaging conditions. On the external validation dataset, the model achieved the best performance, with an accuracy (Acc) of 92.64% and an F1-score of 92.37%. Furthermore, class activation mapping (CAM) visualizations revealed focused and anatomically plausible attention patterns within lesion regions, aiding interpretation and suggesting its potential to assist in breast ultrasound lesion classification.

title: An orthogonal Cro/OR3 system reveals an influence of astrocytes on motor neuron positioning
abstract: Abstract Precise spatiotemporal control of gene expression is essential for dissecting complex biological systems. Here, we introduce a phage-derived Cro/O R 3 binary system for transcriptional activation that functions robustly in zebrafish and human cells. A Cro repressor fused to the VP16 activation domain efficiently drives expression of O R 3 operator-linked genes, and its activity can be targeted to specific cell types using enhancer-trap and promoter-controlled zebrafish lines. As a proof of concept, we manipulate glutamate transporter Glast/Slc1a3b-expressing cells in the central nervous system by Cro/O R 3-mediated expression of a human ataxia-associated, uptake-deficient Glast/Slc1a3b variant, causing spastic, uncoordinated movement and axial deformation. Concurrent Gal4/UAS-mediated visualization reveals substantially disrupted positioning of motor neurons, highlighting their selective sensitivity to extracellular glutamate homeostasis during spinal circuit assembly. Together, these results establish the Cro/O R 3 system as an orthogonal platform for targeted gene expression, enabling precise mechanistic dissection of how specific cell types and their interactions underlie diverse biological processes.

title: Targeting TRP channels in hearing loss from mechanisms to otoprotection
abstract: Hearing loss, a highly prevalent global disease with complex pathogenic mechanisms, poses significant challenges due to limited treatment options and secondary complications. Recent research highlights the crucial roles of transient receptor potential (TRP) channels in auditory physiology and pathology, including cochlear electrophysiology, endolymph ionic homeostasis, neurotransmitter release, inflammation, and sensorineural injury responses. Although previous reviews synthesized TRP-mediated pathological mechanisms in hearing loss, clinical translation and otoprotective drug discovery remain underexplored. This review characterizes inner ear TRP spatiotemporal expression, traces the hair cell mechanoelectrical transduction (MET) channel research trajectory, details their dual regulatory mechanisms, and compiles emerging TRP-targeting otoprotective candidates. It further highlights limitations including restricted preclinical models, scarce otoprotective drugs, and limited target diversity among existing agents. Finally, it proposes new research directions for future basic and clinical studies on TRP channels and auditory function.

title: miR-7a-5p attenuates hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy by suppressing PARP1-mediated parthanatos
abstract: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) causes severe neonatal brain injury, with PARP1 hyperactivation implicated in neuronal death. Using a rat HIE model and glutamate-exposed HT22 neurons, we found that miR-7a-5p is significantly downregulated in both peripheral blood and the injured cortex of HIE rats. PARP1 hyperactivation triggered parthanatos, characterized by PAR polymer accumulation and apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF) nuclear translocation, without activating caspase-dependent apoptosis. Luciferase assays confirmed direct targeting of miR-7a-5p to the 3′ UTR of PARP1, suppressing its expression. Exogenous miR-7a-5p reduces infarction volume, improves neural morphology, and preserves neurological function recovery in HIE rats. In vitro , miR-7a-5p overexpression or pharmacological PARP1 inhibition attenuated glutamate-induced neuronal death, mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) loss, ROS overproduction, and PAR/AIF dysregulation. Crucially, PARP1 agonist MNNG reversed miR-7a-5p-mediated neuroprotection, establishing the indispensability of the miR-7a-5p/PARP1 axis. miR-7a-5p is a key regulator of parthanatos, suppressing PARP1 hyperactivation, mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction, and offering a therapeutic target for HIE.

title: Exploratory single-cell multiomics suggests naive CD4+ T cell dysregulation in treatment refractory rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Around 20% of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have disease that remains refractory to multiple targeted treatments, highlighting a major clinical challenge. We determine single-nucleus transcriptional and chromatin landscapes (10x Genomics Epi Multiome) on 14,625 primary CD4 + T-cells isolated from treatment-naive early and refractory (defined as per the EULAR definition of difficult-to-treat) patients with RA. We systematically analyze circulating regulatory profiles to reveal potential mechanisms and therapeutic targets that may contribute to the difficult-to-treat phenotype. We highlight disease-stage-specific alterations in naive and Th1-like memory CD4 + T-cells. In particular, refractory naive cells show signatures of heightened activation, upregulation of pathways aligning with T cell anergy, diminished regulation at regulatory loci (e.g., FOXP1, ICOS) and blunted stimulation responses; consistent with a more desensitized or exhausted state. Genes such as LGALS3, ZBTB7B and FOXO4 emerge as potential candidate regulators of the difficult-to-treat state. Finally, through RA GWAS integration, we prioritize putative causal variants in cis-regulatory elements.

title: Stable isotope approaches for CNS lipid metabolism: From precision quantification to metabolic tracing
abstract: Lipids are central to membrane organization, signaling, myelination, and metabolic homeostasis in the central nervous system (CNS), where their abundance, turnover, and spatial distribution are tightly regulated. Stable isotope approaches provide complementary ways to interrogate this complexity. Here, we integrate evidence from cellular, animal, and human studies to compare stable isotope dilution (SID) and chemical isotope labeling (CIL) for precise lipid quantification with metabolic tracing strategies that resolve synthesis, turnover, pathway contribution, and lipid trafficking. We examine their implementation across mass spectrometry, NMR, vibrational spectroscopy (VS), and imaging platforms, together with kinetic and flux-modeling frameworks that connect isotope-enrichment patterns to pathway activity. We further highlight spatially and cell-type-resolved isotope measurements that extend lipid analysis from bulk abundance to regional and cellular metabolic organization. These advances establish a framework linking lipid composition with metabolic dynamics and provide mechanistic insight into CNS physiology, neurological disease, myelin repair, and metabolic intervention strategies.

title: Adolescents infer latent motives to build generalizable models of others’ behavior
abstract: Understanding and predicting others' behavior is a key developmental task in adolescence as social interactions become more complex. Because social situations rarely repeat exactly, accurate prediction requires generalization beyond past actions. We examined how adolescents ( n = 127; ages 10–20) predicted others' behavior across a series of economic games. Prediction accuracy improved with age. Computational modeling showed that this improvement was driven by an increasing tendency to infer unobservable motives underlying behavior (e.g., greed and risk aversion), with older adolescents more likely to infer multiple motives. In particular, inferring risk aversion became more common from early to mid-adolescence. These results suggest that adolescents increasingly build abstract, generalizable models of others' behavior, supporting flexible social reasoning in novel contexts.

title: Anodal tDCS alters perceived visual contrast in humans
abstract: Cortical gain modulation is thought to alter perceptual experience, most prominently demonstrated by the effects of spatial attention on contrast appearance1. Whether externally induced changes in cortical excitability produce comparable perceptual consequences remains unclear. Here, we tested whether anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over occipital cortex alters perceived contrast. Using a contrast-appearance paradigm, participants judged which of two gratings appeared higher in contrast. Anodal stimulation produced systematic shifts in the point of subjective equality (PSE), such that stimuli presented in the contralateral visual field were perceived as higher in contrast. This effect reversed across stimulus configurations and was absent under sham stimulation, ruling out response bias. Psychometric slopes were unchanged, indicating no reliable modulation of contrast sensitivity. These findings demonstrate that tDCS alters contrast appearance, suggesting that changes in cortical excitability can directly influence perceptual experience through gain-like modulation of sensory responses.

title: Adenoviral vector co-expressing ALDH1 and ADH1 mitigates alcohol toxicity and modulates glucose and lipid metabolism
abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption remains a global health concern, with ethanol and its toxic metabolite, acetaldehyde, causing significant physiological harm. Current hangover remedies fail to enhance alcohol metabolism at a fundamental level. In this study, we engineered a recombinant adenovirus, catalase 68-acetaldehyde dehydrogenase 1-alcohol dehydrogenase 1 (C68-ALDH1-ADH1), co-expressing dehydrogenases ALDH1 and ADH1 to improve alcohol metabolic capacity. In vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrated that C68-ALDH1-ADH1 significantly reduced hepatic alcohol and acetaldehyde levels and alleviated liver injury. Overexpression of ALDH1 and ADH1 also improved glucose and lipid metabolism. Notably, the lipid metabolism related gene fatty acyl-CoA reductase 2 ( FAR2 ) was found to be associated with ALDH1/ADH1 expression, linking it to alcohol detoxification and the fatty alcohol cycle. C68-ALDH1-ADH1 further ameliorated non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) through this pathway. These findings supported a potential protective effect of C68-ALDH1-ADH1 in treating alcohol-related disorders.

title: Fragile streak goals elicit multimodal pressure responses and late-stage performance decline
abstract: Abstract Psychological pressure is thought to relate to performance in an inverted-U pattern, yet evidence is mixed, possibly because manipulations rarely produce high pressure. We induced scalable pressure using a streak goal that resets after a failure in a force-control task. Participants pursued ten consecutive successes (streak goal) or 100 successes irrespective of sequence (total goal). Under the streak goal, heart rate, pupil size, and perceived pressure rose as participants approached their maximum streak; under the total goal, heart rate and pupil size showed little modulation. Performance followed an inverted-U under the streak goal—improving then declining at the maximum streak—whereas the total goal showed no late-stage drop. This dissociation suggests the late-stage decline reflects pressure, not the streak itself. Despite this clear performance decrement, analyses of movement vigor, feedforward/feedback kinematics, and individual differences in pressure responses revealed no consistent systematic signatures at the group level. Fragile streak goals thus provide a multimodal pressure manipulation and a platform for testing mechanisms underlying choking in human motor control.

title: Corrigendum to “WaveMamba-Net: Dual-frequency adaptive wavelet state-space network for real-time pulse signal classification in wearable health monitoring” [iScience 29 (2026) 116045]
Microbes and TNF drive colitis in the absence of innate lymphoid cells
abstract: Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) are critical sources of cytokines necessary for intestinal homeostasis in immunocompetent conditions, yet their necessity in innate colitis remains unclear. Using a model of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in mice lacking adaptive immunity, we investigated whether ILCs are required for innate colitis. Interleukin-15 receptor alpha-deficient mice lacked intestinal ILC1 and natural killer (NK) cells, but innate colitis in these mice was not diminished. Deletion of IL-2 receptor gamma chain, which ablates all ILCs and NK cells, also did not prevent innate colitis. Antibiotic treatment of mice lacking all ILCs prevented colitis. Similarly, TNF deficiency prevented colitis in the absence of all ILCs, demonstrating that TNF is essential for microbe-driven innate colitis in the absence of ILCs. These findings reveal that ILCs are redundant for innate colitis. Studies of innate colitis in the absence of ILCs may help understand mechanisms underlying IBD and the effectiveness of anti-TNF therapies.

title: PP2A-dependent downregulation of GABAB receptors modulates somatostatin interneurons function and plasticity
abstract: Abstract Cortical circuits rely on a precise balance of inhibitory and excitatory neurotransmission to encode information reliably and prevent pathology. Metabotropic GABA B receptors (GABA B Rs) are key regulators of inhibitory signalling in mammalian neurons. In GABAergic interneurons (INs), GABA B R activation reduces inhibition overall, leading to disinhibitory mechanisms. In the hippocampus, somatostatin-expressing (SST) INs form a major subtype that provides feedback inhibition to the distal dendrites of principal cells (PCs) and other INs. Plasticity of SST INs is well established as a mechanism controlling hippocampal circuit function through both inhibitory and disinhibitory pathways and depends on metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs) and GABA B Rs. However, whether activation of GABABRs induces metaplastic changes in SST INs, and how this influences circuit function and behaviour, remains unclear. Here, we combined quantitative SDS-digested freeze-fracture replica immunoelectron microscopy, ex vivo electrophysiology, in vivo behavioural testing, and pharmacological manipulation of GABA B Rs. We show that receptor activation directly regulates SST IN plasticity via protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A)-dependent internalisation. GABA B R activation not only controls its own surface expression but also regulates membrane levels of mGluR1α and high-voltage-activated Ca v 1.2 (L-type) Ca 2+ channels. This GABA B R-dependent metaplasticity shifts circuit plasticity toward greater enhancement of long-range inputs to the CA1 region and disrupts contextual memory formation. These findings demonstrate that receptor-mediated surface dynamics in SST INs are critical for maintaining physiological neurotransmission and proper hippocampal microcircuit function.

title: The structure of technological learning: Insights from water electrolysis for cost forecasting, policy, and strategy
abstract: Forecasting the cost evolution of emerging clean technologies is crucial for informed policy, investment, and decarbonization decisions, yet it remains deeply uncertain. Learning curves, which link cost declines to cumulative deployment, are widely used for technological cost forecasting. However, applying them to emerging technologies is challenging due to parametric uncertainty in learning rates, which are scarce and highly uncertain, and structural uncertainty stemming from multiple plausible learning frameworks. Using water electrolysis as a case study, we evaluate how different learning structures, from shared to fragmented learning across technology variants and regions, alter expected cost paths. We interrogate model assumptions that represent contrasting industrial realities, including competition among electrolyzer variants and supply chain fragmentation associated with protectionism and industrial policy. We find that plausible modeling choices generate widely different trajectories, with materially different implications for policy design and technology strategy. We argue for routinely applying multiple learning frameworks to explore decision spaces and stress-test conclusions for scale-up planning, national industrial strategy, and energy systems modeling.

title: Cellulase catalysis on cell surfaces using Caulobacter S-layer display
abstract: Abstract Sustainable bioprocesses for energy and materials production and waste resource recovery are needed to support circular economic development. Enzyme surface display on cells or functionalized materials has emerged as a promising paradigm for sustainable bioprocess innovation. Surface (S)-layers are geometric, monomolecular, highly stable crystalline protein lattices encasing the outside of many bacteria and archaea. Several S-layer genes have been shown to tolerate heterologous insertions, thereby enabling high-density display of peptides of interest on cell surfaces without additional costly immobilisation or conjugation steps. Here, we employ an S-layer display platform in Caulobacter vibrioides CB2A JS4038 to express functional cellulases up to 445 amino acids in length. We explore critical design considerations needed for successful catalytic display and demonstrate synergistic activities between differentially expressed cellulases relevant to combinatorial lignocellulosic biomass conversion. Functionalised S-layers capable of transforming lignocellulosic biomass could have useful applications in engineering whole-cell biocatalysts and synthetic microbial consortia tuned for different bioprocess applications.

title: Calibrated flow cytometry enables rapid detection of CD45−EpCAM+ extracellular vesicles for pancreatic cancer clinical assessment
abstract: Reliable non-invasive biomarkers are needed to optimize treatment selection and enable real-time monitoring of pancreatic cancer (PC). We developed a bead-calibrated, multiparametric flow cytometry (FC) protocol to detect, enumerate, and subtype circulating intact extracellular vesicles (EVs) in blood. Among 120 individuals analyzed by this platform, patients with PC had significantly higher levels of CD45 − EpCAM + EVs than controls. These EVs correlated positively with advanced tumor stage, while their combination with serum CA19-9 improved monitoring accuracy in an exploratory cohort. Findings were supported by two PC mouse models, in which circulating CD45 − EpCAM + EVs correlated with tumor volume. Remarkably, high baseline levels were associated with chemotherapy non-response and shorter overall survival. Overall, this practical, bead-calibrated FC method identified circulating CD45 − EpCAM + EVs as a promising biomarker candidate for PC. The platform may facilitate robust detection of new circulating EV markers and support disease monitoring and treatment stratification.

title: Working memory gating across sensory modalities reveals modality-specific maintenance mechanisms
abstract: The flexible resolution of the conflict between updating and maintenance demands in working memory is thought to rely on a selective gating mechanism. While gating of visual information has been extensively studied, gating of multisensory information remains poorly understood. We addressed this gap by contrasting task performance and accompanying neuro-oscillatory modulations across a purely visual and two audiovisual variants of a working memory gating task. Task-dependent performance differences emerged specifically for gate closing. Across tasks, gate closing was consistently associated with alpha band activity modulations supporting the integration of task-relevant information and beta band activity modulations controlling the reconfiguration of the gate state, while theta band activity modulations were overall negligible. However, the functional localization and relative magnitude of these oscillatory modulations varied between tasks. Together, our findings suggest that working memory gating is not amodal, but that maintenance processes in particular are shaped by the sensory context.

title: β7-Integrin worsens diet-induced metabolic syndrome in mice by altering intestinal lipid handling and colonic inflammatory monocyte infiltration
abstract: Western diet (WD)-induced metabolic syndrome (MetS) involves obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and low-grade inflammation. While β7 integrin-expressing adaptive immune cells contribute to WD-induced MetS, the role of β7 integrin in innate immunity remains unclear. To address this, the effect of antibody-mediated β7 integrin blockade or β7 integrin deficiency on WD-induced MetS was studied in recombination activating gene-2-deficient mice. Loss or inhibition of β7 integrin protected mice from WD-induced obesity, dyslipidemia, and glucose intolerance, partially via loss of β7 integrin-MAdCAM-1 interactions. β7 integrin deficiency altered intestinal lipid handling and monocyte infiltration into the colon and adipose tissue. Adoptive transfer confirmed that β7-expressing monocytes promote metabolic dysfunction in WD-fed recipients. Phospho-signaling analyses revealed attenuated PI3K-Akt pathway activation in β7 integrin-deficient colonic macrophages, and antibody treatments caused minor shifts in fecal microbiota profiles. Thus, β7 integrin-expressing innate immune cells drive WD-induced metabolic inflammation through monocyte recruitment, macrophage activation, and altered intestinal fat metabolism.

title: Thermal regulation and molecular stabilization mechanism of composite phase change material modified cement-emulsified asphalt
abstract: Increasing extreme heat events have intensified heat accumulation in urban environments, exacerbating urban heat island effects and reducing outdoor thermal comfort, thereby creating an urgent demand for thermally regulated infrastructure materials. Here, we develop a high-density polyethylene (HDPE) supported PA (paraffin) composite phase change material (CPCM) to simultaneously improve structural stability and thermal regulation performance of cement-emulsified asphalt (CEA) in road applications. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that HDPE effectively suppresses PA migration through intermolecular interactions and polymer chain entanglement, thereby enhancing CPCM stability at elevated temperatures. The optimized CPCM-CEA composite exhibits a pronounced thermal regulation effect, requiring 120 min longer to reach 50°C and maintaining a 4.3°C lower surface temperature than the control specimen under identical heating conditions. This work provided a framework for designing thermally regulated pavement materials for mitigating heat accumulation in urban environments.

title: Left atrial appendage occlusion versus antithrombotic therapy in nonvalvular AF with ASCVD and prior embolism
abstract: Managing nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and prior embolism is challenging. This retrospective study evaluated long-term outcomes of left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) compared with oral anticoagulation (OAC) and antiplatelet therapy (APT) in primary ( n = 647) and external validation ( n = 570) cohorts. The primary composite outcome included recurrent ischemic stroke or systemic embolism, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality. After inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), risks of the primary outcome, major bleeding, and mortality for LAAO were comparable with or lower than those of OAC and APT. For recurrent embolism, competing-risk analyses showed both OAC (SHR = 3.578, p = 0.003) and APT (SHR = 2.494, p = 0.040) carried a higher risk than LAAO. Results were consistent in the external validation cohort. These findings suggest LAAO may be a reasonable option for this high-risk population, offering a lower risk of recurrent embolism and comparable risk of major bleeding relative to pharmacological therapies.

title: ATP-free fatty aldehyde biosynthesis enables an autonomous lux-based bioluminescence system
abstract: Autonomous bioluminescence systems enable continuous light emission in engineered organisms by genetically encoding both luciferase enzymes and their substrate biosynthetic pathways, offering a powerful platform for non-invasive and long-term monitoring of biological processes. However, bioluminescence output is highly sensitive to substrate availability and host metabolic state, often leading to signal instability under energy-limited conditions. Here, we report an alternative luciferin biosynthetic strategy for the bacterial Lux bioluminescence system in which the adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent LuxEC complex is replaced by α-dioxygenase (αDOX), an enzyme that directly converts fatty acids into fatty aldehydes without consuming ATP. Using machine learning-guided directed evolution, we engineered αDOX variants that markedly enhanced bioluminescence intensity when coupled with bacterial luciferase. The resulting ATP-free Lux bioluminescence system enabled single-cell-level bioluminescence imaging and showed a smaller reduction in light emission than the native LuxCDABE system under several antibiotic treatments, although these experiments do not establish ATP availability as the causal mechanism.

title: Promises and limitations of current ancient human epigenetic clocks
abstract: Age-at-death estimation of archaeological human remains is central to paleodemographic research yet remains particularly challenging for adults, where osteological methods often produce imprecise age ranges. Epigenetic clocks can accurately predict chronological age in modern humans, but their applicability to ancient human DNA is unclear due to data limitations and indirect methylation inference. Here, we evaluate existing epigenetic clocks on ancient human methylomes combining high-coverage genomic data and a correction framework. Using DNA methylation estimates inferred across different CpG window sizes, neither direct clock application nor regression-based retraining produced reliable age-at-death estimates, and adult-subadult classification did not return statistically supported age classes. In contrast, X chromosome methylation separated males and females, suggesting that broad biological signals remain detectable at sufficient sequencing depth. These results indicate that current approaches can recover global biological signals but remain insufficiently sensitive to capture gradual age-related variation. Estimating age-at-death from ancient methylomes will therefore require methodological advances beyond correction alone, including reference data and improved models for inferring damage-derived epigenetic signals.

title: Long non-coding RNA prompts immune-related adverse events risk and immunotherapy response in pan-cancer
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve cancer outcomes but can cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs) that compromise treatment. Using FAERS real-world data, we developed a two-layer network algorithm to identify irAE-associated lncRNAs (irAEsLncs) across 18 cancer types. The irAEsLnc network showed organ-specific patterns and cancer-specific irAE susceptibility, while irAEsLncs were associated with immune infiltration, inflammatory responses, immune activation, and checkpoint molecules. Single-cell analysis of ICI-induced colitis linked irAEsLncs to inflammatory macrophage and T cell states and metabolic reprogramming. irAEsLnc-derived signatures independently predicted prognosis and responses to targeted therapy and immunotherapy, with ALAL-1/CD80/MEF2C predicting ICI efficacy in lung adenocarcinoma. Knockdown of ALAL-1 and SEC61G-DT suppressed tumor cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and macrophage-mediated inflammation. These findings connect irAE-associated lncRNAs with toxicity and antitumor immunity and support their potential as biomarkers for treatment stratification.

title: Mucin-rich environment shapes Pseudomonas aeruginosa cytotoxicity and phage-mediated epithelial protection
abstract: Abstract Mucin hypersecretion, a hallmark of chronic respiratory diseases (CRD), creates a complex microenvironment that reshapes host immunity and microbial behavior. However, its impact on bacteriophage therapy remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that, despite reducing Pseudomonas aeruginosa internalization, exogenous mucin increases bacterial-induced cytotoxicity and inflammation in airway epithelial cells, while driving CRD-like transcriptional changes, including hypoxia and stress responses. Under bacterial culture, mucin selectively downregulates bacterial virulence factors without impairing growth. P. aeruginosa -infecting bacteriophage DMS3vir retains full lytic activity in mucin-rich conditions and, in synergy with mucin, enhances protection against cytotoxicity in epithelial cells. DMS3vir also reduces IL-8 gene expression without triggering antiviral responses. Furthermore, mucin supplementation shapes phage-resistant P. aeruginosa phenotypes, altering colony pigmentation, pyocyanin production, and motility, influencing virulence trade-offs. These findings uncover the dual role of mucins as modulators of infection and sensitizers to phage protection, paving the way for optimized, mucosa-adapted phage therapies in chronic lung diseases.

title: Convergence of sweet and umami in the mammalian taste bud
abstract: The sense of taste enables animals to identify nutrients and avoid harmful substances. Although the five basic taste qualities—sweet, umami, bitter, sour, and salty—are mediated by distinct molecular receptors, the extent and functional significance of receptor co-expression remain intensely debated. Here, we use in vivo two-photon calcium imaging in mouse taste buds to directly visualize how taste qualities are encoded by taste receptor cells (TRCs) and by innervating gustatory fiber terminals. We find that most TRCs are selectively activated by a single taste quality. However, a significant population of TRCs responds to both sweet and umami stimuli, consistent with extensive sweet-umami double tuning among gustatory ganglion neurons. Moreover, in situ hybridization reveals co-expression of sweet and umami receptors in TRCs from both mouse tongue and human tongue biopsies. Finally, experiments with conditioned taste aversion, a basic form of learned food avoidance, show that sweet and umami taste cross-generalize behaviorally. Together, our findings reveal significant convergence between sweet and umami taste coding both in the tongue and in the peripheral gustatory neurons.

title: The potential biomarkers of organ transplantation in the era of machine perfusion: Current status, challenges, and future directions
abstract: Machine perfusion (MP) is a technology that mimics the physiological state in an ex vivo environment to preserve organs and enable their dynamic assessment. Biomarkers measured during MP hold significant promise for predicting post-transplant outcomes and guiding decisions on organ utilization. However, the clinical translation of this field is currently hindered by a lack of robust research defining the relevant biomarkers, their types, and their clinically applicable thresholds. This review outlines the development and fundamental principles of MP devices and provides a definition and classification of biomarkers. We systematically summarize and categorize potential MP biomarkers for the liver, kidney, lung, heart, and pancreas. Current research into MP biomarkers remains insufficient, and its clinical application is constrained by factors including MP platform heterogeneity and donor variability. Further studies are needed to determine the sensitivity, specificity, stability, and reproducibility, while exploring dynamic monitoring for timely assessment and intervention during MP.

title: An MMP-14/STAT3 feedback loop upregulates PD-L1 to drive immunosuppression and tumorigenesis in bladder cancer
abstract: Bladder cancer is a common genitourinary malignancy in which immune checkpoint signaling contributes to treatment resistance. Matrix metalloproteinase MMP-14 degrades the extracellular matrix to facilitate cancer cell invasion, but its intracellular signaling functions remain incompletely characterized. Using TCGA data, all-human cell models, and T cell co-culture assays, we showed that MMP-14 expression correlated with clinicopathological features, negatively regulated immune processes, and was associated with regulatory T (Treg) cell enrichment. MMP-14 promoted proliferation and reduced apoptosis of bladder cancer cells and, in co-culture, suppressed T-cell-mediated killing. Mechanistically, MMP-14 was regulated by STAT3 and directly interacted with STAT3, promoting STAT3 phosphorylation at Y705 and upregulating PD-L1 expression. These results define an MMP-14/STAT3/PD-L1 axis that drives T cell dysfunction and Treg accumulation in bladder cancer, suggesting a target for overcoming immunotherapy resistance.

title: Sexual dimorphisms of the olfactory system are conserved across bumblebee species
abstract: Bumblebees are integral to ecosystems as crucial pollinators. However, neuroscience has kept its focus on studying workers of commercially available species: Bombus terrestris (Europe), B . impatiens (North America), and B . ignitus (Asia). Here, we conducted a detailed comparative study of the brain and antennal anatomy in wild worker and male bumblebees of 6 common European species ( B. terrestris , B. pascuorum , B. pratorum , B. lapidarius , B. hypnorum , and B. lucorum ), with specific focus on their peripheral and central olfactory system. We found striking sexual dimorphisms that remain consistent across species and may underlie the differences in foraging preferences in bumblebees. We also developed a bespoke machine learning-based pipeline for automatic segmentation of confocal images of antennal lobes, which greatly speeds up the image analysis.

title: Spectrum-dependent dysbiosis and recovery patterns of the gut microbiota following antimicrobial exposure
abstract: Broad-spectrum antimicrobials profoundly alter gut microbial ecosystems; however, post-antimicrobial recovery remains incompletely understood. Here, we used a short-term oral exposure model in mice treated with clindamycin, moxifloxacin, or ceftriaxone, representing antimicrobials with distinct antibacterial spectra. Each antimicrobial induced distinct patterns of gut microbiota perturbation and cecal enlargement. At day 0, immediately after antimicrobial exposure, antimicrobial-specific differences in microbial composition and diversity were observed, followed by distinct recovery trajectories through days 3 and 5. Clindamycin induced sustained dysbiosis with limited recovery, whereas ceftriaxone caused pronounced initial disruption followed by partial recovery by day 5. Moxifloxacin produced transient perturbation with greater recovery of microbial diversity. Together, analyses of taxonomic composition, α-diversity, and β-diversity demonstrated that both the magnitude of the initial perturbation and early recovery were antimicrobial dependent. These findings delineate spectrum-dependent patterns of gut microbiota disruption and early recovery following antimicrobial exposure and highlight antimicrobial-specific effects on gut microbial resilience.

title: Mediterranean-ketogenic vs. medium-chain triglyceride supplemented Mediterranean diet: Effects on the gut-brain-immune axis in Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Ketogenic diets have been proposed as potential neuroprotective interventions for Parkinson's disease (PD), but concerns remain regarding their effects on the gut microbiome and gut-brain-immune axis. We conducted a randomized crossover trial comparing 8-week Mediterranean-ketogenic (MeDi-KD) versus medium-chain triglyceride-supplemented Mediterranean (MeDi-MCT) diets, separated by an 8-week washout (NCT05469997). Primary outcomes included changes in gut microbiome taxonomic and functional profiles, fecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production, and biomarkers of intestinal permeability and inflammation. Neither intervention significantly altered microbiome diversity or functional gene abundance, established features of PD-associated dysbiosis, nor fecal or plasma biomarkers of intestinal permeability (zonulin) or inflammation (calprotectin). The MeDi-KD modestly reduced total fecal SCFAs, while both interventions increased the relative abundance of Roseburia hominis , and the MeDi-MCT was associated with decreases in plasma IL-1β and IL-8. No severe adverse events were reported, supporting further investigation of MeDi-KD strategies in larger, longer-duration PD trials.

title: Stable Cu2O/TiO2 nanorod photoelectrodes for enhanced photoelectrochemical water splitting in ethanol-assisted systems
abstract: The heterojunction of the Cu 2 O/TiO 2 nanorod photoelectrode was synthesized via a facile hydrothermal method and electrodeposition method. The influence of Cu 2 O deposition on the structural, optical, and photoelectrochemical properties of the photoelectrodes was systematically investigated through comprehensive physicochemical characterization. Under AM 1.5 simulated solar illumination, the optimized Cu 2 O/TiO 2 nanorod photoelectrodes achieved a photocurrent density of 1.30 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE in an ethanol-containing electrolyte. The enhanced photoelectrochemical performance was attributed to improved light utilization and more efficient charge separation with suppressed electron-hole recombination resulting from the formation of the Cu 2 O/TiO 2 heterojunction. Simultaneously, ethanol also served as a sacrificial electron donor in the proposed system. Notably, the Cu 2 O/TiO 2 nanorod photoelectrodes can be promising photoelectrodes for solar-driven hydrogen production with a simple, economical, and environmentally friendly approach.

title: Extracellular neuroligin-ICAM5 coupling drives dendritic growth via actin remodeling
abstract: Neuroligins (NLGNs) organize neuronal connectivity by engaging a diverse set of interaction partners, yet how extracellular recognition couples to intracellular growth programs remains unclear. Using affinity proteomics, we identify intercellular adhesion molecule-5 (ICAM5), a cell-surface protein localized to dendritic filopodia, as a novel neuroligin interactor. Surface plasmon resonance and cell-based assays demonstrate direct binding between the ICAM5 and NLGN3 extracellular domains and reveal that ICAM5 engages all neuroligin isoforms. ICAM5 is required for NLGN-induced dendritic outgrowth, but the NLGN3–ICAM5 complex does not contribute to synaptogenesis. Mechanistically, ICAM5 sustains PAK–Cofilin signaling and F-actin organization in growth cones, positioning it as a downstream effector that links neuroligin engagement to actin remodeling. Together, these findings define a neuroligin–ICAM5 axis that couples extracellular recognition to intracellular actin remodeling to control neuronal structural development.​

title: Astrocytes improve tactile categorization by modulating sensory processing in neurons
abstract: Astrocytes are active elements in sensory processing; however, it remains unclear whether they contribute to the perception and categorization of sensory stimuli. Specifically, whether astrocytes in the secondary somatosensory cortex (S2), a higher-order cortical area whose neuronal activity underlies perceptual choices, actively contribute to this process is unknown. Here, we show that chemogenetic modulation of S2 astrocytes improves mice's performance on a categorization task. Calcium imaging shows that S2 astrocytes respond to vibrotactile stimuli in a nonlinear manner, comprising selective, variable, and inhibited response profiles. Furthermore, chemogenetic modulation of S2 astrocytes bidirectionally adjusts ensembles-specific gain of sensory-evoked neuronal responses, reshapes sensory adaptation and facilitation, and increases the signal-to-noise ratio of sensory-evoked responses. These findings demonstrate that the dynamics and interplay of S2 neuro-astrocyte circuits shape perceptual decision-making during sensory categorization.

title: Intestinal epithelial Casd1 regulates mucus sialic acid O-acetylation and limits tissue damage from large-intestinal mucosal insults
abstract: ABSTRACT The intestinal mucus network, primarily composed of O -glycosylated MUC2 mucin polymers, is essential for protecting the gastrointestinal tract from microbial threats. Sialic acid (Sia), a terminal monosaccharide on complex O -glycans, plays a key role in maintaining mucus integrity and is frequently modified by Casd1-dependent O -acetylation ( O Ac). Despite its prevalence, the biological significance of sialic acid O Ac ( O Ac-Sia) modifications in human and murine mucus remains unclear. We hypothesized that O Ac-Sia variants on mucus interact with the microbiota and are required for optimal mucus barrier function and host-microbe homeostasis in the colon. To test this, we profiled O Ac-Sia on human and mouse MUC2 in situ using viral-derived probes with bacterial FISH and confocal microscopy; generated intestinal epithelial cell (IEC)-specific Casd1 null mice (IEC Casd1 -/- ); performed sialylomic and O -glycomic HPLC-MS analyses; assessed microbial communities by 16S rRNA sequencing with quantitative microbial profiling (QMP); and evaluated disease susceptibility using DSS colitis and Citrobacter rodentium infection models. Results revealed that both human and murine mucins are extensively O -acetylated and interact with the microbiota, suggesting biological relevance. IEC Casd1 -/- mice were viable and displayed a complete loss of mucin O Ac-Sia, indicating Casd1 is the sole contributor to O Ac-status. Unexpectedly, mucus function was intact in IEC Casd1 -/- mice, with no difference in structure or quality vs. WT co-housed littermates.16S rRNA analysis showed a modest but significant sex-specific reduction of microbial loads in male IEC Casd1 -/- mice, and a clear trend toward reduced Turicibacter spp. vs. WT mice in both male and females, without impacting overall short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production. DSS treatment led to more severe and extensive tissue damage in IEC Casd1 -/- mice. C. rodentium infection led to increased damage in the cecum and distal colon of IEC Casd1 -/- mice without affecting pathogen load, suggesting that O Ac-Sia status has a role in tolerance defense. These findings establish intestinal epithelial Sia O -acetylation as a component dispensable for mucus and host-microbe homeostasis at baseline, but important in limiting damage to mucosal inflammatory insults.

title: iPSC-derived RPE and retinal organoids from two phenotypically different Stargardt disease patients show differences in ABCA4 function
abstract: Stargardt disease is a phenotypically heterogeneous disease caused by bi-allelic mutations in the ABCA4 gene. We generated retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells, photoreceptor precursors (PhRPs), and retinal organoids (ROs) from two induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cell lines derived from two phenotypically different Stargardt disease patients. We observed that RPE cells from the patient with peripheral affectation showed reduced ABCA4 expression, reduced phagocytosis and digestion of photoreceptor outer segments (POSs), and accumulation of lipid byproducts. ROs from both patients show stunted segments, more rods, caspase-3 activation, and lipofuscin accumulation at week 45 of maturation. Phenotypical differences seen in Stargardt disease patients are caused by their specific ABCA4 variants, but cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the process of photoreceptor degeneration are still poorly understood. Here, we suggest that peripheral phenotypes associated with these macular dystrophies can be linked to poor clearance of POSs by RPE cells, giving these cells a higher role in the pathogenesis of the disease.

title: Mapping the monthly habitat dynamics of greater amberjack using MaxEnt model in the Taiwan Strait: Implications for sustainable blue transformations
abstract: Understanding species-habitat relationships is critical for marine ecosystem management. We applied maximum entropy (MaxEnt) model to assess how marine environmental variables shape the monthly distribution of greater amberjack ( Seriola dumerili ) in the Taiwan Strait (20°N–28°N), using historical (2014–2019) presence data. The models demonstrated strong presence-background discrimination (AUC > 0.9, TSS > 0.75). Map-based interpretation indicates that predicted suitable habitat expands in winter, peaks across Taiwan Strait in summer, and contracts to fragmented southwestern patches by late autumn; these spatial patterns are qualitative rather than quantified area estimates. Dominant environmental contributors shifted seasonally: sea surface height and mixed layer depth in winter-spring, sea surface temperature, and salinity in summer, and mixed layer depth and temperature in autumn, with chlorophyll- a and eddy kinetic energy contributing minimally throughout. Results inform fishery-associated habitat identification and habitat-based fisheries management, within a framework linking distribution patterns to Sustainable Development Goals and blue transformation targets.

title: Metabolic exhaustion underlies sarcopenic obesity susceptibility in aging mice as revealed by multi-omics factor analysis
abstract: Background: Sarcopenic obesity (SO) affects up to 40% of older adults with obesity, yet many remain protected despite comparable metabolic burden. The molecular basis for this heterogeneity remains unknown. Methods: We exposed seventy-two 12-month-old female mice to high-fat diet (HFD) or standard diet for 7 months. Multi-Omics Factor Analysis integrated muscle transcriptomics and metabolomics to identify latent factors explaining phenotypic variation. Results: Despite uniform obesity development, aging HFD mice showed marked heterogeneity in muscle outcomes. Factor 3 uniquely distinguished dietary groups and predicted muscle dysfunction independent of adiposity severity. Factor 3 revealed metabolic exhaustion: despite coordinated upregulation of fatty acid oxidation genes (Fabp3, Lpl, Acadl) and oxidative markers, long-chain acylcarnitines accumulated and free L-carnitine depleted, indicating incomplete β-oxidation. Concurrent activation of p53, TNF/NFκB, and oxidative stress pathways indicated comprehensive metabolic decompensation. Plasma acetylcarnitine and pantothenol achieved AUC 0.91 for discriminating sarcopenia phenotypes. Conclusions: Individual susceptibility to sarcopenic obesity reflects differential metabolic exhaustion rather than obesity severity, detectable through circulating biomarkers.

title: Fine mapping of early adipogenesis identifies committed progenitors with dual white and beige potential
abstract: Thermogenic capacity in adipose tissue varies among individuals and declines with age, obesity, and insulin resistance. To investigate the cellular basis of this variability, we performed parallel white and beige adipogenic differentiation using subcutaneous adipose progenitors from six healthy subjects. Beige adipogenesis elicits subject-specific, UCP1-dependent and non-canonical thermogenic programs. Single-cell transcriptomics reveals varied proportions of progenitor populations, defined by differential expression of extracellular matrix, cell adhesion, and cytoskeletal genes. Mapping adipogenic commitment uncovers a continuum of transcriptional states largely shared between white and beige differentiation. Within this continuum, we identify ICAM1-positive committed progenitors contributing to both white and beige phenotypes. Beige induction increases the proportion of structural adipose tissue resident cells with distinct extracellular matrix signatures, suggesting early microenvironmental remodeling primes plasticity in mature cells. These results support a model in which diverse adipocyte fates arise from plastic progenitors, with individual differences in thermogenic adaptation driven by genetic, environmental, and epigenetic factors.

title: Deficiency of peripheral serotonin caused by Tph1 abrogation attenuates cerebral malaria severity
abstract: In cerebral malaria (CM), the most severe neurological complication caused by Plasmodium falciparum infection, accumulating evidence suggests that tryptophan metabolism mediates disease severity by modulating inflammation and, consequently, blood-brain barrier disruption. Here, we have established an experimental CM mouse model to dissect the differential role of the host tryptophan-serotonin metabolic axis in regulating disease pathogenesis. Peripheral serotonin-deficient mice ( Tph1 −/− ) displayed reduced mortality and blood-brain barrier permeability defects. In addition, we found that in the absence of serotonin synthesis via the enzyme Tph1, mice develop inflammation characterized by a mixed type 1 and type 2 cytokine signature. Pharmacological depletion of peripheral serotonin through injection of the Tph1 inhibitor telotristat in wild-type mice significantly improved resistance against CM. Thus, we propose that targeting serotonin synthesis through Tph1 antagonism could have a therapeutic role in P. falciparum infection and may act as a potential treatment strategy for CM. Video abstract

title: ESX-5 paralog deletions in Mycobacterium tuberculosis alter macrophage cytokine signaling and bacterial heavy metal response
abstract: (Mtb) viability and putatively linked to pathogenesis, but a functional understanding of how it interacts with the host is unknown. ESX-5 is encoded at a single genomic locus with small, paralogous, secreted targets (ESX-5a, 5b, 5c) spaced throughout the genome. To examine host-pathogen interactions of these putative virulence clusters, we made mutant strains lacking these loci and infected primary human macrophages. Surprisingly, all deletion mutants independently reduced cytokine secretion during infection, specific to certain analytes. This defect depended on viable bacteria and was mediated by a post-transcriptional mechanism. In bacterial transcriptomic analyses, each mutant downregulated heavy metal response genes compared to wild type bacteria. Treatment of Mtb with Cu or Cd led to increased ESX-5a and ESX-5c expression, concurrent with increased TNF and IL-6 secretion in macrophages compared to untreated bacilli, indicating a link between ESX-5 expression and cellular cytokine levels.

title: Remodeling of synaptome architecture following traumatic brain injury
abstract: ABSTRACT A single cortical impact in mice altered the number and molecular composition of excitatory synapses across 222 brain regions. Early effects targeted synapses with rapid protein turnover, followed by changes in slow-turnover synapses. This injury-induced remodelling of synaptome architecture mirrors responses to genetic mutation, ageing, sleep deprivation and experience, suggesting that reorganisation of excitatory synapse populations is a shared mechanism underlying brain plasticity across diverse conditions.

title: TXNIP/p-PRKAA promotes ferroptosis through the BECN1/SLC7A11 signaling pathway in intestinal ischemia/reperfusion injury
abstract: Ferroptosis has emerged as a key player in intestinal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Although BECN1 has been recognized as a crucial factor in the progression of I/R injury, its role in ferroptosis during intestinal I/R injury is still inadequately understood. In this study, we established an in vivo model of intestinal I/R injury and an in vitro model of oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) in Caco-2 cells. Our findings indicated that ferroptosis significantly contributed to the aggravation of intestinal tissue damage and cellular death. BECN1 expression levels were increased. By overexpressing or silencing BECN1, it was observed that activated BECN1 promotes ferroptosis during OGD/R by targeting SLC7A11. Furthermore, TXNIP/p-PRKAA regulates ferroptosis during I/R through the BECN1/SLC7A11 pathway. Finally, in vivo TXNIP knockout inhibited ferroptosis and attenuated intestinal I/R injury through the BECN1/SLC7A11 pathway. To summarize, this research highlights the critical role of TXNIP/p-PRKAA in modulating ferroptosis through its interaction with BECN1/SLC7A11. TXNIP and BECN1 are potential therapeutic treatment targets.

title: MEK blockade exhausts the transcriptional reserve of lipid modifications and sensitizes mutant HRAS to statins
abstract: Abstract Atorvastatin calcium (ATO), a small molecule inhibitor of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, effectively reduces endogenous cholesterol synthesis, thus becoming the basic drug for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases in clinical practice. It has been reported that the antineoplastic effect of ATO in breast cancer and pancreatic cancer; however, its efficacy in thyroid cancer remains largely unknown. Here, we demonstrated that ATO preferentially killed HRAS wild-type (HRASWT) thyroid cancer cells by decreasing AKT phosphorylation but had little effect on HRAS- or PIK3CA-mutant thyroid cancer cells. Mechanistically, ATO impaired the localization of wild-type HRAS to cell membrane by blocking its prenylation, thereby inhibiting its activity. Further studies showed that the PI3K/AKT pathway was essential for the growth of HRASWT thyroid cancer cells, but mutant HRAS mainly activated the MAPK/EKR signaling pathway in thyroid cancer cells, making them resistant to ATO. Combining ATO with MEK inhibitor produced a significant synergistic anti-tumor effect on HRAS-heterozygous mutant thyroid cancer cells by disrupting the membrane localization of HRAS via the inhibition of both prenylation and palmitoylation. Taken together, this study demonstrates that ATO selectively eradicates HRASWT thyroid cancer cells by suppressing the prenylation of HRAS proteins and proposes a new therapeutic regimen for HRAS-mutant thyroid cancers by combining ATO and MEK inhibitor.

title: PathwayFinder enables linked exploration of cell types and gene modules in spatially resolved transcriptomics data
abstract: The rapid development of spatially resolved transcriptomics technologies has provided opportunities and challenges for understanding biological systems.
