Interpreting these data requires integrated analysis of gene expression and cell types within their spatial context, however, existing tools fall short in scaling this linked interactive exploration to large-scale datasets. We present PathwayFinder, a visual analytics application designed to bridge the gap between gene-centric and cell-centric analysis. Unlike standard workflows that view cells and genes in isolation, PathwayFinder links them through a multi-scale interactive interface. This allows researchers to explore the relationships between transcriptomic profiles and tissue architecture, for example, by selecting a cell type to instantly discover its potential marker genes, or brushing gene modules to identify cell populations expressing them and their spatial distributions. Through this tight integration of gene, cell, and spatial views, PathwayFinder facilitates rapid discovery of co-expressed gene modules, specialized cell subpopulations, and functional hypotheses in spatial contexts.

title: Controlled activin A signaling enables liver organoid generation from human pluripotent stem cells
abstract: Abstract Morphogen gradients critically regulate the coordinated emergence of endodermal and mesodermal lineages during liver bud formation, yet current human hepatic organoid models inadequately replicate these spatial cues. Here we demonstrate that precise modulation of Activin A concentrations within a dynamic 3D vertical-wheel bioreactor system enables the co-emergence and spatial organization of hepatic epithelium and septum transversum mesenchyme-like populations from human pluripotent stem cells. High Activin levels induce uniform definitive endoderm and enhanced hepatic maturation, whereas low levels promote epithelial tube–like structures encased by mesenchymal cells, recapitulating early liver diverticulum architecture. This gradient-based approach autonomously generates parenchymal and non-parenchymal hepatic lineages, providing a scalable platform to model human liver organogenesis and engineer ventral foregut–derived tissues.

title: The lagged and cumulative effects of permafrost and seasonally frozen soil on water use efficiency in the Qilian Mountains, Northwest China
abstract: Permafrost in the Qilian Mountains is highly sensitive to climate change, affecting ecosystem energy, water, and carbon cycling. Using MODIS data and the self-calibrated Palmer Drought Severity Index (scPDSI), we analyzed WUE dynamics and drought responses in permafrost and seasonally frozen soil regions during 2001–2020. WUE showed an overall gradual decline and an intra-annual increase-decrease–increase pattern, with growth rates peaking in November and the lowest values occurring in June. A threshold of 0.6 gC m −2 mm −1 demarcated the two frozen-soil types. Delayed drought responses occurred in 50.77% of vegetation, with a mean lag of 6.82 months; seasonally frozen soil mainly showed non-lagged and long-term responses, whereas permafrost mainly showed non-lagged and short-term responses. Cumulative effects affected 40.49% of vegetation, with a mean duration of 5.06 months. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for understanding drought impacts on vegetation WUE across contrasting frozen-soil environments.

title: Species-specific sensorimotor noise levels explain saccadic suppression strength differences between macaques and zebrafish
abstract: Active sensing requires integrating information about self-generated movements and afferent inputs. However, such information is inherently variable and relies on uncertain extrapolations. Saccadic suppression of visual sensitivity is a classic example of sensory motor integration. Here, we used a control theory model based on efficient state estimation to predict that optimal saccadic suppression strength depends on the time-dependent magnitude of unexplained sensory and motor variability. Using two drastically different species, macaques and zebrafish larvae, we experimentally measured saccadic suppression in the superior colliculus and the homologous optic tectum. Species-specific oculomotor noise was quantified experimentally, and sensory noise was estimated. We found that inter-species differences in sensory and motor noise levels, as well as their theoretically predicted impacts on visual sensitivity, are consistent with observed differences in saccadic suppression strength. Our results highlight the importance of computational resource limits of the brain for understanding performance differences that have evolved in homologous brain areas.

title: Axonal transcriptome remodeling during PGE2 induced sensitization identifies Tnfrsf12a/FN14 as a regulator of sensory neuron excitability
abstract: Abstract Chronic pain arises when dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons become sensitised to noxious inputs, a process driven by inflammatory mediators such as prostaglandin E 2 (PGE 2 ). Local translation of axonal mRNAs is a key regulator of nociceptor plasticity, yet how axonal transcriptome dynamics contribute to inflammatory sensitisation remains unclear. Using compartmentalised culture systems and RNA-sequencing, we defined axonal and somatic transcriptomes in embryonic (E16.5) and adult (W8) DRG neurons and assessed their remodelling after PGE 2 exposure. We identify a conserved core axonal transcriptome spanning embryonic to adult stages, prominently enriched for ribosomal and mitochondrial functions, consistent with sustained translational and metabolic demands. PGE 2 elicited compartment-specific reprogramming: pathways related to sensory processing and pain were upregulated in axons but downregulated in somata. Functionally, prolonged axonal PGE 2 exposure enhanced capsaicin-evoked Ca²⁺ responses and drove retrograde sensitisation of neuronal somata. Integrating transcriptomics with functional assays, we pinpointed Tnfrsf12a (Fn14), a cytokine receptor linked to regeneration and neuropathic pain, as a PGE 2 -induced axonal mRNA. Crucially, local axonal knockdown of Tnfrsf12a significantly reduced neuronal excitability, providing proof-of-concept that axonally enriched transcripts can be targeted to modulate sensitisation. These findings position conserved axonal transcriptome programmes as drivers of peripheral sensitisation and establish Tnfrsf12a as a therapeutic candidate for inflammatory pain.

title: Automated small-scale devices and robotic systems for analyzing the cellular impact of ambient aerosol particles
abstract: In response to emerging threats associated with natural disasters, environmental pollution, and infectious diseases, the detrimental influences of airborne aerosols on humans have been investigated at the cellular level. Especially, intensive efforts have been devoted to system automation in order to enhance the efficiency, precision, and machine intelligence of aerosol cytotoxicity analysis. In this context, we combine the concepts of small-size automated and robotic platforms used for monitoring the harmful effects of aerosols. A conceptual framework is provided with a focus on mobile and field-deployable platforms that enable automated operation of (bio-)engineered systems on-site. Particular attention is given to the principles of biomimetic device design and the underlying physical and engineering mechanisms, to provide a system-level estimation on the complete "source-to-effect" workflow. In view of workflow integration, additional emphasis is placed on data acquisition and processing, as well as the extension of these technologies to autonomous system-supported environmental health applications.

title: Corrigendum to “Consensus recommendations for neurofibromatosis type 1 management in Asia Pacific” [iScience 29 (2026) 117002]
Benchmarking of cell type deconvolution techniques for microarray data
abstract: Cell type deconvolution algorithms have significantly advanced in recent years. However, a notable gap remains regarding the performance of these algorithms when applied to microarray data, which is widely available in numerous disease contexts. Here we compare the performance of existing cell type deconvolution algorithms across a spectrum of data preparation scenarios and diverse cell types within the context of microarray-based bulk transcriptome. Among the ten algorithms evaluated, MuSiC, qprogwc, and CIBERSORTx emerged as the top performers, demonstrating the highest correlation between the estimated and real cell type compositions ( r max = 0.74, 0.69, and 0.67, respectively). Our study provides a practical framework for microarray deconvolution, while also underscoring the necessity for greater precision in these techniques. Such methods would unlock the full potential of the vast repositories of microarray data in public domains, facilitating deeper insights into cellular compositions in various disease states, and promoting translational research.

title: Unrealized optimal designs challenge models of constraint in early vertebrate evolution
abstract: Jawed vertebrates dominate modern vertebrate diversity, whereas most jawless vertebrate lineages disappeared during the Devonian. Their decline has often been attributed partly to morphofunctional constraints imposed by rigid, heavily armored body plans. We tested this hypothesis in pteraspidomorphs by integrating three-dimensional geometric morphometrics, computational fluid dynamics, Pareto optimality, and phylogenetic comparative modeling. Hydrodynamic performance varied strongly across headshield morphospace, and later lineages tended to occupy more efficient regions. However, extensive areas containing highly optimal designs remained unexplored throughout the group's history. Evolutionary model fitting provided little support for hard phenotypic bounds preventing access to these regions. Pteraspidomorphs therefore retained substantial unrealized functional potential, suggesting that their extinction occurred before they fully explored the range of viable hydrodynamic solutions available to their body plan. More broadly, these results challenge interpretations in which intrinsic morphofunctional constraints exhausted the evolutionary potential of jawless vertebrates.

title: Kidney dysfunction under cardiometabolic stress promotes calorie-intake-independent wasting and frailty-like muscle phenotypes
abstract: Although age-related sarcopenia and frailty are linked to impaired metabolic flexibility and disrupted energy homeostasis, whether this framework explains chronic kidney disease (CKD)-related wasting remains unclear. We show that superimposed nephron loss redirects cardiometabolic stress from obesity and glucose intolerance toward calorie-intake-independent wasting with sarcopenic and physical frailty features. This switch was accompanied by impaired skeletal muscle glucose-utilization programs, a blunted glycemic response to gluconeogenic substrates, and altered hepatic-renal gluconeogenic programs. Integrated omics revealed suppressed glucose programs, impaired fatty acid utilization-related compensation, and amino acid catabolic signatures in skeletal muscle. Similar features occurred with aging plus nephron loss and in older human CKD kidneys with reduced renal PCK1 expression. Cornstarch-based nutritional modulation improved exercise capacity, muscle mass, and serum albumin, highlighting slow-release carbohydrate modulation as a potential therapeutic entry point. These findings support a model in which kidney dysfunction promotes wasting by limiting systemic metabolic reserve and skeletal muscle metabolic flexibility.

title: A physics-informed LLM agent for uncovering typhoon- and earthquake-induced turbine failures and offline yaw-pitch countermeasures
abstract: Extreme typhoons and earthquakes can cause severe damage to wind turbine structures, underscoring the need to better understand failure mechanisms and potential mitigation strategies. This study develops Iwind, a physics-informed large language model agent for wind-turbine engineering analysis. Supported by domain-specific training and multi-path retrieval-augmented generation, Iwind combines ReAct-style reasoning with the model context protocol to invoke the in-house physics solver Zwind for natural-language-driven load simulations. In the reported evaluations, Iwind outperformed its parent model on wind-turbine knowledge tasks and supported load-simulation execution and visual damage inspection. The collected cases showed blade fractures, tower buckling, and overturning under typhoon loading, while some earthquake-damaged turbines showed more pronounced damage in foundations or lower supporting structures. Parametric Zwind simulations further revealed W- and M-shaped offline yaw-pitch response manifolds for the investigated typhoon and earthquake cases, respectively, providing simulation-derived references for parked-state comparison and hazard-region identification. Video Abstract

title: Artificial plastic substrate for tracking and exploring antimicrobial-resistant bacteria transmission pathways in aquatic ecosystems
abstract: Investigating the persistence and dissemination of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARBs) in aquatic ecosystems is challenging because conventional methods require large volumes of water, particularly difficult to collect in regions affected by climate-related stress. This study developed and evaluated artificial plastic substrates (APSs) as an effective sampling tool and assessed the potential role of plastic as a transmission vector for ARBs. Five monthly sampling campaigns were conducted at three sites along the Arrone River. A total of 127 ARBs, including extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacteriaceae and Vibrio spp., were isolated from APSs and raw water (RW) and characterized at the microbiological and molecular levels. APSs recovered more ARBs than RW and captured key antibiotic resistance genes, including class 1 integrons and genes associated with β-lactam, carbapenem, tetracycline, sulfonamide, aminoglycoside, chloramphenicol, and efflux pump-mediated resistance. Overall, APSs proved to be an efficient, cost-effective, reproducible, and minimally invasive tool for monitoring ARBs and ARGs in aquatic ecosystems.

title: TGF-β/activin signaling balances the activity of two major protein quality control mechanisms during growth of Drosophila larval body wall muscle
abstract: Little is known about the mechanism for maintaining quality of the proteins in young and growing muscles despite that they likely face constant challenges to the protein quality control (PQC). Here we explored the role(s) of TGF-β/Activin pathway in the PQC of Drosophila skeletal muscle that grows rapidly during larval stage. We find that the TGF-β/Activin pathway positively regulates the proteasomal activity in skeletal muscle by promoting the expression of proteasomal subunits. The proteasomal activity is then necessary for proper assembly of sarcomeres and for targeting glutamate receptors to the synapse. In contrast, TGF-β/Activin pathway represses autophagy through the suppression of Atg1expression. Consequently, autophagy is elevated in TGF-β/Activin signaling-blocked muscle which in turn has a protective role against the threats to PQC. Together, these results demonstrate a multifaceted role for the TGF-β/Activin pathway in regulating PQC of young and growing muscle in Drosophila.

title: Eigenmode decomposition of asymmetries in whole-brain effective connectivity reveals multiscale hierarchical dynamics
abstract: Abstract The human brain is a complex, hierarchical system operating far from equilibrium, yet the mechanisms linking its directed network architecture to temporal irreversibility remain largely unknown. While prior studies have revealed functional and structural hierarchies, no framework has captured the hierarchical organization of the brain’s directed network in relation to its non-equilibrium dynamics. Here, we present the first large-scale eigendecomposition of whole-brain effective connectivity (EC), estimated from resting-state fMRI using sparse Dynamic Causal Modeling. We isolate the irreversible component of EC, which encodes the directionality of information flow and forms a comprehensive hierarchical network of forward and backward interactions. This hierarchy strengthens in brain states approaching criticality, where slow, oscillatory modes dominate and reflects the influence of long-range anatomical connections that scaffold whole-brain information flow. Our decomposition provides the first multiscale quantification of temporal irreversibility, revealing dual counterpropagating streams along the unimodal–transmodal axis operating at distinct frequencies. Crucially, these hierarchical dynamics carry robust, individual-specific signatures, with unimodal networks contributing disproportionately to subject identifiability. Altogether, this work delivers the first dynamic, whole-brain characterization of effective connectivity-derived hierarchies across spatiotemporal scales and individuals, offering a unified framework for studying brain hierarchy, non-equilibrium dynamics, and subject identifiability.

title: Shark and ray cartilage canals show blood vessels can exist in mature cartilage without endochondral bone formation
abstract: Abstract Although cartilage in tetrapod skeletons is typically said to lack blood vessels, this is only true for adult cartilage. In young bird and mammal cartilage, a dense network of vasculature-containing tunnels —cartilage canals— perforate the growing skeleton, helping nourish the cartilage and develop the ossification centers that will later form the skeleton’s epiphyseal bone. As the canals and their rich vascular network typically recede as animals age, the healthy cartilage of adult animals is typically known to be avascular. Here, however, we use a range of tissue characterization and visualization techniques —including light/electron microscopy and microCT— to show that the skeletons of rays and sharks (elasmobranch fishes) not only possess cartilage canals, but that these structures persist in the adult skeleton. The morphology and tissue composition of elasmobranch cartilage canals argues homology with mammalian cartilage canals and an ancient invasion of the vascular system into cartilage. However, the anatomical location of canals —extending away from mineralized tissue not toward it— and the lack of endochondral ossification in ray and shark cartilage suggest that cartilage canals developed early in vertebrates as a transport system for nutrients and mesenchymal cells into the growing skeleton. We describe distinctive features and variation in elasmobranch cartilage canals, discuss their possible roles and their potential for tissue mineralization, and the biomedical implications for their presence in a clade of animals with continuously growing cartilaginous skeletons.

title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis and preclinical validation identify lansoprazole as a therapeutic candidate for preeclampsia
abstract: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy disorder with often severe consequences across the maternal-fetal dyad and limited treatment options. We performed an integrated meta-analysis of six placental transcriptomic datasets to identify a preeclampsia-specific gene expression signature, revealing dysregulated pathways related to hypoxia, immune dysfunction, and metabolism. Multivariate INTegrative (MINT) analysis was used to establish a smaller predictive signature with potential utility for identifying circulating biomarkers for earlier preeclampsia diagnosis and monitoring disease progression. This preeclampsia signature queried against a transcriptomic database of more than 1,000 compounds identified lansoprazole, a widely used proton pump inhibitor with an established safety profile, as the top-ranked compound based on its ability to reverse the preeclampsia-associated gene expression signature. Protective benefits of lansoprazole were confirmed using a murine model of immune-mediated fetal wastage where treatment overturned elevated soluble FLT1 levels with significantly improved pregnancy outcomes. These findings support further investigation of lansoprazole as a potential therapy for preeclampsia.

title: Reaction time-related compression underlies overestimation of time-constrained reachability
abstract: Humans continuously estimate whether an action can be completed within a limited time window, yet the mechanisms underlying such implicit evaluations remain unclear. Across three experiments (N = 52 in total), we used a novel psychophysical paradigm to quantify reachability judgments in an arm-reaching task. Participants consistently judged actions as possible even when the available time was shorter than their actual execution time, indicating an overestimation of time-constrained reachability. This bias contrasts with explicit motor imagery, where imagined durations typically exceed execution times. Crucially, by dissociating reaction and movement components, we show that this overestimation arises from selective temporal compression of the premotor phase, while movement time is largely preserved. Misperception of external duration did not account for the effect. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized cognitive bias and provide new insights into how humans prospectively evaluate their own motor capabilities.

title: Extending digital biology: Bacterial survival and morphological heterogeneity under antibiotic stress
abstract: Bacterial morphology is modified by antibiotic stress depending on the antibiotic mechanism of action, while changes in morphology can contribute to cell survival. Here we present a workflow that generates morphological signatures for the progeny of individual bacterial cells across 168 antibiotic conditions. The workflow uses stationary microfluidic droplets to encapsulate and grow bacteria and confocal microscopy to image the droplet content. A custom image analysis pipeline labels morphologies in a subset of images to train a neural network. The network yields multidimensional morphological signatures from 82,000 droplets, showing the co-existence of different morphologies even for the progeny of individual cells. The signatures differ with antibiotic type and concentration, providing a way to distinguish antibiotics by their mode of action. Combined with digital detection of bacterial survival within droplets, this workflow provides a quantitative platform to investigate antibiotic resistance and identify the antimicrobial activity of unknown compounds.

title: Gut microbiota composition of India’s Baiga tribe: Insights from an indigenous particularly vulnerable tribal group
abstract: The transition from traditional foraging lifestyles to modernized urban environments is associated with reduced human gut microbiome diversity. To examine this shift within the Indian subcontinent, we used shotgun metagenomics to compare the gut microbiota of 50 adults: 25 from the indigenous, foraging, and particularly vulnerable Baiga tribe and 25 from an urban population in Bhopal, Central India. The Baiga maintained a diverse ecosystem enriched with fiber-degrading bacteria such as Roseburia and Faecalibacterium , forming networks suited to complex carbohydrate fermentation. The urban microbiome showed lower phylogenetic diversity and evenness, with higher relative abundance of Prevotella copri and dairy-adapted taxa. Functionally, the tribal gut retained pathways for environmental sensing and complex plant metabolism, whereas the urban gut was enriched in pathways associated with potential inflammation. These findings identify the Baiga as a reservoir of preserved human microbial diversity relevant to metabolic health.

title: Photocatalytic strategies for mitigating microplastic pollution and greenhouse gas emissions
abstract: Microplastics contaminate water, soil, and air, and their persistence is linked to greenhouse gas emissions. Photocatalysis can break down these polymers via reactive oxygen species but particle shrinkage alone does not prove complete mineralization. Recent photocatalytic systems are examined, including TiO 2 -based materials, S-scheme and Z-scheme heterojunctions, laddered architectures, metal-organic frameworks, and g-C 3 N 4 composites. These systems improve charge separation and visible-light harvesting, with some achieving high mineralization under optimized conditions. Verifying true breakdown requires TOC, LC-MS, and GC-MS because incomplete oxidation can produce toxic intermediates. Photocatalysis may also shorten plastic residence times and reduce methane and nitrous oxide emissions, though this depends on carbon fate, catalyst stability, energy inputs, and water chemistry. Combining photocatalysis with renewable energy and water treatment could offer a practical route to microplastic management, provided catalyst recovery, toxicity, and scale-up challenges are addressed.

title: Brain-computer interfaces for neurodegenerative diseases: A comprehensive review of closed-loop systems from diagnosis to neural rehabilitation
abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology serves as an important bridge between the nervous system and external devices and has shown considerable promise for the diagnosis and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, whose global burden continues to increase: in 2021, more than 57 million people were living with dementia worldwide, with Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounting for approximately 60–70% of cases, while an estimated 11.77 million people were living with Parkinson's disease (PD) in 2021, according to the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. This growing disease burden, together with the progressive loss of cognitive, motor, and communicative functions, highlights the need for more precise approaches to early detection, functional assistance, and individualized intervention. Conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches remain poorly suited to early detection and timely intervention. This paper analyzes the development of BCI technology, from the first detection of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals to the parallel development of invasive and non-invasive systems, and outlines the basic principles of signal acquisition, processing, and decoding, together with the relative advantages and limitations of different approaches. It then focuses on the use of BCI in Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), covering early diagnosis, functional reconstruction, and neuromodulation. The article also discusses the difficulties encountered by BCI technology in terms of technological realization, clinical translation, and ethical considerations, as well as several future research directions, including multimodal fusion, adaptive algorithms, closed-loop control systems, and personalized treatment so as to drive the applications of BCI in precision medicine and in neurological diseases.

title: A narrative review of advances in experimental models of bTBI and neurobehavioral outcome measures
abstract: Blast-induced traumatic brain injury (bTBI) is a common neurological trauma in warfare and terrorist attacks. The use of improvised explosive devices raises its incidence, affecting both soldiers and civilians and bringing heavy medical and social burdens. Dominated by blast shockwaves, bTBI has complex mechanisms hindering early diagnosis. This review summarizes bTBI advances in experimental models, research techniques, primary/secondary pathological mechanisms, neurobehavioral phenotypes, and prognostic factors, differentiating animal and clinical evidence. It addresses existing limitations and proposes future directions, to support early recognition, precise diagnosis, and targeted neuroprotective therapies for bTBI.

title: Multimodal in vitro biocompatibility assessment of functionalized PEDOT neural interfaces
abstract: Conductive polymers such as poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) have emerged as promising neural interface materials due to their favorable electrochemical and mechanical properties. However, biological assessment of new bioelectrode coatings remains dependent on conventional cytotoxicity assays and animal studies, providing limited insight into cell-material interactions. Here, we present a multimodal in vitro framework for evaluating the biocompatibility of functionalized PEDOT coatings as neural interfaces. Standard PEDOT:PSS, functionalized PEDOT:polydopamine (PDA), and PEDOT:dopamine-grafted hyaluronic acid (DAHA) coatings were characterized electrochemically and assessed using SH-SY5Y cells through viability measurements, profilometry, 3D reconstruction, immunofluorescence imaging, and targeted gene expression analysis. While all coatings support cell viability, substrate-dependent differences were observed in cellular organization, multicellular aggregation, extracellular-matrix- and focal-adhesion-associated architecture, and the expression of genes related to cell-matrix interactions and intercellular communication. Our findings demonstrate mechanistic insights surpassing conventional tests, a valuable intermediate step to guide material development prior to in vivo experiments.

title: Transcriptomic conservation defines autoimmune stem-like T cells and uncovers their dependence on Apex1
abstract: Stem-like T cells (T STEM ) critically govern autoimmune responses. Unlike individual transcriptional master regulators of specialized T cells, the primary molecular determinant of T STEM , Tcf1, is shared with naive and other T cells. To unequivocally identify autoimmune T STEM , we established transcriptomic characteristics conserved across multiple immunological settings. We leveraged such conserved features to faithfully distinguish T STEM arising de novo among other Tcf1 + T cells and confirmed their autoimmune functions in vivo in a model of multiple sclerosis. We further detected the transcriptomically identifiable T STEM in corresponding human diseases, and among such T cells we uncovered a specifically increased expression of apurinic/apyrimidinic endodeoxyribonuclease 1 ( APEX1 ). By rigorously investigating Apex1-deficient T STEM in a disease model, we confirmed indispensable roles of Apex1 in governing the disease-producing functions of autoimmune T STEM . Thus, we established conserved features of autoimmune T STEM across species barriers and uncovered APEX1/Apex1 as a functional determinant of T STEM .

title: Sequence of aerobic and resistance exercise influences short- and long-term glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: A randomized trial
abstract: Combined aerobic and resistance exercise improves glycemic control in type 2 diabetes (T2D), yet whether the sequence of the two exercise modalities influences glycemic outcomes remains unclear. We examined acute and long-term glycemic responses to aerobic-then-resistance (AR, n = 28) versus resistance-then-aerobic (RA, n = 28) exercise in 56 community-dwelling adults with T2D over 8 weeks (3 sessions/week). Aerobic exercise was performed on bicycle ergometers for 30 min at 40%–70% heart-rate reserve; resistance exercise targeted major muscle groups at 60%–80% 1RM. Compared with pre-exercise levels, mean glucose ( p = 0.043) and HbA1c ( p = 0.007) decreased only in AR group. Among participants without insulin treatment, insulin levels fell in both groups (AR: p < 0.001; RA: p = 0.001). At week 8, AR showed lower glucose during exercise and recovery ( p = 0.036) and greater nocturnal glucose reduction ( p = 0.015) than RA. Similar conventional improvements seen in both sequences, yet aerobic-first lowered mean/nocturnal glucose at the cost of greater variability, while resistance-first minimized fluctuations.

title: Torsade de pointes risk assessment categorization calculator based on an international multisite study of hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes
abstract: New approach methodologies (NAMs) including human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) coupled with high-throughput platforms such as multielectrode array (MEA) and voltage-sensing optical (VSO) have proven useful for evaluating proarrhythmic risk. Despite the hiPSC-CM comprehensive in vitro proarrhythmia assay (CiPA) focus on proarrhythmic potential, risk assessment scores are not routinely included in regulatory submissions. To address this gap, we developed an open-source, web-based torsade de pointes (TdP) risk assessment categorization (TRAC) calculator utilizing the validated TdP model. The calculator employs a logistic regression model based on three hiPSC-CM compound-induced response predictors. Here, we present a JavaScript implementation of the published regression model equation. By streamlining TdP risk estimation, this tool assists the translatability of nonclinical data and provides an automated approach to evaluate compound safety. This easy-to-use online calculator based on the HESI CiPA myocyte validation TdP model enables routine use with standard laboratory devices.

title: Spatial transcriptomic mapping of anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis reveals perivascular enrichment of type I interferon responses and immune activation
abstract: Abstract Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM), also known as myositis, are a rare and heterogeneous group of autoimmune disorders characterized by chronic inflammation of skeletal muscle. Other organs are also frequently affected, such as skin, joints, and lungs, leading to morbidity and even mortality. Anti-MDA5 autoantibody-positive dermatomyositis (MDA5+ DM) is a unique subtype with a high mortality rate but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, we profiled the spatial transcriptome of a cohort of healthy controls, MDA5+, and MDA5- muscles and found a distinct transcriptomic profile of the MDA5+ muscles with a low percentage of stressed myofibers but increased immune cell infiltration. Niche analysis revealed a distinct microenvironment in the MDA5+ muscles with the endothelial cell (EC) niche showing increased inflammation, dampened oxygen transport function, and a unique enrichment of the Type 1 interferon response. Cell-cell communication and pathway activity analysis uncovered that hypoxia, TGF-β, NF-κB, and TNF-α signaling were enriched in the MDA5+ EC niche. Altogether, our results support a vasculopathy model whereby blood vessels exhibit a strong inflammatory response and impaired oxygen transport function, leading to vasculopathy and perivascular immune cell infiltration in MDA5+ muscles.

title: Deciphering early tau pathology events using an Alzheimer’s disease-seeded organotypic hippocampal slice culture model
abstract: In Alzheimer's disease, the spreading of the tau pathology through the brain is assumed to rely on pathological species of tau acting as seeds. To better understand the underlying mechanisms, we need models allowing us to study tau seeding in a brain-like environment. We developed an ex vivo model based on organotypic hippocampal slice cultures prepared from transgenic mouse pups expressing human pro-aggregative mutant tau. We show for the first time that human brain-derived tau seeds are able to potentiate tau pathology in such cultures. Moreover, tau seeds are generated ex vivo , completing the validation of the model. Then, we shed light on the initial events of tau seeding: tau pathology appears sequentially, first in neurites and then in cell bodies, and misfolding (MC1+) precedes pathological phosphorylation (pS422, pT217). Altogether, this makes the present model a highly valuable bioassay to decipher the molecular and cellular mechanisms leading to tau pathology development.

title: Programmable DNA-Silk hydrogel with temporal mechanical reinforcement for mesenchymal stem cell differentiation and accelerated wound healing
abstract: Abstract DNA-based hydrogels have attracted significant attention in biomedical applications due to their programmability, biocompatibility, and tunable functionalities. However, their clinical translation is hindered by high synthesis costs, limited mechanical strength, poor stability, and complex synthesis protocols. In this work, we present a novel DNA-silk fibroin hybrid hydrogel that overcomes these limitations by combining the unique biofunctionality of DNA with the superior mechanical and chemical properties of silk fibroin. Salmon-derived DNA, an abundant and low-cost source, was incorporated with silk fibroin to form hybrid networks via a simple, scalable process. Silk fibroin served as a robust scaffold, enhancing mechanical strength, controlling degradability, and improving structural stability, while the entangled DNA-silk network reduced rapid DNA degradation. The resulting hybrid hydrogel demonstrated temporal mechanical reinforcement and prolonged stability, with in vitro studies demonstrating that the developed hybrid hydrogel enhanced the chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation of Infrapatellar Fat Pad Mesenchymal Stem Cells (IFP-MSCs). Additionally, hemostatic and in vivo studies demonstrated the potential of DNA-silk fibroin hydrogel as a promising biomaterial for rapid hemostasis and accelerated wound healing. Overall, the developed DNA-silk fibroin hybrid hydrogel offers strong potential for mesenchymal tissue engineering, hemostatic adjuvant and wound healing.

title: In situ-activated engineered bacteria release combined dual-therapeutic proteins for tumor immunotherapy
abstract: The combination of antitumor agents is pivotal for effective tumor immunotherapy. However, achieving precise, in situ co-delivery of therapeutic payloads remains a considerable challenge. Here, we developed a dual-payload-loaded Salmonella typhimurium strain capable of releasing granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) and CD47 nanobody (CD47nb) in response to tumor hypoxia and bacterial quorum sensing (QS). GM-CSF promotes dendritic cell (DC) maturation and enhances M1-like macrophage infiltration, facilitating antigen presentation and CD8 + T cells activation. CD47nb blocks the CD47-SIRPα signaling axis, thereby enhancing macrophage-mediated tumor cells phagocytosis. The combined delivery increased mature DC infiltration from 13.5% to 34.9%, promoted M1-like macrophage activation and CD8 + T cell accumulation in the tumor microenvironment (TME), suppressed tumor growth by 83.7%, and extended the median survival from 14 to 28 days compared with PBS-treated mice. In summary, our findings support precise, in situ delivery of complementary immunomodulators as a promising strategy for tumor immunotherapy.

title: Microbial proteins shape the development of Fab-dimerized glycan-reactive antibodies that target glycosylated HIV-1 envelope
abstract: Fab-dimerized glycan (FDG)-reactive antibodies (Abs) bind a myriad of glycosylated pathogens in a glycan-dependent manner. We defined microbial proteins that bound FDG-reactive monoclonal (m) Abs from human HIV-1 infection (2G12), HIV-1 seronegative human (DH1005), and Simian-HIV (SHIV)-infected (DH851.3) and HIV-1-vaccinated (DH717.2) rhesus macaques. FDG mAbs bound diverse proteins in Candida albicans lysates, including 1,3-beta-glucanosyltransferase PGA4 (PGA4). Recombinant PGA4 was bound by FDG-reactive mAbs in a predominantly glycan-dependent manner, and tetrameric PGA4 induced calcium flux in a Ramos B cell line expressing DH1005 IgM BCR, suggestive of B cell activation. Additionally, we identified multiple bacterial proteins in human stool-derived intestinal microbiota whole-cell lysates that bound FDG-reactive mAbs, including the Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain XcpQ protein. Recombinant XcpQ was also bound by FDG-reactive mAbs in a glycan-dependent manner. These data provide insights into microbial factors that may contribute to the induction and development of this unique category of glycan-reactive antibodies.

title: The ssDNA-binding protein MEIOB sustains synaptonemal complex integrity by stabilizing recombination intermediates during male meiosis
abstract: The synaptonemal complex (SC) is fundamental to meiotic recombination and crossover formation between homologous chromosomes. In yeast, the SC is assembled and sustained by the ZZS complex (Zip2-Zip4-Spo16). However, how ZZS components are recruited and stabilized at chromosomes, and whether their mammalian orthologs (SHOC1-TEX11-SPO16) play similar roles, remain poorly understood. Here, we report that germ cell-specific ablation of the meiosis-specific single-stranded DNA-binding protein MEIOB in mice causes premature chromosomal desynapsis in early pachytene spermatocytes, leading to their elimination before mid-pachytene. Mechanistically, MEIOB associates with SPO16 in vitro , and Spo16 -deficient pachytene-like spermatocytes display comparable premature desynapsis and severely reduced MEIOB foci on chromosomal axes. Moreover, the recruitment of another ZZS component, TEX11, to recombination intermediates is markedly diminished in Meiob knockout pachytene spermatocytes. Together, our findings suggest that the MEIOB-SPATA22 complex may cooperate with SPO16 to support SC integrity and crossover formation during mammalian meiosis.

title: Connectome analysis reveals brain-wide visual processing in Drosophila
abstract: Abstract Sensory processing relies on an intricate interplay between specialized sensory circuits and the broader brain. Leveraging the whole-brain Drosophila melanogaster connectome, we analyzed long-range projections linking the optic lobe (OL)—the principal visual center—reciprocally with the central brain and the contralateral OL to determine how visual features are computed by a brainwide network. By quantifying synaptic polarity and connectivity, we classified the projection neurons into feedforward, feedback, and bilateral groups. Feedforward neurons form an information bottleneck, consolidating diverse visual features from the OL and distributing them through modular pathways for higher-order processing. Feedback neurons densely innervate OL structures, conveying contextual signals in the central brain via precise recurrent loops. Bilateral neurons link local visual circuits across the two OLs, providing a substrate for inter-ocular processing. These findings reveal how early visual pathways interface with brainwide circuits to support diverse brain functions and enable context-dependent flexibility in sensory computation. Highlights Whole-brain connectome analysis identifies three streams of brainwide visual processing Feedforward neurons form a bottleneck and distribute features for higher processing Feedback neurons modulate early vision via layer-specific recurrent loops Bilateral neurons bridge both optic lobes to enable inter-ocular processing

title: Cell-cycle inhibition preserves robust development but rebalances lineages in mouse gastruloids
abstract: Cell differentiation and proliferation are fundamental to multicellular development. While studies in various non-mammalian species show that development can proceed despite disrupted cell-cycle progression, the extent to which normal cell-cycle dynamics are required in mammals remains unclear. Using mouse gastruloids, we examined the effects of cell-cycle inhibition on development. Despite near-complete growth arrest, gastruloids still underwent symmetry breaking, elongation, and germ-layer specification, indicating that core differentiation programs are robust to growth inhibition. However, microscopy and single-cell transcriptomics revealed consistent alterations in cell-type proportions, including delayed differentiation and reduced mesodermal populations. To investigate these changes, we used the differential kinetics of unspliced and spliced cycling transcripts to compare proliferation rates between cell types. While differences in proliferation partly explained the imbalance, our analysis showed that cell-cycle perturbations also modulate lineage-specific differentiation timing and efficiency, highlighting a regulatory role of cell-cycle dynamics in mammalian development.

title: Positive emotional contagion by laughter-like 50-kHz ultrasonic vocalizations in rats
abstract: Rats display advanced empathic abilities, yet current research is focused on empathy toward negative affect, largely neglecting positive affective states. We therefore developed a paradigm suitable for assessing both negative and positive emotional contagion. It relies on ethotransmission (i.e., acoustic emotional communication) of affective states to conspecifics via ultrasonic vocalizations (USV), i.e., alarming 22-kHz USV (negative affect) and laughter-like 50-kHz USV (positive affect). Specifically, we subjected rats to playback of 22-kHz or 50-kHz USV, while assessing their acoustic startle response (ASR), which is known to be emotionally modulated (i.e., potentiated and attenuated by negative and positive affect, respectively). Here, 50-kHz but not 22-kHz USV strongly attenuated the ASR across sexes and development, suggesting that laughter-like 50-kHz USV induced positive affect in receivers, indicative of positive emotional contagion. Our paradigm provides the first quantitative assessment of positive emotional contagion in rats through capitalizing on ethological signals (USV) and simple reflexes (ASR).

title: Quantum-enhanced trusted execution with dynamic policy optimization for zero-trust edge computing
abstract: Zero-trust edge computing faces escalating security challenges from quantum threats, heterogeneous resources, and dynamic operational conditions. This paper proposes Q-TEE-DSO, a collaborative architecture integrating quantum-enhanced trusted execution environments with post-quantum cryptography and reinforcement learning-based dynamic security optimization. By embedding quantum random number generation and lightweight quantum key distribution into hardware-enforced TEEs, the framework strengthens trust-root initialization and session-key establishment under quantum-aware threat models. Instruction-level optimization of lattice-based PQC algorithms, combined with enclave-aware memory isolation and side-channel mitigation, reduces cryptographic overhead on constrained edge devices. A reinforcement learning-driven DSO-Engine dynamically adapts encryption strength, access control policies, and privacy-preserving computation modes according to real-time system load and threat levels. Experimental evaluations on heterogeneous testbeds demonstrate a 37% reduction in cryptographic latency and 42% improvement in energy efficiency compared with conventional approaches, alongside 99.88% availability, robust heterogeneous compatibility, and stable long-term operation across diverse network topologies.

title: Oncogenic CLDN1 promotes thyroid cancer progression through TAp63-mediated glycolytic switching
abstract: Thyroid cancer (TC) incidence has risen globally, with advanced cases showing limited treatment options and poor prognosis. Claudin-1 (CLDN1), a tight junction protein, has context-dependent roles in cancer, but its function in TC remains unclear. Integrated bioinformatic analysis of TCGA and GEO datasets identified CLDN1 as a key hub gene upregulated in TC and associated with poor survival. Functional experiments demonstrated that CLDN1 knockdown suppressed TC cell proliferation, migration, and glycolytic metabolism, while its overexpression promoted these effects. Mechanistically, CLDN1 activated the TAp63 pathway, upregulating glycolytic enzymes (HK2, PKM2, and GLUT1) and enhancing glucose uptake, lactate production, and NADPH/NADP + ratio. The glycolysis inhibitor 2-DG reversed CLDN1-driven oncogenic phenotypes in vitro and in vivo . In xenograft models, CLDN1 overexpression accelerated tumor growth, which was mitigated by 2-DG treatment. Collectively, CLDN1 drives TC progression by reprogramming glycolytic metabolism via the TAp63 pathway, suggesting the CLDN1-glycolysis axis as a potential therapeutic target for TC.

title: RBM42 couples alternative splicing to cytoskeletal organization to direct cortical development
abstract: Alternative splicing coordinates gene expression programs that shape the developing cerebral cortex. Here, we used nervous system-specific Rbm42 conditional knockout mice, RBM42-depleted human SH-SY5Y cells, RNA sequencing, RIP-seq, proteomics, and splice-switching rescue to define how the spliceosomal RNA-binding protein RBM42 supports cortical development. Rbm42 loss caused perinatal lethality, cortical thinning, defective lamination, reduced progenitor proliferation, increased apoptosis, and disrupted neuronal cytoskeletal organization. RBM42 bound and regulated cytoskeleton-associated transcripts, including NIN / Nin and NUMA1 / Numa1 , and its loss altered their splicing in human cells and mouse cortex. Restoring RBM42 corrected these splicing defects and improved proliferation and neurite growth. Selective correction of NIN exon 18 mis-splicing partially restored βIII-tubulin organization and proliferation but did not rescue apoptosis. These findings connect spliceosome-dependent isoform control with cytoskeletal remodeling during cortical development and provide a mechanistic framework for RBM42-associated neurodevelopmental disease.

title: Admission blood-interstitial glucose gap shows metabolic and prognostic associations in mechanically ventilated patients
abstract: Glucose concentration differences across vascular and interstitial compartments may provide complementary insights into metabolic status during critical illness. In this prospective observational study, we obtained synchronized arterial, venous, and interstitial glucose measurements from 140 mechanically ventilated patients. The arterial-venous glucose gap (Gap A-V ) demonstrated greater discrimination for three-month all-cause mortality than the arterial-interstitial glucose gap (Gap A-I ), with areas under the curve of 0.863 and 0.708, respectively. In contrast, Gap A-I was strongly associated with insulin resistance (HOMA-IR, r = −0.85) and resting energy expenditure measured by indirect calorimetry ( r = 0.79). Combining Gap A-I with lactate identified four exploratory metabolic phenotypes with distinct metabolic characteristics and survival outcomes. These findings suggest that glucose gaps capture complementary prognostic and metabolic information, warranting further validation in independent cohorts.

title: PET bottle recycling system in Asia: Lessons learned from six cities
abstract: The rapid growth of bottled water consumption has increased post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottle waste, while the recycling performance varies substantially across Asian cities. This study comparatively examines PET bottle recycling systems in Tokyo, Seoul, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Bangkok, and Kuala Lumpur, focusing on policy and governance, producer and recycler practices, recycling technologies, market conditions, and informal recycling actors. The results reveal distinct recycling pathways: Tokyo and Seoul have mature policy systems and are advancing high-value recycling. Shanghai has a dynamic market-led system dominated by downcycling. Hong Kong shows gradual policy improvement but limited effectiveness, and Bangkok and Kuala Lumpur remain highly reliant on informal recycling under weak enforcement. These differences highlight the importance of coordinated policy, market, technology, and social actors in shaping urban PET recycling outcomes. The study identifies transferable practices, including source separation, inclusive integration of informal recyclers, extended producer responsibility, and effective government coordination, providing guidance for improving PET recycling systems across Asia.

title: VIRMA-associated SRD5A2 downregulation promotes BPH progression through ERα-CREB5-dependent epithelial plasticity
abstract: Some patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) show a poor response to 5α-reductase inhibitor (5-ARI) therapy, potentially due to reduced expression of 5α-reductase type 2 (SRD5A2) in prostatic tissues. Here, we identified decreased VIRMA and SRD5A2 expression in a subset of human BPH tissues. Mechanistic studies in prostate epithelial cells revealed that VIRMA depletion reduces SRD5A2 mRNA stability, leading to altered intraprostatic hormone balance and enhanced estradiol signaling. Elevated estradiol promoted estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) activation and increased cAMP response element-binding protein 5 (CREB5) expression, which was required for epithelial phenotypic changes. These epithelial alterations were associated with stromal remodeling and disease progression. In a hormone-induced rat model, pharmacological inhibition of ERα attenuated prostate enlargement and tissue remodeling, supporting a functional role of ERα signaling in this process. These findings reveal a VIRMA-SRD5A2 regulatory axis and ERα-CREB5-dependent epithelial plasticity as contributors to BPH progression and 5-ARI resistance.

title: Individual olfactory channels shape distinct parameters of sleep architecture
abstract: Across the animal kingdom, olfactory dysfunction and anosmia have been associated with disruptions in sleep. In the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, various studies have demonstrated that broadly inhibiting olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) similarly disrupts sleep/wake cycles, suggesting that baseline ORN signaling is an integral component of olfactory modulation of sleep. However, due to the diversity of ORNs and combinatorial nature of olfactory processing, many of the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which ORNs modulate sleep remain unclear. In this study, we addressed this gap of knowledge by characterizing the contributions of different ensembles of ORNs, individual ORN types, and a known modulator of ORNs on baseline sleep architecture. We find that the activity of distinct ORN types are important for day and nighttime sleep and heterogeneously shape parameters of sleep architecture. Importantly, the effects of ORN signaling on sleep are adjusted across mating status, suggesting that distinct ORN types are recruited within the context of sleep depending on the demands of the animal. Furthermore, the effects of ORN signaling on sleep are in part shaped by heterogeneous serotonin (5-HT) receptor expression. Together, this work identifies cellular and molecular pathways bridging olfaction and sleep, and helps establish a circuit model that can be used to further characterize the behavioral consequences of sensory dysfunction.

title: An explainable machine-learning framework for seasonal early warning of West Nile virus using predictive climate data
abstract: Reliable early-warning systems capable of forecasting West Nile virus (WNV) outbreaks months before the transmission season remain limited. We developed an explainable machine-learning framework that uses seasonal climate forecasts rather than in-season reanalysis, combined with epidemiological, climatic, hydroclimatic, demographic, land-cover, and spatial predictors. The model was independently evaluated under real-world conditions at municipal and regional scales in Greece during 2022–2025 and across 887 areas in 14 European countries during 2022–2024. Explainability analysis identified epidemiological memory, seasonal temperature, hydroclimatic persistence, and environmental suitability as key determinants of outbreak risk. Across Europe, the model detected 89% of outbreaks in previously unaffected areas, demonstrating transferability and the potential of integrating prospective climate information with epidemiological history to support targeted WNV surveillance, vector control, and public health preparedness. Skill losses were not attributable to climate forecast errors, highlighting the value of higher frequency epidemiological surveillance (mosquitoes, sentinels) data, which are rarely publicly available.

title: Nemo-like kinase limits T cell activation while preserving anti-tumor responses
abstract: T cell dysfunction limits the efficacy of cancer immunity, yet the molecular checkpoints that preserve T cell function within the tumor microenvironment are not fully understood. In this study, we identify a previously unrecognized, T cell-intrinsic role for nemo-like kinase (NLK) as a critical mediator of sustained anti-tumor responses. In our experiments, NLK emerged as a dual-function modulator: although NLK deficiency in CD4 + and CD8 + T cells increases proliferation and cytokine production in vitro via enhanced NFAT and AP-1 activation, its loss in vivo paradoxically impairs tumor control. In murine tumor models, NLK-deficient tumor-infiltrating T cells exhibit blunted effector activity resulting in accelerated tumor progression. Conversely, human chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells that overexpress NLK demonstrate superior killing capacity toward target tumor cells. These findings establish NLK as an essential early brake on T cell activation while protecting against their chronic dysfunction, and reveal a molecular pathway that sustains anti-tumor immunity.

title: Neurocognition of dance: Guidelines for using dance as model behavior and research subject in cognitive neuroscience
abstract: Dance and movement science bridges cognitive psychology, neuroscience, cultural studies, philosophical aesthetics, and the performing arts. The field has evolved significantly, examining physical, social, psychological, and neural aspects of dance and movement execution and perception, contributing to a deeper understanding of human cognition and of dance itself. As the field expands, shared guidelines that support methodological rigor, reproducibility, and cultural relevance are of paramount importance. This paper synthesizes current research and introduces a comprehensive seven-principle research design framework for using dance in cognitive neuroscience. Key elements include the operationalization of "dance" in empirical sciences, the definition of who is a dancer, measures of expertise, and the importance of a culturally sensitive, holistic, and interdisciplinary approach to its investigation in the laboratory and in ecologically valid settings. This framework benefits research in dance and movement aesthetics, as well as investigations in social cognition, affective neuroscience, computer science, and artificial intelligence.

title: Corrigendum to “Differential activation of TCA cycle activity and PDH flux by dichloroacetate in skeletal muscle measured by hyperpolarized [2-13C,3-2H3]pyruvate” [iScience 29 (2026) 117325]
abstract: In the original published version of this article, the line colors (light/dark lines) are swapped in both Figure 2E and 2G, resulting in mismatches with the legend.Figure captions and main text are correct and no changes are needed.

title: Identification of multi-omics molecular programs from the peripheral circulation of patients with PAH
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) involves progressive remodeling of the pulmonary vasculature and right ventricle, yet much of our understanding of disease progression relies on rodent studies because opportunities for investigation in humans are limited. We integrated plasma proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic profiles from 402 patients with PAH and 76 healthy controls using latent-network discovery and graphical modeling, with validation in an external cohort and comparison with human and bovine tissue. PAH was associated with broad molecular remodeling across peptides, metabolites, and lipids, with multiple multi-Omic programs converging on disruptions in the TCA cycle. Of note, elevated 2-hydroxyglutarate distinguished PAH across etiologies and comorbidity profiles, was associated with survival and treatment intensity, and was replicated externally. Related TCA-cycle changes were also observed in pulmonary vascular stromal and immune cells. These findings reveal coordinated remodeling across multiple molecular axes and highlight plasma multi-omics as a bridge between clinical phenotypes and tissue-level metabolic reprogramming.

title: Monocyte TNF superfamily receptor dysregulation in tuberculosis-type 2 diabetes mellitus comorbidity
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases susceptibility to tuberculosis (TB) and contributes to immune dysregulation, partly through altered monocyte signaling. Although our earlier work has demonstrated that T2DM alters monocyte subsets and promotes hyper-inflammatory responses during TB, the mechanisms underlying dysregulated TNF superfamily pathways in TB-T2DM comorbidity are underexplored. A study cohort of 176 individuals (TB, TB-T2DM, T2DM-only, and healthy controls) was evaluated. Classical monocytes (CD14 + CD16 − ; n = 20/group) from peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analyzed by flow cytometry for cytokines and activation markers upon stimulation with purified protein derivative (PPD), whole-cell lysate (WCL), and TLR2/4 ligands. Plasma TNF superfamily receptors ( n = 44/group) were quantified using Human ProcartaPlex 12-plex multiplex ELISA. Associations were analyzed using Spearman correlation, and integrated network analyses including protein-protein interaction (PPI), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and Gene Ontology (GO) were performed. In the results, TB-T2DM individuals exhibited significantly increased intercellular cytokines (IL-6, IL-12, IL-1β, IL-1α, IL-10, and TNF-α) and activation markers (PDL-2, CD163, and CD206) compared with TB or T2DM ( p < 0.05). Multiplex ELISA revealed significant decreases in CD137, CD40, GITR, TNFR1/2, and TRAIL-R1/R2 and increases in CD27, CD30, and Fas (APO-1) expression in TB-T2DM. Correlation analysis revealed weak-to-inverse associations between cytokine-associated markers and activation markers with multiple TNF-receptor superfamily members ( p < 0.05). PPI analysis identified a highly interconnected TNF superfamily network, with TNFRSF1A, TNFRSF9, and CD95 as central hubs and KEGG enrichment in cytokine signaling, NF-κB pathway, death signaling, and TNF receptor binding. Together, hyperglycemia-associated monocyte dysfunction alters TNF superfamily receptor expression and receptor-cytokine integration, contributing to impaired immune regulation in TB-T2DM comorbidity.

title: Integrated multi-omics reveals methylation-linked biological heterogeneity in intermediate-risk pediatric acute myeloid leukemia
abstract: Intermediate-risk (IR) pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is clinically heterogeneous and lacks robust molecular stratification. We integrated DNA methylation, whole-exome, and transcriptome profiling in pediatric IR-AML. Unsupervised clustering of methylation profiles identified three stable epitypes (E1-E3) with distinct biological programs: E1 showed enrichment of stress-response and inflammatory pathways, E2 showed proliferative and survival signaling, and E3 showed transcriptional and developmental regulation with global hypomethylation. Despite heterogeneous mutational profiles, pathways converged across epitypes, indicating distinct genetic routes to shared functional outcomes. Immune activation was concordant across transcriptomic and epigenetic layers, with epitype-dependent variation in magnitude. Epitypes were associated with survival, with E1 showing poorer outcomes than E2 and E3. Projection onto an independent pediatric AML cohort showed partial conservation of epitype-associated methylation programs. These findings suggest that epigenetic stratification can capture clinically relevant heterogeneity beyond conventional genomic classification.

title: Deep learning detection and biological interpretation of arterial stiffness from retinal fundus images in diabetes
abstract: Pulse wave velocity is the gold standard for assessing arterial stiffness (AS) but is costly and not widely accessible. This multicenter study developed a deep learning model to predict AS from fundus images. Trained on 64,440 images from 36,412 adults with diabetes at China's National Metabolic Management Centers and externally validated on 6,217 images from two independent hospitals, the model achieved an AUC of 0.780 (95% CI: 0.769–0.792) and 0.772 (95% CI: 0.754–0.790) in internal and external validation, respectively, outperforming models using classical risk factors alone. The fusion model integrating fundus images with clinical factors significantly improved test-set performance (AUC = 0.853, 95% CI: 0.844–0.863) and demonstrated good external generalizability (AUC = 0.801, 95% CI: 0.784–0.816). Ablation studies indicated retinal arteries were associated with AS, with other retinal structures also contributing. These findings support deep-learning-based fundus-image analysis for AS screening in real-world clinical settings, and retinal-structure analyses for exploring AS pathophysiology.

title: Anti-HIV-1 B cell antigen receptor structure and signaling
abstract: The B cell antigen receptor (BCR) complex, comprised of antigen recognition and signaling components, functions in initiating B cell activation. While structural studies have described BCR domain organization, gaps remain in our understanding of its antigen binding domain (Fab, fragment antigen-binding) disposition, and how antigen binding is sensed to initiate signaling. Here, we report antigen affinity and signaling of the immunoglobulin (Ig) class IgM and IgG BCRs and define conformational states of full-length BCRs of two human broadly neutralizing antibodies, the glycan-specific, heavy chain domain-swapped, I-shaped 2G12, and a canonical Y-shaped antibody, CH31, that recognizes the CD4-binding site on the HIV-1 Envelope protein (Env). The BCRs adopted the shapes (I or Y) of their respective soluble antibodies, and both Ig class of BCRs of the same specificity bound Env trimers with similar affinities. We observed antigen-valenc y dependent differential signaling by the 2G12 IgM and IgG BCRs with trimeric Envs. Cryo-electron microscopy of the 2G12 IgG and CH31 IgM BCRs revealed varied Fab orientations. Structural comparisons revealed hinge points and regions of flexibility in the BCRs suggesting a highly dynamic structure of the BCR complex. Taken together, our results provide an integrated understanding of BCR structure, conformation, antigen recognition and signaling, and provide the basis for understanding antigen induced BCR signal transmission. One Sentence Summary: Cryo-electron microscopy structures of full-length B cell antigen receptor complex provide a novel dynamic BCR model and a basis for understanding antigen binding induced signal transmission.

title: Unveiling the failure behavior of rock and steel slag-based backfill composites for deep mining safety
abstract: The global transition toward a low-carbon heavy industry urgently demands the high-value upcycling of industrial solid wastes such as steel slag (SS), while deep underground mining encounters unprecedented structural stability challenges. Cementitious paste backfill synthesized from multi-solid wastes offers a sustainable dual solution for waste valorization and underground space stabilization; however, the multi-field failure mechanisms of rock-backfill composite structures remain insufficiently understood. Herein, we systematically investigate the triaxial mechanical behavior, energy dissipation, and 3D microstructural damage evolution of rock and SS-based backfill composites. By continuously tracking the interactive failure process between the surrounding rock and the backfill core, we demonstrate that increasing lateral confinement drives a distinct transition in the failure regime from brittle axial splitting to ductile shear-dilation. Moreover, through quantitative morphometric filtering, we successfully decouple stress-induced micro-crack networks from pre-existing voids, revealing that lateral stress effectively mitigates shear-crack opening and drives matrix void compaction. Finally, the inflection point in the energy dissipation ratio (Ud/Ue) is identified as a physics-driven, quantitative precursor for predicting macro-structural collapse.

title: Climate change and human activities shape future risks of Bactrocera dorsalis
abstract: Climate change and human activities alter agricultural pest distributions. We developed ensemble species distribution models to assess current habitat suitability of Bactrocera dorsalis using bioclimatic and human activity variables and project future shifts under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) scenarios using bioclimatic variables only. Incorporating human activity variables improved current model performance. Mean diurnal range (Bio2), isothermality (Bio3), and maximum temperature of the warmest month (Bio5) were key climatic predictors. Suitable habitats expanded under all future scenarios, particularly toward northern and central-eastern China, with the greatest increase under SSP3-7.0 in the 2070s. Multivariate environmental similarity surface and most dissimilar variable analyses indicated environmental similarity across most projected areas, whereas novelty in some regions was primarily associated with Bio3. These findings support targeted surveillance and pest risk management while highlighting the importance of assessing environmental novelty in future projections.

title: Tau spread plays an etiopathogenic connection between seizures and Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) display heightened seizure susceptibility, in which neuronal hyperactivity during seizures correlates with exacerbated Tau pathology and cognitive impairment. This study integrated public transcriptomic datasets with machine learning approaches, suggesting Tau spread as a key biological association between seizure activity and AD. We validated activity-dependent Tau release under epileptic stimulation using primary neurons and human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC)-derived neuronal models. Further validation in an AAV-based mouse Tau propagation model revealed robust bidirectional interactions: pathological Tau overexpression worsened seizure outcomes, while seizures accelerated Tau propagation across brain regions, inducing neuronal loss and gliosis. This study characterizes the activity-regulated interplay between epileptic activity and AD-associated Tau pathology, offering a potential therapeutic target for AD comorbid with epilepsy.

title: Exercise-conditioned serum drives mitochondrial remodeling in neurons
abstract: Exercise and fasting strategies are linked to improved brain health. Despite this little is known about how these interventions affect neuronal mitochondrial quality control. We hypothesized that circulating factors induced by acute exercise could stimulate neuronal mitochondrial quality control. To test this hypothesis, we treated primary cortical mouse neurons with serum collected from C57Bl/6J mice immediately following a single bout of exhaustive treadmill running or from sedentary controls. Neurons exposed to exercise serum exhibited increased markers of mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy. Proteomics analysis of exercise serum-treated neurons revealed changes in mitochondrial and autophagy-related proteins and upregulation of mitochondrial biogenesis, protein quality control, and redox signaling pathways. To determine if one bout of exercise activates brain mitophagy in vivo, we subjected mice to an acute fasting and treadmill running paradigm followed by electron microscopy of the frontal cortex. Acute exercise in a fasted state increased mitophagy structures. These results demonstrate that circulating factors induced by acute exercise promote mitophagy and mitochondrial turnover in neurons.

title: TRPM2-mediated Ca2+ entry drives cellular senescence to irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction
abstract: Aberrant Ca 2+ signaling, mediated by multiple ion channels, is increasingly recognized as a central driver of irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction; however, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the transient receptor potential melastatin-2 (TRPM2) channel as a key mediator of irradiation-induced Ca 2+ entry that drives salivary gland dysfunction. Trpm2 −/− mice were resistant to irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction at the acute/early stage of post-irradiation. RNA sequence analysis further showed that cell cycle pathways were upregulated, along with a decrease in ROS and its associated pathways in irradiated Trpm2 −/− mice. Mechanistically, our data show that loss of TRPM2 decreases cellular senescence, restores mitochondrial Ca 2+ handling and bioenergetics, along with DNA repair and protein synthesis. Finally, we show that pharmacological inhibition of senescence with quercetin or piperlongumine prevents irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction. Together, our findings provide a mechanistic link between TRPM2-dependent Ca 2+ signaling and cellular senescence as a key driver of irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction.

title: Sequential syntax of EEG microstates captures the temporal dynamics of inhibitory control
abstract: Cognitive processing relies on rapid reconfigurations of large-scale brain networks, yet traditional EEG microstate analyses reduce these dynamics to static metrics or isolated transitions. We integrated conditional successor analysis and Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) techniques adapted from genomics to characterize microstate sequence organization during a Go/NoGo task in 30 healthy adults. Generalized Estimating Equations revealed no condition-level differences in coverage, lifespan, or occurrences, confirming that global descriptors lack sensitivity to the temporal dynamics underlying inhibitory control.Conditional successor analysis identified three motifs significantly enriched in NoGo during the early processing window (100–500 ms): A–C–D (p_FDR = 0.015), A–B–E (p_FDR = 0.018), and E–A–D (p_FDR = 0.034). These motifs share a common entry point in microstate A and converge toward inhibitory engagement in microstate D, indicating that condition-specific patterns emerge through transition dynamics rather than changes in individual state properties. MSA demonstrated robust non-random temporal organization across all conditions and windows (all z > 11.5, all p < 0.001; OR = 2.68–3.51), with comparable similarity values across condition-window combinations (0.333–0.349), reflecting a shared global temporal architecture. NoGo conditions yielded directionally higher odds ratios than Go, with early NoGo showing the greatest sequential constraint.These results demonstrate that inhibitory processing is associated with dynamic reconfigurations of shared networks expressed at the sequential syntax level. Conditional successor analysis and MSA capture local motifs points and global temporal structure respectively, establishing sequence-based methods as a principled framework for linking millisecond-scale brain dynamics to cognitive function.

title: Optimizing chlorine management in garlic to improve nitrogen use efficiency and agronomic performance
abstract: Chloride (Cl − ) depletion has emerged as a potential constraint in intensive garlic production, where chlorine (Cl)-containing fertilizers are rarely applied. We evaluated the agronomic, nutritional, economic, and environmental effects of Cl fertilization using a two-year field experiment with six Cl application rates (0–300 kg ha −1 ) in a major garlic-producing region of China. Chloride accumulated predominantly in stems and leaves and promoted nutrient accumulation, photosynthetic performance, bulb development, and nutritional quality. Cl application also increased nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) use efficiency and reduced cumulative nitrate leaching by up to 37.6%. An application rate of 180 kg ha −1 produced the highest yield and economic return while maintaining favorable quality and environmental performance, whereas benefits declined at higher rates. These results indicate that appropriately managed Cl fertilization can improve garlic productivity and nutrient-use efficiency while reducing N loss, providing a basis for more balanced nutrient management in intensive garlic production.

title: Oleoyl-L-carnitine regulates PPM1B through BIRC6, inducing tumor concomitant cardiac fibrosis
abstract: Cancer increases the risk of heart failure progression, and cancer survivors face elevated odds of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Clinical observations link breast cancer severity to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction in patients undergoing surgical resection. Using metabolomic profiling of human breast cancer tissues and quantification in both patients and mouse models, we identified elevated levels of the tumor metabolite oleoyl-L-carnitine (OLcarn). Using affinity-enrichment proteomics with biotin-OLcarn in cardiac fibroblasts, we identified baculoviral IAP repeat-containing protein 6 (BIRC6) as a candidate interacting protein. Furthermore, binding of OLcarn to BIRC6 promoted ubiquitination of the protein phosphatase PPM1B and increased SMAD3 phosphorylation, thus activating pro-fibrotic signaling cascades. These results define a mechanism whereby a tumor-derived metabolite promotes cardiac fibrosis via the BIRC6/PPM1B/SMAD3 axis. This pathway reveals a key mode of tumor-heart crosstalk and may inform potential therapeutic strategies for cancer-associated cardiac fibrosis.

title: A randomized controlled trial of alternate-day versus daily iron therapy in ulcerative colitis in remission
abstract: Effectiveness and safety of alternate day vs. daily oral iron therapy for iron deficiency anemia is not well-established in ulcerative colitis patients. This randomized, open-label trial was conducted among patients with ulcerative colitis in remission who had iron-deficiency anemia. Fifty-six patients were randomized to daily vs. alternate-day oral iron therapy to compare the mean change in hemoglobin level after 8 weeks. Our study did not show any significant difference in mean hemoglobin levels, RBC indices, or iron profiles between the daily and alternate-day oral iron groups. Adverse events and disease flare were also not statistically significant in the two groups. Further studies are needed to explore this strategy in larger sample size and using other iron formulations. CTRI/2023/02/049438.

title: Institutional design of community energy storage: Value creation, capture, and distribution
abstract: Community energy storage can create economic value, but how ownership, market access, pricing, and network tariffs shape its creation, capture, and distribution alongside grid impacts remains unclear. We develop an integrated modeling framework and apply it to a Swiss energy community case study. Broader market access creates additional storage value, while under dynamic pricing community ownership allows members to retain more of it than third-party ownership. Local sharing prices can redistribute savings but have limited influence when value is driven by market arbitrage. Network tariffs change the relative benefits of individual and shared batteries and, in the community examined, narrow PV-non-PV savings gaps under shared storage. Broader market access can increase peak imports and exports, whereas contracted-capacity charges can moderate import peaks. These findings suggest that institutional design can play an important role in balancing economic performance, distributional outcomes, and grid impacts.

title: Using ChatGPT to evaluate the integration status of wetland conservation in local plans
abstract: Plan evaluation supports the development of higher quality plans.
