We examined whether language models could assist evaluation of wetland conservation in local comprehensive plans through prompt optimization. Using GPT-4o mini as both optimizer and evaluator, we developed prompts on five Nebraska county plans and compared basic and optimized prompts for GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini on twenty held-out plans across 56 indicators. Mean county-level agreement with human reference scores increased from 47.69% to 62.20% for GPT-4o and from 43.35% to 58.75% for GPT-4o mini under ternary scoring. This approach may enhance the reliability of language models for assessing planning quality and support planners in evaluating wetland conservation in local plans.

title: From osmolytes to oxidative stress: Temporal exometabolite shifts and microbial community responses in rehydrated biocrusts
abstract: Biocrusts are vital to dryland ecosystems, yet their microbe-exometabolite associations during rehydration remain poorly understood. This study investigated both bacterial and fungal diversity and exometabolite dynamics in light cyanobacterial crusts (LCCs) and cyanolichen crusts (CLCs) under rewetting over 96 h. Wetting increased the abundance of Firmicutes and reduced that of Actinobacteria within a day, while Shannon diversity remained stable in LCCs but declined in CLCs. Fungal communities were dominated by Ascomycota, with the lowest diversity at 24 h in LCCs. Targeted exometabolomics identified extracellular compounds categorized into three temporal clusters: early accumulation of amino acids, sugars, and osmolytes; intermediate divergence between LCCs and CLCs; and late enrichment of oxidative-stress-related metabolites. Network and Zi-Pi topology analyses identified urocanic acid, pipecolic acid, and S-adenosylhomocysteine as putative keystone metabolites, suggesting roles in microenvironmental regulation and microbial associations. These findings provide insights into the fundamentals of the resilience of biocrust communities during rewetting.

title: Machine learning-based classification of healthcare-associated infections in rehabilitation settings
abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) represent a challenge in rehabilitation settings, where prolonged stays and complex clinical conditions increase infection risk. This retrospective observational study applied a machine learning (ML) approach to classify HAI presence in patients undergoing rehabilitation. Cross-sectional surveillance data were collected at three time points across 22 facilities. An elastic-net logistic regression model was internally cross-validated on an initial cohort (2,966 patients) and temporally validated on an independent cohort (1,459 patients), with model interpretability assessed using SHAP analysis. Balanced accuracy was 72% and 74.5%, sensitivity 71% and 77%, and specificity 73% and 72% in internal and temporal external validation, respectively. Vascular and urinary catheterization emerged as the strongest predictors, while incontinence, pressure ulcers, and variables related to care setting and healthcare pathways showed additional contributions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of ML-based HAI classification in rehabilitation and provide insights into infection-associated factors that may help prioritize prevention efforts.

title: Exploring viral diversity and functions in the deep-sea sediments of the Bay of Bengal: A first viromic account
abstract: This study presents the viral communities in Bay of Bengal abyssal deep-sea sediment (3,747 m depth) characterized by employing metagenome based characterization. Illumina sequencing of virus-enriched sediment generated 39.4 million reads. A large proportion of these reads of ∼70% remained unclassified. The virome was dominated by dsDNA viruses, particularly Caudoviricetes , with Kyanoviridae as the most abundant family. As a result of assembly, 209 high-confidence viral contigs were recovered, and the gene-sharing network analysis revealed no clustering with known reference genomes, confirming predominantly uncharacterized viral lineages. Host predictions linked viruses to Pseudomonadota , Bacteroidota , and archaeal taxa including Nanoarchaeota . Functional annotation identified genes related to DNA replication and nucleotide metabolism, with limited auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) associated with carbohydrate and redox pathways. One complete circular ssDNA genome ( Genomoviridae ) was recovered. Overall, the Bay of Bengal deep-sea sediment harbors highly diverse, largely uncharacterized viral communities with potential roles in benthic biogeochemical cycling.

title: Histone lactylation in fibroblast-like synoviocytes drives CXCL1-mediated immune cell recruitment in rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Activated fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) are central players in autoimmune arthritis, contributing to disease progression by recruiting immune cells through a recruitment phenotype. However, the mechanisms underlying this phenotype remain poorly understood. One hallmark of autoimmune arthritis is metabolic reprogramming, characterized by enhanced glycolysis and lactate accumulation. These metabolic alterations have been implicated in the pathogenesis of autoimmune arthritis through diverse and complex mechanisms. Histone lactylation, a recently identified post-translational modification driven by elevated lactate levels, has been shown to regulate various physiological and pathological processes. Nonetheless, its role in FLS during autoimmune arthritis has not been fully elucidated. In this study, elevated plasma lactate levels were identified as a robust clinical diagnostic biomarker for autoimmune arthritis based on the analysis of a publicly available metabolomics dataset. Further investigations demonstrated that lactate-mediated histone lactylation is notably elevated in synovial FLS derived from autoimmune arthritis patients. This epigenetic modification was associated with increased expression of the chemokine CXCL1, which promotes immune cell recruitment. Therapeutic interventions targeting this pathway—either through CXCL1 neutralization or inhibition of histone lactylation—effectively reduced immune cell infiltration, alleviated joint inflammation, and mitigated bone destruction in CIA and SKG mouse models of autoimmune arthritis. These findings underscore the pivotal role of histone lactylation in mediating the recruitment phenotype of FLS and highlight its potential as a novel therapeutic target for autoimmune arthritis.

title: Progranulin from LGMN-high macrophages attenuates adipocyte lipolysis-related signaling via SORT1 in obesity
abstract: Obesity-associated adipose tissue dysfunction involves coordinated immune and metabolic remodeling. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing of human visceral white adipose tissue, we identified an obesity-enriched LGMN-high macrophage state with increased GRN expression and predicted PGRN-SORT1 signaling toward adipocytes. In macrophage-adipocyte co-culture systems, LGMN knockdown reduced macrophage PGRN abundance and enhanced adipocyte lipolysis-related signaling, whereas recombinant PGRN attenuated these effects in a SORT1-dependent manner. In high-fat diet-fed mice, AAV-mediated Lgmn knockdown reduced PGRN-SORT1 signaling, increased lipolysis-related protein levels, and improved adiposity, glucose homeostasis, circulating lipids, and inflammatory markers. These findings support an LGMN-PGRN-SORT1 macrophage-adipocyte communication axis linking obesity-associated myeloid remodeling to altered adipocyte lipid metabolic programs.

title: CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling characterizes a targetable fibroblast-lymphocyte niche in pulmonary fibrosis
abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis arises from diverse injuries but converges on progressive scarring without curative therapy. We integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets from human idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), silicosis, and non-IPF interstitial lung disease (ILD) and validated candidate pathways in human tissues and a silica-induced mouse model. CXCL12 and CXCR4 were recurrently upregulated in fibrotic lungs. CXCL12 localized mainly to fibroblast-lineage niches, while CXCR4-positive lymphocytes were consistently increased in fibrotic lungs. Cell-cell communication analysis and transwell assays supported a CXCR4-dependent lymphocyte migration toward conditioned medium from silica-stimulated fibroblasts. In human lung tissues, CXCR4-positive lymphocytes were associated with TGF-β-rich fibrotic regions. Therapeutic administration of Plerixafor after the establishment of fibrosis reduced lymphocyte accumulation, inflammatory cytokines, TGF-β-associated signaling, and extracellular matrix deposition in silica-exposed mice. These findings identify CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling as a targetable fibroblast-lymphocyte program in fibrotic lung disease.

title: Osteopontin influences weight gain and immune cell composition during ART-treated chronic HIV infection
abstract: Despite the ability of antiretroviral therapy (ART) to effectively suppress, but not cure, human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV), people with HIV (PWH) remain at increased risk for metabolic and inflammatory comorbidities that worsen with age. However, the molecular mediators linking HIV-associated inflammation to clinical physiological outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we identify osteopontin (OPN) as a sex-specific modulator of weight change in a humanized HIV-infected mouse model of ART-treated chronic infection. Knockdown of OPN (OPNkd) completely abolished weight gain observed in untreated infected males. In contrast, untreated OPNkd females showed a 3-fold increase in body weight relative to OPN-expressing controls. ART initiation was associated with an OPN-dependent 8% increase in female body weight despite a concurrent decrease in food intake. Longitudinal analyses revealed sex- and treatment-dependent shifts in myeloid and CD4+ T cell frequencies. Collectively, these findings support OPN as a sex-specific biomarker for immune and weight-related comorbidities.

title: Behavioral ontogeny in a pelagic tunicate reveals developmental maturation and context-dependent modulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Behavioral developmental plasticity refers to the lasting changes in an organism’s behavior that occur during development in response to external and internal cues, enhancing survival and reproduction. While well studied in vertebrates, its occurrence in other chordates, including tunicates, the closest relatives of vertebrates, remains unclear. We built a behavioral atlas of the planktonic tunicate Oikopleura dioica across its life cyclefrom larval to adult stages using high-throughput tracking and unsupervised analysis. Swimming kinematics, exploration, and thigmotaxis increased with development. Adults exhibit a unique innovation, known as the house, a complex extracellular filtration structure encasing the animal trunk, which drastically alters locomotion and exploration compared to free-swimming individuals. Postural variation during ontogeny is captured by seven basic shapes (“eigenoikopleuras”), with complex shapes becoming more frequent over time. Spatiotemporal embedding and Hidden Markov modeling revealed that behavioral refinement arises from changes in motor modules and their transitions. House occupancy similarly shifts these modules, indicating context-specific specialization. This continuous behavioral maturation parallels Oikopleura ’s neotenic morphology, retaining a larval body plan unlike other tunicates. Our atlas provides a quantitative framework for exploring the evolution of behavioral developmental plasticity in chordates.

title: Individual variation in food odor sensitivity is related to neuropeptide signaling and starvation in Drosophila
Cell intrinsic heme synthesis is required for the proper activation of naive CD4+ T cells
Flowering stage shapes the sensory quality and metabolite profile of kiwifruit floral tea
Farm exposure is associated with human milk immune profile and microbiota
abstract: Prenatal and early life farm exposure, and breastfeeding, are associated with protection from allergic diseases. We hypothesize that farm exposure influences the human breast milk microbiome and immune proteins. The immune protein profiles and microbial communities of 152 human breast milk samples were compared among three maternal farm exposure groups (traditional agrarian, farm, and non-farm) in rural Wisconsin to identify signatures associated with farm status and atopic disease. We found significant differences between farm groups for 23 immune proteins (p-adj<0.05), microbiome diversity (p=2.2E-05), and microbiome richness (p=8.0e-06). Traditional agrarian human breast milk had the highest immune protein levels and microbiome diversity and richness, followed by farm and non-farm human breast milk. Furthermore, Gram-positive bacterial species correlated with IL-23 mediated signaling events (p-adj<1.0E-05). These data suggest that increased farm exposures promotes human breast milk that is more microbially-diverse and rich in immune-associated proteins, ultimately influencing immune development in the infant.

title: Reticular chemistry-based engineering of covalent organic frameworks for multimodal cancer therapy and ultrasensitive biosensing
ICAM-5: A marker for neuronally derived extracellular vesicles
abstract: Abstract Current methods for isolating neuronal-derived extracellular vesicles (NDEVs) from human biofluids lack specificity. In addition, some of the reported markers for NDEV isolation are present as soluble proteins instead of extracellular vesicle (EV) associated proteins. To address the research gap, this study aimed to identify a novel marker for NDEV isolation that is NDEV associate and highly specific to the central nervous system. To achieve this, human cortical neurons were used for isolation of EVs invitro . Mass spectroscopy was performed to screen for potential EV surface markers. This analysis yielded 63 brain specific proteins among which ICAM-5 was selected for further validations in human serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples. Our analysis shows that ICAM-5 is present on the surface of NDEVs, colocalizing with standard extracellular vesicle markers like CD-63 and CD-9. We further confirm that NDEVs isolated using ICAM-5 contain neuronal proteins (tau, neuronal specific enolase) but not glial markers. Using ICAM-5 as a NDEV marker, EVs were eluted from human serum samples of with traumatic brain injury. Our results show enhanced levels of ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1), a marker of neurological injury, in serum samples from patients with TBI when compared to currently known markers of NDEV. Our findings demonstrate that ICAM-5 is specific EV associated marker for isolating NDEVs from human biofluids that can potentially improve the enrichment of NDEVs from biofluids thereby improving diagnosis and monitoring of neurological conditions.

title: Progress and perspectives on DNA-enabled architectures for energy storage and conversion
From epidemiology to mechanisms of inflammation in hypertensive cardiac damage
